body: Cash, traveller's cheques and other bearer monetary instruments exceeding 60,000 dirhams, or the equivalent in any currency, must be declared to customs. A passenger under 18 has no allowance of their own. Their money is added to the parent's or guardian's limit, so a family cannot split the threshold. An undeclared amount is treated as smuggling — a criminal matter, not a forgotten form.
title: From 60,000 dirhams you must declare, or it counts as smuggling

body: Visitors may bring narcotic and controlled medicines with them, up to their need for three months. A prior electronic approval from the Ministry of Health and Prevention is optional for travellers. Without it, declare these medicines on arrival, with the prescription and the medical report. The prescription names you, the medicine, its dose, form and duration of treatment, the date and the physician. It should be issued within the last three months and recognised or stamped by the healthcare facility following you up. Transit passengers who stay in the port need no approval, but should carry the prescription.
title: Controlled medicines: three months' supply, declared on arrival or pre-approved

body: Pharmaceutical preparations and medicines are restricted goods in the UAE. That expressly includes narcotics used for medical purposes. Bringing them in or taking them out requires prior approval from the designated authority, which for medicines is the Ministry of Health and Prevention. Medical devices, accessories, laboratory solutions and sterilization devices fall under the same line and the same authority. Get the approval before you import or export them. The text does not say what happens if you do not, and it does not describe a separate procedure for personal-use medicines. Separately, narcotic substances of all types are strictly prohibited from import and export.
title: Medicines need prior approval from the UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention

body: Flying a drone for fun in the UAE is closed to visitors: the pilot must be at least 18 years old and a UAE resident. Registration goes through the UAE Drones platform with a UAE Pass, which a visitor does not have. Before any flight a training certificate from a school accredited by the civil aviation authority is required. The drone itself is registered, must carry remote identification, and every flight needs approval. Then come the limits: up to 5 kilograms, within sight, in daylight, up to 400 feet (120 metres), clear of airports and helipads. So there is no lawful way for a tourist to fly here — leave the drone at home.
title: Only a UAE resident may fly a drone for fun — a tourist cannot

body: In Dubai's nature reserves, hunting, moving, killing or harming the living creatures there is prohibited. So is taking living things, rocks or dust out of a reserve. You may not bring in animals or species that do not already live there, or pollute its soil, water or air. Driving a vehicle in a reserve needs a permit from Dubai Municipality. Breaking these rules can bring imprisonment (the law sets no term), a fine of up to 500,000 dirhams, or both. On conviction, the court orders the offender to remedy the damage caused and may confiscate seized items obtained from or used in the offence. The basis is Articles 8 and 10 of Dubai Law No. 11 of 2003.
title: Dubai reserves: harming wildlife or taking out rocks or animals is a crime

body: Insulting someone through an electronic network or device is a cybercrime in the UAE. It carries imprisonment, a fine of AED 250,000 to AED 500,000, or both. Using a network or device to invade someone's privacy without their consent, where the law does not allow it, is also a crime. This covers photographing people in public or private places with that aim, and publishing their photos or information to harm them, even if it is true. It also covers taking or publishing photos of the injured, the dead or accident victims without the consent of those concerned. These privacy offences carry at least six months in prison, a fine of AED 150,000 to AED 500,000, or both.
title: Online insults and photos that invade privacy are crimes in the UAE

body: Get a Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) import permit before bringing a cat or dog into the UAE. Implant the microchip before the rabies vaccination. One source says a vaccination given before chipping is not accepted, and a fresh rabies shot is needed after chipping. Pets must enter as manifest cargo, not as cabin baggage or checked baggage. One permit covers a maximum of 2 pets per person per year. The permit is valid for 90 days from issue on the Zoovet page. Another source says 30 days, so check the permit itself. MOCCAE bans these dog breeds and their crosses: American Pit Bull Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier and American Bully. It also bans Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Tibetan Mastiff, Neapolitan Mastiff, Dogue de Bordeaux, Boerboel and Bullmastiff. The list ends with Cane Corso, Bully Kutta, Presa Canario and Japanese Tosa. Service, emotional support or medical dogs are an exception, with the documents MOCCAE requires. If a requirement is not met, the pet is held at your expense or sent back, and a banned breed may be rejected or confiscated.
title: UAE pet import: MOCCAE permit, microchip first, cargo only, banned breeds

body: The customs list of goods strictly prohibited from import or export includes poppy with its shells and seeds. They sit in one line with opium, heroin, morphine, cocaine, qat and cannabis, as narcotic substances of similar effect. There is no quantity below which the line stops applying, and no exception for food. That is the whole difficulty: the seeds travel inside ordinary things — a bread roll, a pastry, a spice mix, a ready-made filling. Read the ingredients before you pack, and do not assume a bakery item is outside a narcotics list.
title: Poppy seeds sit on the banned list between cocaine and cannabis

body: Personal income tax here is zero, so people rarely think about residency. They should: since 2023 it is defined by law, and 183 days of presence within any 12 consecutive months makes you a tax resident. For local residents and Gulf nationals the threshold is lower — 90 days, given a permanent home or a job. Any days count, even parts of a day, and they need not be consecutive. A certificate for treaty purposes is issued only at 183 days, even if residency arose earlier.
title: There is no income tax, but residency still arises — and that matters back home

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. The UAE itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. Transit counts too: a layover of more than 12 hours at an airport in an affected country is treated as arriving from there. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

body: Driving under the influence of alcohol in the UAE has no fixed fine — the court decides it. The offence also carries 23 black points, and a light vehicle is held for 60 days. Drugs and brain-affecting substances are the same, with the licence suspended for a year counted from the end of the punishment. This comes from the traffic control rules of the Ministry of Interior. So the practical line is not a small glass but none at all.
title: Alcohol at the wheel in the UAE: the court sets the penalty

body: For personal use or treatment you may bring medicines into Armenia without any certificate, whether or not they are registered in Armenia. The limit is up to 10 kinds, with three consumer packs of each. A prescription, medical history or other document signed by a doctor that accompanies the medicines can justify a larger quantity for the course of treatment. Not declaring goods over the allowed quantities can lead to administrative or criminal penalties.
title: Armenia: medicines for personal use, up to 10 kinds with three packs each

body: A medicine with narcotic or psychotropic substances needs no licence to enter or leave Armenia if you present medical documents for it. They must confirm the medical need and name the medicine and the quantity. Give customs these documents, or their certified and notarised translation into Armenian. Only such medicines registered in Armenia may be brought in. At the border, fill in a customs declaration stating the quantity a doctor prescribed and that you obtained it legally. Not declaring such medicines can lead to administrative or criminal penalties.
title: Armenia: narcotic and psychotropic medicines need papers and a declaration

body: If you enter Austria from a non-EU state carrying cash or equivalent means of payment worth €10,000 or more, you must declare it to customs. You can declare it in writing or electronically. The form is called "Cash declaration CC2". You can download it in English from bmf.gv.at under Customs > Cash controls, or get it at your customs office. The text gives no penalty for failing to declare, so none is stated here. This provision sits in the part of the leaflet on entry from non-EU states; the part on entry from EU states has no cash rule.
title: Carry €10,000 or more in cash into Austria from a non-EU state: declare it

body: In the Open category, every drone flown in Austria must have adequate insurance, at least 750,000 Special Drawing Rights under the Aviation Act. The remote pilot must get the landowner's consent for take-off and landing. Flying a drone against the rules may be an administrative offence under § 169 of the Aviation Act. Depending on the breach, the district authority can impose fines of up to €22,000.
title: Austria: drones need insurance and landowner consent; fines up to €22,000

body: If you take up accommodation in a dwelling in Austria, you must register with the local registration authority within three days of moving in. You do this at the Municipal Office, or in Vienna at the Municipal District Office. You need a registration form signed by the accommodation provider. If you are not an Austrian citizen, you also need a travel document such as a passport. Failing to register is an administrative offence. The fine is up to 726 Euro, and up to 2.180 Euro if you repeat it. Registering without actually having taken up accommodation is also punishable (sham registration). You do not have to register if you are provided with a dwelling for no more than three days. Tourist accommodation such as hotels, guest houses and privately rented rooms works differently. There you are registered by an entry in the accommodation's guest register.
title: Register a new residence in Austria within three days, or face a fine

body: If you have a home in Austria, or Austria is your usual place of residence, you are subject to unrestricted Austrian income tax. In principle, all your income, in Austria and abroad, is then taxed in Austria. Nationality does not matter. A home counts only if you have regularly used it as a home over a longer period and it meets the personal requirements of a home. A short stay, such as a holiday or a business trip, does not make Austria your usual place of residence. After a stay of six months, this unrestricted liability applies in all cases, and it counts back to the start of the stay. Suppose you have no home or usual residence in Austria. If you are employed there or receive income there, for example a pension, you are subject to limited tax liability. Double taxation agreements can reduce the tax if you could be taxed in more than one country. The text names no penalty.
title: Six months in Austria makes you liable to Austrian income tax

body: Vehicles on Austria's highways must carry a toll sticker, called a vignette. You can buy it at automobile clubs such as ÖAMTC and ARBÖ, at post offices, at tobacco shops, at some gas stations and online. If you drive without a valid sticker, or with one that is not properly affixed, you face high fines. The police and customs authorities may collect the toll you evaded plus an additional sum as a substitute fine. The text does not give the amount of the substitute fine.
title: Austrian motorways require a toll sticker (vignette) or you face high fines

body: If you do not live in Azerbaijan, you may temporarily bring in a car or motorcycle permanently registered abroad for 90 days. The period can be extended to the term of your visa or temporary residence permit, up to one year. The extension needs security for the customs payments. Right-hand-drive vehicles may not be brought in at all. A non-resident who takes the vehicle out late bears administrative liability.
title: Driving into Azerbaijan: a car registered abroad may stay 90 days

body: You may bring any amount of cash into Azerbaijan if you follow customs procedures. Foreign currency up to USD 10,000 and up to 20,000 manats leave on an oral declaration. 20,000 manats or more, and jubilee or commemorative manat coins, need a written declaration. Foreign currency up to USD 50,000 can leave in cash when you present customs documents confirming you brought it in. The currency control page adds a condition for amounts from USD 10,000 to USD 50,000. You must give customs the documents and a written declaration. Both must show you brought that amount in as cash. Above USD 50,000 it goes out only by transfer through authorized banks and national postal operators. A certificate from the bank of the country the currency came from, confirming the cash transfer, is then required. These rules are the same for foreigners and for citizens of Azerbaijan.
title: Cash out of Azerbaijan: USD 10,000 by word, up to USD 50,000 with papers

body: Goods not meant for production or commercial use can leave without customs payments within set limits. For sturgeon caviar the limit is 125 grams, once a calendar month. For sturgeon itself it is 5 kilograms. The once-a-month limit does not apply to accompanied baggage carried by air.
title: Leaving Azerbaijan: at most 125 grams of sturgeon caviar a month

body: Cultural property on Azerbaijan's protected list can be taken out only with a certificate from the Ministry of Culture confirming it may be exported. Cultural property crossing the border must be declared in writing to customs. National cultural property leaves the country only for temporary exhibitions, tours, presentations, restoration work and international cultural events. As a rule, that is for no more than six months a year.
title: Protected cultural property leaves Azerbaijan only with a certificate

body: From the age of 18 you can bring in 1.5 litres of alcohol and 200 cigarettes for personal use, once a calendar month, without customs duties. Together with the monthly allowance of goods and up to 30 kilograms of food, their total customs value may not exceed USD 800. The once-a-month limit does not apply to accompanied baggage carried by air. The rules are the same for foreigners as for citizens of Azerbaijan.
title: Duty-free into Azerbaijan: 1.5 litres of alcohol and 200 cigarettes a month

body: When you apply for an Azerbaijan visa, your passport or other travel document must stay valid for at least 3 months after the visa expires. Check the passport's expiry date against the visa period you request before you apply. The text lists this as a document requirement for visa issuance and states no penalty. The state visa fee is not refunded, whatever the result of the application. So a passport that is too close to expiry could cost you the fee. This applies to visa applications. The text says nothing about passport validity for travellers who do not need a visa.
title: Passport must be valid at least 3 months beyond your Azerbaijan visa

body: Medicines in the quantity you need for personal use enter Azerbaijan without customs duties, even ones not registered there. Whether the amount is for personal use is decided by customs, from its nature, quantity and how often you bring it. Medicines, drug substances, psychotropic substances and medical supplies whose circulation Azerbaijan controls are imported on the basis of an opinion of the Ministry of Health.
title: Azerbaijan: controlled medicines are imported on a Health Ministry opinion

body: Every mobile phone and other wireless device you bring into Azerbaijan must be declared to customs, whatever it is worth. You can declare in writing, at an e-kiosk, on e.customs.gov.az or in the Smart Customs app. To register a phone on portal.rinn.az, it must first be registered in the electronic system of the State Customs Committee. Not declaring a phone brings administrative responsibility.
title: Declare your phone to customs when you enter Azerbaijan

body: Citizens of Kazakhstan who stay in Azerbaijan for more than 30 days must register their place of stay. Apply online on the State Migration Service website, by e-mail to qeydiyyat@migration.gov.az, or in person at an ASAN service centre. Missing the deadline brings administrative liability.
title: Citizens of Kazakhstan staying over 30 days in Azerbaijan must register

body: Foreigners staying in Azerbaijan for more than 15 days must register their place of stay; citizens of Kazakhstan have a longer period. Other foreigners apply within 15 days of arrival. Apply online on the migration service's website, by e-mail to qeydiyyat@migration.gov.az, or in person at a regional migration department or an ASAN centre. You need the application form and a copy of your passport, including the visa page and the pages showing your last entry; registration is free. If you move, register at the new place within 5 working days. A temporary stay in another flat of the owner of your registered flat needs no new registration. Failing to register in time is a basis for administrative liability.
title: Over 15 days in Azerbaijan: register within 15 days (Kazakh citizens: 30)

body: If you were duly notified to report for conscription and did not come, the military commissariat can temporarily bar you from leaving Belarus. The same applies if you broke military registration duties so that you could not be notified. The ban lasts until you report for the conscription procedures. The commissariat sends you a notice no later than one day after deciding. Border guards enforce the ban at the crossing point. The commissariat can let you leave for a set period if you need medical care that cannot be given in Belarus. It can also do so if a close relative living abroad is gravely ill or has died. To check in advance, ask your local internal affairs office whether you are in the database of citizens barred from leaving.
title: Missing a conscription call-up can bar you from leaving Belarus

body: A court can temporarily bar you from leaving Belarus for unpaid debts. This covers debts, taxes or other obligations set by a court decision in force or an enforcement document. The same applies if the bailiff's measures are not enough to collect the debt in full and on time. Officials of a debtor company can be barred too. The creditor or the bailiff applies to the court, which hears it within ten calendar days of receiving it and notifies both sides. The ban is imposed only if it does not stop you meeting your other obligations. Border guards enforce the ban at the crossing point. At your request, the court can suspend this debt ban for a period it sets. You, the creditor or the bailiff can ask the court to lift it, and the court decides within three calendar days of the request. To check in advance, ask your local internal affairs office whether you are in the database of citizens barred from leaving. Separately, once a civil lawsuit is filed against you, a court can bar you from leaving for a set period, at most until the case ends.
title: Unpaid court debts can get you barred from leaving Belarus

body: Since 28 September 2023 individuals may not import, operate or make civil drones in Belarus. Six months later the ban reached keeping and trading them too. It is wider than it looks: it covers not only camera-carrying craft but model aircraft with no equipment at all, and identifiable spare parts. Only balloons, kites and flying toys without remote control are left out. At the border there is no fine, simply a refusal of release, however you carry or declare the drone. From there two roads: take it back out of the EAEU, or lose it to customs under chapter 51 of the EAEU Customs Code. Bringing back your own drone, taken out of the country before the decree, is not provided for either.
title: A drone will not be let into Belarus, not even a radio-controlled toy

body: Keep your imported goods within your duty-free allowance, which depends on how you cross the border. The allowance is counted per person and per crossing. By air you can bring goods worth up to 10,000 euros and up to 50 kg. By land or on foot the limit drops twentyfold to only 500 euros and 25 kg. Goods sent by post or by a carrier get 200 euros and 31 kg. Above the allowance, you must pay duty of 30 per cent of the excess value, and never less than 4 euros per kilogram of excess weight. A boxed new laptop or phone brought in by car will barely fit inside it.
title: Duty-free goods: up to 10,000 euros by air, 500 by car or train

body: You may bring in medicines with narcotic or psychotropic substances for your own treatment, but only a limited amount. Narcotics: no more than a week's need; psychotropics: no more than 90 single doses. What decides it at the border is the document. It must name the medicine, its dosage and the amount you need per day. It is an extract from your medical records or a prescription, carrying the doctor's own seal and signature. An electronic prescription, or an uncertified printout of one, is not accepted by customs at all. A document in another language needs a certified translation into Belarusian or Russian, and without this the medicine is seized.
title: A narcotic medicine needs a paper prescription, not an electronic one

body: The offence is wider than sharing. Article 19.11 of the Code of Administrative Offences punishes making, storing and transporting such material with intent to distribute, not only the distribution itself. Confiscation of the item comes with the fine in every case. A second, heavier paragraph applies to anything on the national list of extremist materials. There the penalty runs from ten to thirty basic units, with community work or administrative arrest as alternatives, again with confiscation. The list is broad and changes, so what was lawful on your phone last year may not be now.
title: Extremist material: keeping it to share is punished, not only sharing

body: A foreigner staying temporarily in Belarus must hold an insurance contract — a Belarusian one from Belgosstrakh or Beleximgarant, or one concluded with a foreign insurer. Without it the foreign ministry expressly allows refusal of both the visa and entry. A foreign policy faces more requirements than people expect. It must state the insurer's name and address, the phone numbers of the insurer or of an international assistance service, and your name. It must be valid on Belarusian territory and for the whole period of stay, with a sum insured of no less than €10,000. A Belarusian contract can be arranged online before the trip on either insurer's site, or at the border crossing point itself.
title: Without a policy you can be turned away, and not every foreign policy counts

body: A child under 18, unless married or declared fully capable, leaves Belarus on their own travel document. Travelling with one or both parents or other legal representatives, the representative shows the border guard a document proving that status. That can be the child's birth certificate or the representative's travel document with an entry about the child. A child travelling without them, alone or with another adult, needs the written consent of both legal representatives. A notary must certify the consent, or the citizenship and migration office where the representative or child lives, or a competent foreign authority. A consent issued abroad needs legalisation or an apostille, unless a treaty says otherwise. If it is in a foreign language, it needs a notarised translation into a state language of Belarus. One representative's consent is enough, with a supporting document, if the other has died, lost parental rights, or been declared dead, incapable or missing. The same holds if the other is wanted in a criminal case, or the father was recorded at the unmarried mother's request. It also holds if a court decision, a marriage contract or an agreement on children allows the trip without the other's consent. A child who lives abroad permanently needs only one representative's consent. A representative who disagrees with these rules can ask a court to set a different exit order for the child.
title: A child leaving Belarus without parents needs both representatives' consent

body: If you stay in Belarus for more than 10 working days, you need to register. You can register with the citizenship and migration divisions of the local internal affairs bodies, or through the unified electronic services portal, portal.gov.by. If you stay in a hotel, hostel, sanatorium or other collective accommodation, its administration registers you by default when you check in. The page does not say what happens if you do not register. It gives no deadline other than the 10 working days. The visa-free stay itself cannot be extended beyond the established 30 days.
title: Staying over 10 working days in Belarus means registering; hotels do it for you

body: Residency comes from staying more than 183 days in a calendar year. But time spent abroad is included in that count: business trips, holidays and medical treatment count as days of presence here. So leaving for a month to stay under the threshold does not work. A resident is taxed on worldwide income; a non-resident only on local income.
title: Business trips, holidays and medical treatment abroad count as days here

body: From 1 December to 1 March, motor cars up to 3.5 tonnes and buses up to 5 tonnes need winter tyres in Belarus. Passenger cars and combined passenger-and-cargo cars over 3.5 tonnes need them too. Winter tyres go on every wheel. Without wear indicators, a winter tyre with the mountain-and-snowflake mark and an M+S, M&S or M S mark is unfit below 4 mm of tread. Studded tyres must be on all axles, and are banned in June, July and August.
title: Winter tyres from 1 December to 1 March, on every wheel

body: Non-residents and temporary residents must declare all alcohol, tobacco and vaping products they bring into Canada. The limit is 1.5 litres of wine, or 1.14 litres of spirits, or 8.5 litres of beer. For tobacco it is 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars or 200 grams of manufactured tobacco, and up to 12 vaping containers. The minimum age for alcohol is 18 if you enter in Alberta, Manitoba or Quebec, and 19 elsewhere. Duties and taxes may apply even within these limits.
title: Alcohol, tobacco and vapes in Canada: declare them, within limits

body: Bringing cannabis across the Canadian border is a serious criminal offence, even though cannabis may be legal in Canada. If found, it may be confiscated. Any cannabis you carry must be declared, including CBD products made from cannabis or hemp. Failing to declare it can bring a penalty of up to CAD 2,000.
title: Bringing cannabis across Canada's border is a serious crime

body: Declare the cash and monetary instruments worth CAD 10,000 or more that you carry when you enter or leave Canada. Canadian and foreign currency count together, as do cheques, money orders and bank drafts. Carrying such a sum is legal as long as you declare it. Funds seized as suspected proceeds of crime are not returned.
title: Declare CAD 10,000 or more in cash when entering or leaving Canada

body: In Parks Canada places, drink alcohol only at registered campsites, private residences or licensed premises. It is not allowed at beaches, day use areas, cook shelters or on trails. Drinking alcohol while boating is illegal, just like drinking and driving. Breaking the law in a national park or national historic site can bring eviction or tickets. In more serious cases it can bring court appearances or large fines. The text gives no specific amounts. Some campgrounds ban alcohol for certain periods of the year, and notices online and at the campgrounds say when.
title: In Canadian national parks, drink only at campsites, homes or licensed premises

body: Importing a controlled substance into Canada unless the regulations allow it is a crime, punishable by up to life imprisonment for Schedule I or II drugs. A narcotic or controlled drug must be prescribed to you or to a person in your care travelling with you, in labelled pharmacy or hospital packaging. You may bring the lesser of a single course of treatment or a 30-day supply at the usual prescribed dose. Benzodiazepines and other targeted substances must also be prescribed and labelled. For these, a visitor living abroad has a limit on the quantity. It is the least of three amounts: the container's contents, a 90-day supply, or the daily dose times the days planned in Canada. Carry these medicines yourself and declare them to a Canada Border Services Agency officer when you arrive. The rules give an individual no way to bring in restricted drugs.
title: Controlled medicines into Canada: declare, up to 30 days, 90 for benzodiazepines

body: Canada does not limit how much money you carry in or out, and carrying it is not illegal. But if you carry currency or monetary instruments worth CAN$10,000 or more, you must declare it, both when you enter and when you leave. Monetary instruments include cheques, money orders, bank drafts, traveller's cheques, stocks and bonds. The amount can be in Canadian or foreign currency, or a mix. The rule covers all travellers, couriers and people carrying money for someone else. If you do not declare the full amount, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) can seize all of it. It may be returned after you pay a penalty of 5% to 50% of the seized funds. If the CBSA suspects the money is proceeds of crime or funds for financing terrorism, it will not return it. When leaving, report to a CBSA office before you go; at an airport, do this before the security screening area. When entering, report in one of these ways: at an airport kiosk, or on your CBSA Declaration Card (if one was provided to you). You can also use your Advance Declaration, or tell a border services officer verbally. You cannot use NEXUS while carrying this amount, and money sent by mail or courier must also be declared.
title: Declare CAN$10,000 or more in cash when entering or leaving Canada

body: To fly a drone of 250 grams or more in Canada, a foreign pilot needs a Canadian drone pilot certificate, even with a licence at home. Such drones must be registered, and foreign pilots cannot register theirs. Instead, they can apply for a Foreign SFOC-RPAS. Drones under 250 grams need no registration and no Foreign SFOC-RPAS, except to fly at an advertised event.
title: A foreign pilot flying a 250 g+ drone in Canada needs a Canadian certificate

body: If you are outside Canada and live in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), South Sudan or Uganda, Canada will not finalize your application. This covers visas, electronic travel authorizations, work permits, study permits and temporary resident permits. A visa, travel authorization or temporary resident permit you already hold is suspended too. Airlines get a "no board" message, so you cannot fly to Canada. Once the Order ends, applications resume and documents are reinstated. You may still have to follow public health measures then. The Minister may exempt a person case by case, for example for urgent protection or humanitarian reasons. The Order does not apply to Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or people already in Canada. It also does not apply to US citizens and lawful permanent residents. It is in force until 23:59:59 Eastern Standard Time on November 27, 2026.
title: Canada suspends visas and permits for residents of DR Congo, South Sudan, Uganda

body: Declare all food, plant and animal products when you arrive in Canada, and any pet travelling with you. Undeclared food, plant and animal products and pets may be seized. You may also have to pay a penalty of up to CAD 1,300.
title: Declare food, plants, animal products and pets when entering Canada

body: Do not fly a drone for recreation in any Parks Canada place. Only a permit or special permission allows it, so if you have neither, leave the drone at home. Breaking the rules in a national park or national historic site can bring an eviction or a ticket. In more serious cases it can mean a court appearance or a large fine. The page gives no amount for drone flying.
title: Parks Canada places are no-drone zones without a permit

body: If you spend 183 days or more in Canada in a year, Canada deems you resident for income tax for that year. The days count whether they come in one stay or in several. A resident's income for Canadian tax includes income from sources inside and outside Canada. A tax treaty can override this: if it makes you resident only in the other country, Canada treats you as non-resident. This rests on section 250 of the Income Tax Act.
title: 183 days in Canada in a year make you a Canadian tax resident

body: China bans travellers from bringing in meat and meat products, including offal and dried meat. The same list covers milk and dairy products and fresh fruit and vegetables. It applies to hand luggage, checked baggage and parcels alike, and what is found is returned or destroyed there and then. Failing to declare, or declaring falsely, is fined by the quarantine service — up to 5,000 yuan. Industrially packaged processed food is not on the list, but you will be the one explaining that.
title: Sausage, cheese and fruit in your suitcase are destroyed on the spot

body: Two thresholds, and they are set by two different acts. Foreign cash above the equivalent of 5,000 US dollars must be declared to customs in writing on entry. On the way out, up to 5,000 needs no permit; between 5,000 and 10,000 you must get a carrying permit from a bank first. Chinese currency has its own ceiling: 20,000 yuan per person per crossing, in either direction. People crossing several times in one day, or several times within fifteen days, are treated separately on the way in.
title: Declare cash over USD 5,000 or CNY 20,000

body: In China, carving on, daubing or otherwise deliberately damaging a state-protected cultural relic or a scenic or historic site is an offence. It brings a warning or a fine of up to 500 yuan. In more serious cases, it brings five to ten days of administrative detention and a fine of 500 to 1,000 yuan. A foreigner who breaks these rules may also be ordered to leave China by a deadline, or be deported. The basis is the Public Security Administration Punishments Law as revised on 27 June 2025, Articles 10 and 75.
title: China: carving or daubing a relic or scenic site — fine, detention, expulsion

body: The power to look inside your phone comes not from a customs rule but from the Counter-espionage Law. Article 25 lets state security officers check the electronic devices, facilities, programs and tools of individuals and organisations. Three conditions bind it: a counter-espionage task, the approval of a state security head at city level or above, and a service card shown to you. If they find something endangering national security they must first order it put right. Sealing or seizing the device comes only after a refusal to comply, or when the danger remains. The seal must be lifted once the danger is gone, and inspection must not go beyond what the task requires. So this is not a routine search of every traveller at the border.
title: Phone inspection is lawful only under the counter-espionage law

body: The drone rules prohibit foreign aircraft, and aircraft flown by foreign personnel, from carrying out surveying and mapping flights in China. There is no permit for this case: the ordinary route needs the sanction of two ministries and a Chinese partner, which does not extend to drones. The surveying law describes the activity broadly: determining, collecting and expressing the shape, size, position and attributes of natural features or structures. Processing and supplying the data obtained counts too. An ordinary video clip does not fall under that description, but footage tied to coordinates may. The penalty is heavy: the drone and the results are confiscated, plus a fine of 100,000 to 500,000 yuan. In a serious case the fine is 500,000 to a million, and the authorities decide on departure within a set period or on expulsion.
title: A mapping flight by a foreigner is prohibited, and it reaches deportation

body: A drone or its core parts may not be brought into Beijing; the ban has held since 1 May 2026. The one exception covers aircraft already in the city, so it is no help to a visitor. The whole city is controlled airspace, and carrying a drone in means confiscation and a fine of 500 to 5,000 yuan. From 15 November 2026 a revised regulation forbids flying in the city outright, and forbids keeping a drone there at all. Across the rest of the country an owner must register the drone under their real name. There is no weight floor: aircraft lighter than 250 grams count too. Flying unregistered costs up to 200 yuan, and 2,000 to 20,000 in a serious case.
title: A drone cannot be brought into Beijing, and elsewhere it must be registered

body: Chinese law lists when a foreigner is not allowed in: no valid documents, or refusing or evading border inspection. It also covers the grounds that would have blocked the visa, among them the risk of harming national security and public interest or public order. A third ground is being likely, after entry, to do something that does not match the type of visa you hold. The border authority may refuse entry without giving a reason — the law says so in as many words. Whoever is refused is ordered to go back, forced back if they will not, and may not leave the area set for them while waiting.
title: The border may turn you back without telling you why

body: From 15 September 2026 a State Council regulation adds a ban for lying on the papers. It covers false material and false statements, both when applying for a visa abroad and when asking to enter at the border. The immigration or visa authority may then bar you for one to five years. The word is may, not must: it is a decision, not an automatic consequence. The same one-to-five-year ban runs from the day a punishment is served, where someone was punished for obstructing border control or for obtaining documents by deception. Writing a false invitation letter for someone else costs a private person 5000 to 10000 yuan. So fill the form exactly, and do not simplify an answer about your purpose, your accommodation or your earlier visits.
title: False information for a visa or at the border can bring a 1 to 5 year entry ban

body: A foreign licence on its own does not let you drive here. The rules require a temporary driving permit from the vehicle management office. For a short entry it is issued for three months, and if the stay runs longer than three months the term is extended to a year. Only a full licence counts: the rules expressly exclude learner, temporary and probationary ones. An international permit plays no part here at all — the rules never mention it, and it is no substitute for the permit. Driving without the permit brings a fine of 200 to 2000 yuan, to which detention of up to fifteen days may be added. If you go on to apply for a full Chinese licence, your own licence will need a translation from an agency or certified by a notary.
title: Your own licence does not work: a Chinese temporary permit is required

body: Reaching the international network is allowed only through the gateway channels of the state public telecommunications network. No organisation and no individual may set up or use any other channel for it. The rule is written about channels, and the word VPN does not appear in it at all. Break it and the police order the connection stopped and issue a warning. They may add a fine of up to 15,000 yuan and confiscate whatever was earned by it. If another law is broken at the same time, that one applies as well, and a crime is prosecuted.
title: The law says nothing about VPNs: it forbids every channel but the state one

body: If you carry narcotic drugs or class I psychotropic substances into or out of China for treatment, bring a medical diagnosis certificate. It must come from a medical institution. Bring proof of your identity too. You may carry no more than the maximum dose of a single prescription. Customs releases them on the principle of personal use and a reasonable amount. The text does not state a penalty for arriving without the papers. Prescription limits are as follows. Injectable forms: one dose. Other forms: no more than 3 days' worth. Sustained-release preparations: no more than 7 days' worth. For class II psychotropic substances the limit is normally 7 days' worth. A doctor may allow longer in special cases if the reason is written down.
title: Narcotics and class I psychotropics: bring a diagnosis certificate and ID

body: China's nature reserves are divided into a core protection zone and a general control zone. In the core zone, human activity is banned except for listed kinds, such as monitoring, research, rescue work and residents' needs. Activities allowed by laws or approved by the State Council are also exempt. In the general control zone, only listed activities are allowed, and eco-tourism is among them. Reserves that protect natural relics may allow eco-tourism in the core zone after scientific review. An activity outside the list can bring a fine of up to 100,000 yuan in the core zone. In the general control zone, the fine is up to 50,000 yuan. Illegal building works cost up to 1 million yuan in the core zone and up to 500,000 yuan in the general control zone. Causing ecological damage costs up to 5 million yuan in the core zone and up to 2 million yuan in the general control zone. Without approval, foreigners may not collect specimens or do similar things anywhere in a reserve. The basis is the Regulations on Nature Reserves, State Council Order No. 830, in force since 15 March 2026.
title: China's nature reserves: activity in the core zone, a fine up to 100,000 yuan

body: Staying in China past your permitted time brings a warning, and in a serious case 500 yuan for each day. The fine stops at 10,000 yuan, but five to fifteen days of detention can be imposed instead. Working without the right to work costs 5,000 to 20,000 yuan, with the same detention in a serious case. Refusing to show your entry documents or your residence permit to the police brings a warning and up to 2,000 yuan. Whoever puts up or hides a foreigner staying illegally pays 2,000 to 10,000 yuan of their own.
title: Every day of overstay is 500 yuan, and work without the right is dearer

body: Stay anywhere but a hotel and you must register yourself. Article 39 of the Exit and Entry Administration Law allows 24 hours from arrival. Registration goes through the local public security organ, and the person accommodating you may do it for you. A hotel registers you automatically at check-in — which is exactly why the duty gets forgotten. You will need your passport and the tenancy agreement; some cities, Beijing among them, accept it online. Article 76 punishes failure with a warning and a fine of up to 2,000 yuan.
title: Register your address within 24 hours

body: Parts of China are closed to foreigners, and entering one without approval means being ordered out at once. In a serious case it is five to ten days of detention. Whatever you gathered there is taken: written records, audio and video, files on your devices and other things are confiscated or destroyed. The equipment used to gather them is confiscated as well. Refusing an order from the police or state security to leave an area by a set date brings five to fifteen days of detention.
title: Wander into an area closed to foreigners and the photos go too

body: Residence starts at 183 days in a calendar year, but that alone does not tax everything. Foreign income becomes taxable only from the seventh consecutive year. It also requires more than 183 days here in each of the six preceding years. The count resets in two ways: a year under 183 days, or a single trip abroad longer than 30 consecutive days. The exemption is not automatic: it has to be filed with your local tax office. The count runs from 2019, so the earliest year the rule can bite is 2025.
title: Worldwide income from the seventh year, and a month abroad resets the count

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. China itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. Transit counts too: a layover of more than 12 hours at an airport in an affected country is treated as arriving from there. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

body: Medicines containing narcotics, such as morphine, must be prescribed by your doctor, and you may bring a quantity for your own use. Coming from outside the Schengen area, carry a multilingual certificate from the prescribing doctor with the doses, active ingredient and length of the trip. The health authority of the country you come from must authenticate it. Ordinary medicines may be brought for personal needs, up to three months' supply of each. Counterfeit medicines may not be brought in even for personal use.
title: From outside Schengen, a narcotic medicine needs an authenticated certificate

applies_when: you need a Schengen visa
body: The foreign ministry lists the conditions for issuing a visa plainly, and the consulate must establish each of the four positively for every applicant. First, the purpose of the trip must be plausible and comprehensible. Second, living and travel costs must be covered from the applicant's own assets or income. Third, the holder must be willing to leave the Schengen area before the visa expires. Fourth, travel health insurance valid across the whole Schengen area and for the entire stay. If own funds cannot be proven, a formal undertaking from a third party can cover the financing, under sections 66 and 68 of the Residence Act.
title: Germany checks four conditions for the visa, each one separately

body: It is not the calendar year that makes you resident but an unbroken stay of more than six months. Such a stay may start in October and end in April. The count runs not from day 183 but from the first day of that stay, so residence arrives retroactively, and short absences are ignored. There is a let-out that few know about. The rule does not apply if the stay is purely private — visiting, recreation or medical treatment — and lasts no more than a year. The second route is shorter and has no let-out: keeping a dwelling here that you intend to use is enough, and days stop mattering. A resident is taxed on worldwide income.
title: Six months running makes you resident retroactively, but a holiday has a let-out

body: Entering an environmental zone (Umweltzone) is allowed only for cars displaying a green Umweltplakette on the windscreen. Foreign-plated vehicles are covered in exactly the same way. The badge is valid in every environmental zone and has not changed since 2007, so even a new Euro 6 car gets a green one. Driving or parking in a zone without one is a regulatory offence carrying a €100 fine. Visitors from abroad are advised to order the badge about three weeks before the trip. The main rental-car trap: the badge is the owner's responsibility, that is the rental company's, but the fine reaches you. Check the windscreen before you drive off the lot.
title: No green sticker, no city centre — and the fine follows you even in a rental

body: Publicly displaying the symbols of banned organisations — flags, badges, uniform parts, slogans and forms of greeting — is prohibited by law. The penalty is up to three years in prison or a fine. It applies to everyone in Germany, and not knowing about it is no defence. Tourists have been detained precisely for a photo with such a gesture outside the Reichstag. Symbols confusingly similar to the banned ones are covered too.
title: A banned gesture in front of the Reichstag costs up to three years

body: The threshold covers all currencies at once: cash and traveller's cheques are added up and converted to dollars. Above 10,000 a written declaration is required, counted per person and per crossing of the union's external border. Above 100,000 you must also prove where the money came from. Between the member states — Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia — there is no customs border, so on such flights there is nothing to declare. You answer for the silence, not for the sum.
title: Over $10,000 needs a declaration, and all currencies count together

body: Egyptian law treats taking an antiquity out of the country as smuggling, not as a customs matter. Article 41 of the antiquities protection law punishes it with temporary hard labour or a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 Egyptian pounds. The object itself is confiscated, along with the equipment and the vehicle used to move it. The case need not even reach the airport. Under article 43, possessing an antiquity disposed of contrary to the law carries one to two years in prison. So an old-looking coin or figurine bought at a market is a hazard in itself. If it looks old, safer not to buy it: proving its age will be your problem.
title: Taking antiquities out is a criminal offence, market souvenirs included

body: Propagation material is a separate matter, and the personal allowance does not cover it. Under plant quarantine regulation 562/2019 any regulated consignment may enter only under a quarantine import permit. The exemption for personal items up to 50 kg expressly does not extend to propagation material: seeds, saplings, seedlings, cuttings. Quarantine inspectors examine goods accompanying passengers too. So a sapling or a packet of seeds bought as a gift will not make it home — it will be taken at the border.
title: A sapling or a packet of seeds will be taken at the border

body: Local currency has a hard ceiling in both directions: no more than 5,000 Egyptian pounds in and no more than 5,000 out. Foreign currency has no limit on arrival, but an amount from 10,000 US dollars or the equivalent must be disclosed. On the way out the 10,000 becomes a ceiling rather than a threshold. A non-Egyptian may take out more only if it was disclosed on arrival. So the arrival declaration is not paperwork for its own sake — it is what lets you leave with the money you did not spend.
title: No more than 5,000 Egyptian pounds, and declare foreign currency above $10,000

body: The Civil Aviation Ministry issues flight permits for drones. The application asks for a letter from the company or client and a request signed and stamped with the company seal. It also needs the original airworthiness certificate, the company's operating competence certificate and the insurance certificate. Processing takes a week from filing if the papers raise no remarks. Fixed fees are paid when applying.
title: Egypt's drone flight permit asks for a company's papers

body: Carry an international permit alongside your national driving licence. Your national licence must travel with it, because the international permit translates your national licence rather than replacing it. Roadside officers accept the pair far quicker than working out which convention applies today. Egypt acceded to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic on 15 December 2023. The United Nations depositary lists Egypt as a party, with no reservation recorded. Egypt was outside the convention before that date, which is why older guidance still says a foreign licence counts for nothing here.
title: Carry an international driving permit with your licence in Egypt

body: Egypt keeps an IMEI register: a handset that has run on an Egyptian SIM for more than 90 days without being registered loses service. A short trip on a foreign SIM needs nothing. On 21 January 2026 the customs authority and the regulator NTRA annulled the general exemption for the phone a passenger carries. Tourists and Egyptians living abroad keep the exemption for the same 90 days. A second phone is a separate trap: with a local SIM in it past 90 days, duty falls due at up to 38.5% of its value. Registration goes through the Telephony app by IMEI. If you already holidayed in Egypt with this phone before 2025 and used a local SIM, its IMEI is already on file.
title: Phone blocked after 90 days on a local SIM

body: Personal photography in public places is free in Egypt: no permit, no fee, for residents and tourists alike. The exceptions are named. Land, buildings, installations and equipment of the ministries of defence, military production and interior are photographed only with prior approval. So are other sovereign, security and judicial bodies, the chambers of parliament, and the buildings of ministries and government offices. Publishing is limited too: no images that insult the country or its people, and nothing indecent. Children are not photographed at all, and people are not photographed or published without their written consent. The decree names no penalty, so what follows a breach comes from other laws.
title: Filming a ministry or a military site needs permission first

body: In Egypt's natural protectorates, catching, transporting, killing or disturbing wildlife is forbidden. So is damaging or removing living organisms or natural features, such as shells, corals, rocks or soil, for any purpose. Damaging or removing plants and polluting the soil, water or air are banned too. Driving vehicles there needs the administrative body's permission, within the limits set by Prime Minister's decree. A breach carries a fine of 500 to 5,000 Egyptian pounds and/or up to a year in prison. A repeat offender is fined 3,000 to 10,000 pounds and/or imprisoned for at least a year. The offender also pays for removal or repair, and equipment used may be confiscated. The basis is Law No. 102 of 1983 on nature protectorates.
title: Egypt's protectorates: removing shells or coral, up to a year in prison

body: Travellers of certain nationalities must register within seven days of each entry into Egypt. Register with the Immigration Authority or a police station that has an Immigration Department desk. Bring the original passport you used to enter Egypt. The duty covers all visa types, including tourist and business visas, and residency permits. Select hotels may be able to register you. If you do not register, you may have problems when leaving Egypt. You may also be unable to get a residency visa endorsement. You may be fined from EGP 350 to EGP 1,500 (Egyptian pounds). No official list of nationalities has been published, and more may be added. The reports name 36 countries, among them Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Check with an immigration officer on arrival whether the duty applies to you.
title: Some nationalities must register within seven days of each entry to Egypt

body: Egypt's income tax law counts you as a resident in several ways, and the day count is only one. You are resident if you stay in Egypt for more than the law's day limit within twelve months. Those days may be consecutive or spread across several trips. You are also resident if you have a permanent home in Egypt. The executive regulation gives "permanent home" a wide meaning. It covers being in Egypt most of the year, in a place you own, rent or occupy in any capacity at all. It also covers having a commercial shop, a professional office, a factory or another workplace in Egypt where you carry on your activity. So staying under the day limit does not protect you if you have such a workplace there. The text gives no penalty. It only sets who counts as resident for the income tax law.
title: Egypt treats you as resident for tax by days, permanent home or workplace

body: Tramadol is an ordinary painkiller in the West, but Egypt treats it as a narcotic. Bringing it in even with a valid prescription can lead to arrest for drug trafficking. Travellers have received multi-year prison terms. The same applies to other controlled opioids. If you genuinely need a restricted medicine, carry a doctor's medical certificate legalized by the Egyptian embassy in your country. Practical takeaway: check every medicine in advance and don't assume a prescription will protect you.
title: Tramadol and opioids = narcotics, even with a prescription

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. Egypt itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. Transit counts too: a layover of more than 12 hours at an airport in an affected country is treated as arriving from there. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

body: A Spanish child under 18 who lives in Spain needs written permission to leave Spain without a parent or guardian. The father, mother or guardian must sign it. The child also needs a valid ID. For travel within the European Union, the European Economic Area and Switzerland, that is the national identity document (DNI). For any other country, it is a valid passport. The permission is shown at border crossings. A child without valid permission cannot travel. Forms and the procedure are on the websites of the Spanish Ministry of the Interior for the DNI and the passport. If a situation requires a minor to leave Spain over a period of time, one permission that covers the circumstances is enough. The requirement does not apply to Spanish children living in Spain who enter Spain unaccompanied, or to Spanish children habitually resident outside Spain. Non-Spanish children need no permission to leave Spain, unless a specific law of a state requires it.
title: Spanish minors living in Spain need signed permission to leave unaccompanied

body: Since 2023 low emission zones are compulsory in every municipality over 50,000 inhabitants and in island territories. Where air quality limits are exceeded, municipalities over 20,000 must have one too. The trap is the sticker: the traffic authority issues the environmental badge to vehicles on its own register, so a foreign plate does not have one. Cities therefore keep separate registers: in the Barcelona metropolitan area every foreign-plated vehicle must register, and one registration covers all of its zones. Breaching a zone restriction is a serious offence carrying a 200 euro fine, reduced to 100 if paid voluntarily within twenty days. For a visitor the sting is elsewhere: if the driver cannot show legal residence in Spain, the officer sets the amount on the spot. Without payment the car must be moved and immobilised where the officer says.
title: Low emission zones: register a foreign plate, or pay the fine on the spot

body: Spain is one of the few Schengen countries that actually checks the financial-means requirement on entry. In 2026 the rate is about €122 per person per day, but there is a floor: no less than €1,089.90 regardless of trip length. So even for a four-day trip you must show the full minimum, not €122 × 4. Cash, a bank statement or a card with available credit all count. Fail to prove it and you can be turned back at the border — holding a visa does not help.
title: Border officers may ask you to prove funds — about €122 per day

applies_when: you need a Schengen visa
body: Spain's consulates name the part most often forgotten: a holder of a multiple-entry visa must carry valid medical insurance on every entry into the Schengen states. The policy also has to be valid for the full duration of the visa applied for, not only the first trip. A renewable policy counts only up to the end of its current period, so one that renews itself monthly proves nothing beyond that month. What the cover must amount to and what it must pay for is the Schengen requirement, stated with it.
title: With a multiple-entry visa the policy travels with you every time

body: You are treated as habitually resident in Spain if either of two things applies. The first is staying in Spain more than 183 days in the calendar year. The second is having the main centre or base of your activities or economic interests in Spain, directly or indirectly. Occasional absences count toward the days, unless you can prove tax residence in another country. Temporary stays under voluntary cultural or humanitarian cooperation agreements with Spanish public authorities do not count. Proof of tax residence abroad is a certificate from that country's tax authority, valid for one year. A residence permit there does not by itself make you a tax resident there. You are also presumed resident in Spain if your spouse and dependent minor children habitually live in Spain, unless there is evidence to the contrary. This applies only if your spouse is not legally separated. Residence status covers the whole calendar year, so a change of residence does not split it. If you claim residence in a tax haven, now called a non-cooperative jurisdiction, the tax administration may require proof of 183 days there. Where two countries both treat you as resident, Spain's double taxation agreements generally look first at where you have a permanent home.
title: More than 183 days in Spain in a year makes you a Spanish tax resident

applies_when: you arrive from a country outside the EU. It does not apply to travel within the EU, or from Norway, Switzerland, Iceland and Liechtenstein.
body: Meat and dairy from outside the Union cannot be brought in for personal use, in hand luggage or checked alike, and the quantity does not matter. The exemptions are three and each has its own limit. Powdered infant milk, infant food and medically required foods pass up to 2 kg combined, if unrefrigerated before opening and in branded packaging for direct sale. Fishery products pass up to 20 kg or the weight of one fish, whichever is higher — so one large fish is allowed whatever it weighs. Everything else not on the prohibited part of the annex passes up to 2 kg. What does not comply is seized and destroyed under national law.
title: No meat or dairy from outside the EU; fish up to 20 kg is allowed

body: The duty is the same at every external border of the Union. Carrying cash of 10,000 euros or more, you declare it to the authorities of the member state you enter or leave through. You also have to make it available for control. Cash is wider than banknotes: currency, bearer-negotiable instruments, prepaid cards, and gold — coins of at least 90% gold content, bullion of at least 99.5%. Failure is not settled with a fine alone. The authorities may detain the cash by administrative decision for up to 30 days, or 90 after an assessment of necessity and proportionality. The penalty itself is national: you may carry any amount, and the offence is staying silent.
title: From 10,000 euros you declare, and a prepaid card counts as cash

body: A drone under 250 grams does not escape registration: if it has a camera and is not a toy, the operator must be registered. It is the person who is registered, not the aircraft, and it is done through the national aviation authority. Drones with a C1–C4 class label and home-built ones up to 25 kilograms are registered in any case. The remote pilot must be at least 16, though a state may lower that to 12.
title: The camera matters more than the weight: a 249-gram drone needs registration

body: The ban on meat and dairy from third countries is the European one, and French customs applies it in full. What French customs adds is who counts as a third country. Since 1 January 2021 the United Kingdom does, so cheese brought from London is barred like any other. The list they name is broad — meat, pâté and sausage, milk, yoghurt, cheese, butter. From Andorra, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Northern Ireland there is no quantity limit at all.
title: Cheese from London is barred too: the United Kingdom is a third country

body: Driving in a low-emission zone (ZFE-m) of a French city requires a Crit'Air sticker. In the Greater Paris zone, cars that are unclassified or carry Crit'Air 5, 4 or 3 are banned on weekdays from 8:00 to 20:00. Public holidays are excepted. The sticker is also compulsory when, during a pollution episode, the prefect introduces differentiated (alternating) traffic. This is announced in the media the evening before, by 19:00. Driving in a zone in a car not allowed there, or without a sticker, usually means a fixed fine of €68. The fine can reach €450. The car can also be immobilised and impounded. The sticker costs €3.85 including postage for delivery in France. For a car registered abroad it is ordered only online, and certificat-air.gouv.fr is the only official site that issues it. It goes on the front of the car, visible from outside.
title: The Crit'Air sticker costs €3.85, and only one official site issues it

body: A child who lives in France and leaves the country without a parent or another person with parental authority must carry an exit authorization (AST). This applies to French and foreign children, throughout France including overseas territories, and on trips within the European Union. The AST is Cerfa form no. 15646*01, filled in and signed by one person with parental authority. Attach a photocopy of that parent's identity document. A French child also needs an identity card or a passport. A foreign child needs a passport, plus a Republican Identity Document (TIR) or a Movement Document for Minor Aliens (DCEM). For a foreign child, photocopy the signing parent's passport and residence permit. Show the documents to the border guard in the event of a check. No registration at the town hall or prefecture is needed. You can fill in the form online on service-public.fr or print it and fill it in by hand. If the child travels with only one parent, some countries may ask for proof that the other parent agrees, so check the destination's requirements beforehand.
title: Minors living in France need a signed exit form to travel without a parent

body: Apart from exceptions, you may not hide your face anywhere in public in France, such as a park, a cafe or a shop. The fine is 150 euros, and it can come with or be replaced by a citizenship course. A scarf, a cap or sunglasses are allowed as long as your face is identifiable; a balaclava, a burqa or a mask are not. Exceptions: clothing required by law or for health or work, sport, artistic or traditional events and places of worship. At a demonstration, hiding your face to avoid identification is punished more heavily, up to a year in prison where disorder occurs or may occur. A French or EU citizen without proof of identity may be held up to 4 hours, or 8 in Mayotte and French Guiana. A foreigner who cannot show a residence document may be taken to police or gendarmerie premises to have their right to stay checked.
title: Hiding your face in public in France: 150 euros in the general case

body: There are four tests and they do not add up: meeting any single one is enough. The tests are a home or main place of stay in France, a professional activity here, or the centre of your economic interests. The fourth is state service abroad with no personal tax there. The home is where the family normally lives, so someone posted abroad who left their family here is normally still resident in France. The reverse is awkward too. A main place of stay means more than six months in a year, regardless of where the family is and whether you live in a hotel. Only a double taxation treaty can soften the outcome, an international rule standing above domestic law under article 55 of the Constitution.
title: Any one of the tests is enough, and counting days is optional

body: Bringing cash of £10,000 or more in or out between Great Britain and any country outside the UK requires a declaration. A family or group is counted together: if the total reaches £10,000 you must declare, even when each person carries less. Fail to declare and Border Force seizes all the cash you are carrying. To get it back you may have to pay a penalty of up to £5,000. The declaration can be filed 72 hours before travel online, or on the spot through the red channel. The declaration itself carries no penalty: any sum may be carried, what is punished is staying silent.
title: £10,000 in cash or more must be declared, or all of it is seized

body: To bring a controlled medicine into the United Kingdom you need a letter from your doctor. It must state your name, address, date of birth, travel dates, destination and the medicine itself with its dose and total amount. Carry the medicine in your hand luggage, in its original packaging with a readable label, and keep the letter with it. A separate Home Office licence is needed if you carry more than three months' supply. It is free, but must be applied for at least 14 days ahead.
title: A controlled medicine needs a letter from your doctor

body: Before flying a drone or model aircraft outdoors in the UK, you must hold the IDs the CAA (Civil Aviation Authority) requires for its weight. Flying without them is against the law. You can be fined, and in the most serious cases you could be sent to prison. A drone of 100g to less than 250g needs a Flyer ID. With a camera it also needs an Operator ID. Without a camera the Operator ID is optional. A drone of 250g to less than 25kg needs both a Flyer ID and an Operator ID. Under 100g no Flyer ID is required, though the CAA strongly recommends one. You do not need either ID if you only fly indoors or where the aircraft cannot escape, such as inside a closed netted area. The CAA does not recognise overseas registrations or qualifications. Visitors must get both IDs from the CAA before flying in the UK.
title: UK drones from 100g need a Flyer ID; with a camera, an Operator ID too

body: Before you take a child abroad, you must get permission from everyone with parental responsibility for the child, or from a court. Taking a child abroad without permission is child abduction. A mother automatically has parental responsibility, but she still needs permission from anyone else who has it. A letter from the person with parental responsibility is usually enough. It should include their contact details and details of the trip. You might be asked for it at a UK or foreign border. If you cannot get permission, apply to a court. Give the trip dates, the return details and the contacts of people with parental responsibility who are staying in the UK. For a longer trip, give more information, such as the child's education abroad. Exception: with a child arrangement order saying the child lives with you, you can go for 28 days without permission. That does not apply if a court order says you cannot. Check the age limit for a child with the embassy or consulate of the country you are going to.
title: Taking a child abroad from the UK needs everyone's parental permission

body: Driving into London is charged twice over. The Ultra Low Emission Zone costs 12.50 pounds a day for vehicles that fail the emission standards. Entering the centre costs another 18 pounds, on weekdays from 7 to 18 and at weekends from 12 to 18. A foreign number plate changes nothing: the charge and the penalty are issued in exactly the same way. The centre charge can be paid as late as midnight on the third day after the journey, but then it is 21 pounds. An unpaid day costs a 180 pound penalty, or 90 if settled within two weeks. A charging day runs from midnight to midnight, so a drive through the zone at night is two chargeable days and two separate penalties.
title: London charges twice over, and a night drive counts as two days

applies_when: you are entering Great Britain — England, Scotland or Wales — and what you may carry depends on whether you come from the European Union area or from outside it. The Union here also takes in Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, the Faroe Islands and Greenland.
body: Great Britain takes meat and dairy off you even when you arrive from the European Union. Cheese, milk, butter, yoghurt, pork, beef, lamb, mutton, goat, venison and anything made from those meats may not come in. Fish, poultry, eggs and honey from those same countries are still allowed. From outside the Union no meat and no milk products pass at all, and fish is capped at 20 kilograms. Powdered infant milk, infant food and medically needed food pass up to 2 kilograms, unrefrigerated and in unopened branded packaging. Declare it and the food is destroyed; say nothing and the fine reaches 5,000 pounds, or the case goes to court. If you are unsure about something, take the red channel.
title: Meat and dairy are taken off you, the European Union included

body: Bringing a dog, cat or ferret into Great Britain follows a separate scheme with two strict conditions. First: the animal travels as manifest cargo only. Cabin and hold travel are not accepted on flights into the country, with private charters the sole exception. Second applies to dogs only: treatment against tapeworm with a praziquantel product. The window is narrow — no earlier than 120 hours and no later than 24 hours before arrival, that is between one and five days. Done sooner or later, the animal is refused; cats are not covered by this requirement. You must arrive by an approved route through a designated point of entry.
title: A dog must be wormed 1-5 days before arrival, and cannot fly in the cabin

body: Do not ride a privately owned electric scooter on public land. If you do, you could face a fine, you could get penalty points on your licence, and the scooter could be impounded. The government trial rules cover rental e-scooters only. They do not apply to private ones. A rental e-scooter from a trial may be used on the road, but not on motorways. You may also use it in cycle lanes in an official trial area. Never ride it on the pavement. To use a rental e-scooter you need a provisional or full UK driving licence with a category Q entitlement. A valid overseas licence also works if it meets the conditions in the guidance. You cannot ride one while drunk or otherwise intoxicated.
title: Privately owned e-scooters are illegal on public land

body: The 183-day threshold works one way only: spend that much and you are a resident outright. But you can also become one at 16 days, if you were resident here in one of the past three years. That takes four ties to the country: accommodation, work, family and time spent here before. The more ties, the fewer days needed: two ties and 91 days is enough, one tie and 121. Someone who was never resident here is outright non-resident below 46 days.
title: Sixteen days can make you a resident — if you have ties to the country

body: The Immigration Rules let an officer cancel entry clearance on arrival when the purpose you name differs from the purpose written in it. They also allow refusal when a passport does not satisfy the officer about who you are. A visitor must separately satisfy the decision maker of being a genuine one. That means leaving at the end of the visit and not making the country a home through frequent visits. It also means funds for the whole trip without working. So carry the return ticket, the booking and proof of money. And answer exactly what you put in the application — the mismatch itself is a ground.
title: A visa can be cancelled on arrival if your purpose differs from it

body: Cash and securities over 30,000 lari (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared at customs; below the threshold you don't. Carrying more than the threshold without a declaration, or with an incorrect one, means a fine from 3,000 lari (for sums of 30,000-50,000 lari) or confiscation. Use the red channel if you carry more than the limit.
title: Declare cash over GEL 30,000

body: You may bring medicines for yourself, but with conditions. Products containing controlled substances are allowed only for personal use and only in a quantity not exceeding a 31-day course. They must be declared at customs. You need a prescription or a doctor's note stating your details, the medicine name, composition, dosage and duration of use. Carry the medicines in original packaging so the name and active ingredient are legible. Unlawful import of narcotic or psychotropic substances is a criminal offence in Georgia.
title: A controlled medicine: no more than a 31-day course

body: Cultural valuables may leave Georgia only on a permit from the Ministry of Culture, which is what allows the item through customs and across the border. The permit is single-use and valid for three months, and the item goes through a mandatory state appraisal before it is issued. The list is broad and reads like a flea market stall. It covers archaeological finds, coins and seals over 100 years old, ethnographic material, handmade paintings and applied art, sculpture, engravings and old books. Stamps withdrawn from circulation, furniture 100 years or older and antique musical instruments are on it too. An ordinary souvenir is outside the law: modern crafts of a souvenir character and serially produced goods are expressly excluded. The seller does not decide which is which, the appraisal does, so arrange the permit for anything old before you leave.
title: An icon, a dagger or an old coin: only with a Ministry of Culture permit

body: In Georgia, intentionally damaging or destroying a cultural heritage site is a crime, punished by a fine or up to two years in prison. Intentionally damaging a monument of national significance carries a fine or two to four years. Destroying a national monument, or damaging or destroying a world heritage monument, carries four to eight years. Even by negligence, damaging cultural heritage or a national monument carries a fine or up to a year. The basis is Article 259² of the Criminal Code of Georgia.
title: Damaging cultural heritage in Georgia: a fine or prison, up to eight years
