body: Georgia answers drink-driving by suspending the right to drive rather than by fining you. Between 0.3 and 0.7 promille of ethanol in the blood the right is suspended for six months. Above 0.7, or if you refuse the test, it is suspended for a year. Driving while suspended adds 2,000 lari, five to fifteen days of detention and another year of suspension. A driver who has no licence at all pays 2,000 lari for the same offence.
title: Drink-driving here takes the right to drive, not money

body: Operators of drones of 250 g or more register online with Georgia's Civil Aviation Agency on uas.gov.ge. Registering the drone itself is free of charge. Label the drone with your registration number before flying. In the open category the remote pilot needs a competency certificate, issued after a free online test. Keep the drone within 120 metres of the ground, unless overflying an obstacle, and at a safe distance from people. Over public events you fly only with the agency's special permission or if the operator holds a LUC with the appropriate privileges. Restricted and prohibited areas need an authorisation.
title: A drone of 250 g or more is registered with Georgia's aviation agency

body: Article 260 of the criminal code punishes illegal acquisition and storage of a narcotic drug with imprisonment of up to 6 years. The long sentences begin one step further out. A large quantity, a group acting by prior agreement, an official position used or a repeat carries 5 to 8 years. An especially large quantity or an organised group carries 8 to 20 years or life. Consumption without a prescription sits elsewhere, in article 273, together with small quantities. That article reaches only a person penalised under the administrative code or previously convicted, and costs a fine or 120 to 180 hours of community service. So the frightening figures are real, and they are the top of a scale whose bottom is somewhere else entirely.
title: Possession carries up to 6 years; a large amount, 8 to 20 years or life

body: A foreigner may drive in Georgia on a national licence until it expires, but no longer than one year from their last entry. The word to notice is last: leaving and coming back resets the count. For someone who steps out now and then, the year never runs out. The law does not require an international permit: the national licence alone gives the right to drive. After the year the licence is exchanged for a Georgian one without a test. You bring an application, a passport or residence permit, the licence itself, proof of registration or address, and a fee. A rental company may demand an international permit separately, but that is a term of its contract, not a requirement of the law.
title: A licence is good for a year, counted from your last entry

body: Georgia sets the allowance by type of border crossing, and the gap is sixfold. Arrive by air and goods worth up to 3,000 GEL and up to 30 kg come in duty-free. Arrive by car or bus and it is only 500 GEL for the same 30 kg, once per 30 calendar days. Food is counted separately: 500 GEL and 30 kg per calendar day. Anything above the allowance must be declared in writing, as must cash from 30,000 GEL.
title: 500 GEL at a land border, 3,000 by air

body: Moving your car away from the scene of a road accident in Georgia is fined 250 lari by itself. Leaving the scene, with the car or on foot, costs 250 lari and the right to drive for six months. Someone who had no licence in the first place pays 1,500 lari instead. Not stopping when a traffic policeman signals costs 500 lari. If any of it creates a hazard or blocks traffic, the fine goes up again.
title: Driving off after a bump costs the licence for six months

body: From 1 January 2026, under government resolution 602, a tourist must enter Georgia holding a valid health and accident insurance policy. The sum insured must be at least 30,000 lari, and the policy must cover the whole stay, from entry to departure. A Georgian or a foreign insurer will do, and the policy may be shown on paper or on a screen, in Georgian or English. It is checked at the crossing point by the patrol police, not by an airline and not by a hotel. The law sets no fine for the tourist: the border is the only place where not having a policy changes anything. The rule does not apply to diplomatic passports and visas, or to drivers working international freight and passenger routes.
title: From 2026 the policy is checked at the border, 30,000 lari minimum

body: Staying past your lawful time in Georgia costs 1,000 lari and a ban on entering for six months. More than three months over, and it becomes 2,000 lari with a two-year ban. Beyond a year it is 3,000 lari and three years. Breaking the rules of transit through the country costs 500 lari. The fine follows you out: until it is paid, no Georgian visa and no permission to enter are given. Whoever invited you is not safe either — inviting or employing a foreigner against the rules brings a warning or 2,000 lari.
title: Overstaying costs 1,000 lari and six months of not being let back in

body: Swearing in a public place, pestering people offensively or otherwise disturbing public order is petty hooliganism. It costs 500 to 3,000 lari, or administrative detention of up to twenty days. A second time brings 3,000 to 5,000 lari or detention of five to sixty days. For a foreigner the code adds expulsion from Georgia and a ban on entering for up to three years. An unpaid fine on the second offence is replaced by detention rather than forgiven.
title: Swearing in the street can cost 3,000 lari and, for a foreigner, expulsion

body: The threshold is 183 days, but not inside a calendar year. The tax code counts them in any unbroken twelve calendar months that end in the tax year in question. Leaving in December resets nothing. Any part of a day counts as a whole day. Days spent abroad for treatment, rest, a business trip or study are counted as days in Georgia, so a break does not always break the count. Days pass uncounted only in narrow cases: diplomatic and consular status, staff of international organisations, transit through Georgia, and a stay for treatment or rest.
title: 183 days are counted over any twelve months in a row, not over a calendar year

body: Before any drone flight in Greece you must check the airspace restrictions on the DAGR (Drone Aware Greece) platform. In its yellow and magenta zones, such as airports and archaeological sites, flights may be allowed under conditions or banned outright. Prior approval is required in most cases. Do not fly over critical sites such as ports, hospitals, archaeological sites or military and government installations without prior authorisation from the HCAA. In a yellow or magenta zone you must submit an authorisation request to the HCAA before flying. Send the Drone Flight Notification Form at least 5 working days ahead. You will receive an email reply with instructions for your flight. Outside these zones no special approval is needed if you follow the EASA Open Category rules.
title: Greece: check DAGR first; drones in yellow or magenta zones need an HCAA request

body: During a short-term stay in Croatia, a third-country national must have registered accommodation. Whoever provides the accommodation must register it within one day of your arrival, through eVisitor or by notifying the local police. If the host cannot register it, you must do it yourself within two days of entering Croatia or of changing accommodation.
title: Croatia: register your accommodation within two days if the host cannot

body: This applies to Canadian citizens aged 18 to 35 who want to enter Croatia under the Canada–Croatia youth mobility memorandum. They are required to regulate their temporary residence. Canadians need no visa to enter, but must apply for initial temporary residence. The application goes to a Croatian embassy or consulate in the country where they legally live, or to a local police station in Croatia. You need these documents: a passport valid beyond the planned stay, and a return ticket or enough money to buy one. You also need proof of funds, health insurance, a criminal record certificate and proof of accommodation. A consular fee of 100 $ is charged, it may change, and it is not refundable. Once residence is granted, register at the local police station within 3 days of entering Croatia. Within one month of arrival, hand in proof of accommodation, such as a lease, to the police. The scheme can be used only twice, with a pause between stays, and each stay may not exceed 12 months. The text does not say what happens if these steps are skipped.
title: Canadians aged 18 to 35 on the youth scheme must apply for temporary residence

body: Bringing drugs into or out of Croatia is forbidden. The exception is medicine that contains drugs. You may carry only what you need for up to five days, and you must have the right medical documents with you. Other medicines for personal use may be brought in for treatment of up to one month. These also need medical documents, such as your medical history. The text does not state a penalty for breaking this rule.
title: Croatia: medicines with drugs limited to five days, others to one month

body: If you change your tax status from non-resident to resident of Croatia, you fill in Questionnaire TU. You hand it to the competent tax office when you register in the Register of Tax Payers. If you change from resident to non-resident, you fill in Questionnaire TI. You submit it when you deregister from the Register. The tax authority may also ask for the form in other situations. Attach documents that back up your answers, such as copies of identity documents and a tax residency certificate from another State. Originals need a certified Croatian translation in Latin script. You sign that your answers are true, accurate and complete, under full material and criminal liability. Under the General Tax Act, you have a permanent residence if you own or hold an apartment for at least 183 days. That period can fall in one or two calendar years. You do not have to stay in the apartment.
title: Becoming or ceasing to be a Croatian tax resident requires a questionnaire

body: Every arriving passenger, children and infants included, must fill in the All Indonesia form in advance and get a QR code (allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id or the app). It merges the former customs and health declarations. Submit within 3 days before entry. Mandatory since 1 September 2025 at Denpasar, Jakarta and Surabaya, and since 1 October 2025 at all international airports. One adult may file for the family, but each traveller gets their own QR code. Without the QR code you will not clear customs — officers have no manual override. The declaration covers luggage pieces and goods above duty-free limits: alcohol, tobacco, medicines, electronics (which may also need IMEI registration).
title: All Indonesia: mandatory form before arrival

body: Report cash and other payment instruments of 100 million rupiah or more—in any currency—to customs on entry and exit. If you say nothing at all, the fine is 10 per cent of the entire amount you carry, not just the excess. If you report but get the figure wrong, customs charges 10 per cent on the difference only. Either way, the fine stops at 300 million rupiah.
title: Declare cash from 100 million rupiah or pay a fine on the whole sum

body: The health ministry's order on the classification of narcotics puts codeine in schedule three, under its chemical name, three-methylmorphine. Dihydrocodeine, ethylmorphine, norcodeine and acetyldihydrocodeine are on the same list. That matters because a cough syrup or a painkiller sold over a counter elsewhere is a scheduled narcotic here. Bringing one in is a question under the narcotics law, not a customs formality. Carry the prescription and a doctor's letter, and ask the mission before you fly whether your medicine needs separate authorisation. If it does and you have none, the medicine is contraband rather than luggage.
title: Codeine is a scheduled narcotic here, and the schedule is a ministry order

body: Indonesian immigration law does not ask whether you were paid. Article 122 punishes a foreigner who deliberately does something other than what their residence permit was granted for. The penalty is up to 5 years and a fine of up to 500 million rupiah. The same article punishes anyone who orders a foreigner to do so or gives them the opportunity. So the villa that hosts you for a review and the brand that arranges it are inside the provision, not beside it. There is a visa for the purpose: the official list carries C5A, the content creator visit visa.
title: Working outside your visa purpose: up to 5 years, and your host answers too

body: In Indonesia, cultural heritage (cagar budaya) means objects, buildings, structures, sites and areas formally designated as worth preserving. They are chosen for their importance to history, science, education, religion or culture, on land or in water. No one may damage cultural heritage, in whole or in part. Deliberately damaging it carries up to 15 years in prison, a fine of up to 5,000,000,000 rupiah, or both. The basis is Law No. 11 of 2010 on Cultural Heritage, Articles 1, 66 and 105.
title: Damaging Indonesia's designated heritage: up to 15 years in prison

body: In principle the regulation allows flying from sunrise to sunset. A night flight needs the Director General's approval after a safety assessment. In uncontrolled airspace you may fly up to 400 feet, that is 120 metres, without approval; higher needs it. Approval is also needed in controlled airspace, in an airport's safety zone and within 3 nautical miles of a helipad outside it. Prohibited and restricted areas need the approval of the authority in charge of them. Flying without approval or against it can bring criminal sanctions, revocation of an approval and blacklisting. The regulation also allows jamming the frequency, forcing the drone out and bringing it down in a safe area.
title: Drones fly from sunrise to sunset; at night only with approval

body: Enter your brought phone or tablet's IMEI into the customs register for an Indonesian SIM card to work. Registration is free, but you pay 10 per cent import duty and 12 per cent VAT (value-added tax). The extra duty and the income tax are not charged. Declare your goods on arrival, electronically or to an officer, to deduct 500 dollars from the customs value of personal goods. Declare nothing and duty is worked out on the full value. Ordinary baggage has no two-device limit; the goods only have to be personal rather than merchandise. The rule of two applies to free zones such as Batam, and the length of your trip has nothing to do with it.
title: Phone IMEI: the 500-dollar duty cut is only for goods declared on arrival

body: Overstaying costs one million rupiah for every day, counted from the very first one. But paying your way out is not always an option: the fine applies only up to 59 days. From day 60 the penalty is different — deportation and a ban on entry, with no paying option left. Under Law 63/2024 the ban runs up to ten years and can be extended by another ten. Deportation can also come before day 60 if you cannot pay the fine. Paying it does keep you off the blacklist. Not everyone can extend their stay: visa exemption and a visa on arrival already extended once cannot be extended again — you have to leave.
title: A million rupiah a day, and from day 60 you cannot pay your way out

body: The immigration law knows no 24-hour deadline of the kind written about everywhere. The owner or manager of lodging hands over a foreign guest's details when an immigration officer on duty asks, not in advance. An officer may also request information from a private host. What sits on the foreigner, though, is a duty that usually goes unnoticed. They must report to the local immigration office any change of address, and also of civil status, citizenship, occupation and guarantor. The penalty is the same for guest and host: up to three months' detention or a fine of up to 25 million rupiah. So keep your host informed, and do not assume nothing is asked of you.
title: You report a change of address in Indonesia yourself, not your host

body: Indonesian licence classes are separate, and the ladder that lets one class stand in for another never reaches motorcycles. Class C is the motorcycle class and class A is for cars. Article 84 sets out what each class may stand in for, and C appears in none of those lists. A licence issued abroad works through an agreement between Indonesia and the issuing country. So the word motorcycle has to be on the document you hand over. At a roadside stop three separate offences are on the table: riding with no valid licence at all, up to four months or 1,000,000 rupiah. Riding without the machine's registration papers is up to 500,000, and being unable to produce a licence you do hold, up to 250,000.
title: No car licence in Indonesia covers a scooter, whichever country issued it

body: There are three tests and any one of them is enough. The first is more than 183 days within any twelve months, continuous or broken, with part of a day counted as a whole one. The second is presence during a tax year with the intention to live here, proved on paper. That paper is a residence card, or a visa or permit valid beyond 183 days. A work or tenancy contract of the same length counts, and so does evidence that the family moved. The third test disarms you: residing covers a place available to you at any time that is not merely somewhere you pass through. It covers the centre of your personal, social, economic and financial affairs and even your daily habits here, so days may not be needed at all.
title: Three tests, and days are only one of them

body: Personal goods up to a customs value of 500 dollars per person per arrival come in free of duty and tax. Above that, ten per cent duty is charged on the excess, plus VAT. Drink and tobacco are counted separately: one litre of alcohol for travellers of 21 and over, and 200 cigarettes. Vapes have their own measures: 30 millilitres of liquid for an open system, and only 12 for a closed one. Those two are for travellers of 18 and over. Carry several kinds of tobacco product and the allowance is split proportionally between them.
title: 500 dollars per arrival, and the vape liquid is measured in millilitres

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. Indonesia itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. The requirement states no separate transit rule, but with a connection in an affected country it is safer to have the certificate. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

applies_when: you arrive from a country other than Nepal, Bhutan or Myanmar — for those three the allowances are different.
body: The free allowance does not cover alcohol beyond two litres, cigarettes beyond a hundred sticks, cigars beyond twenty-five or tobacco beyond 125 grams. What stands above those lines is taxed at the baggage rates. Cigarettes pay 100 per cent plus a 3 per cent education cess. Wine and spirits pay 150 per cent plus 4 per cent; beer pays 100 per cent plus 3. Carrying anything dutiable means the red channel, because the green one is for a passenger with nothing to declare.
title: Two litres of alcohol and a hundred cigarettes, then the duty starts

body: A foreign visitor may bring in and take out Indian rupee notes — no more than 25,000 per person. Citizens of Pakistan and Bangladesh may not do so at all. Foreign currency comes in without any cap on the amount. On arrival you fill in a CDF form if the notes alone exceed $5,000, or the total foreign exchange exceeds $10,000. Keep the form: on departure it is what proves the currency was brought in. Old Indian coins are separately prohibited from being taken out.
title: You may bring rupees in — up to 25,000 — and must declare cash over $5,000

body: An international driving permit is not one document but two, made under two different conventions, and they are not interchangeable. The Indian rules define it as the licence issued in India to an Indian national for use in countries party to the Geneva Convention of 1949. The framework India works within is therefore the Geneva one. By the United Nations depositary India is a party to the Geneva Convention and not to the Vienna Convention of 1968. Permits issued in Russia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and most of Europe are the Vienna kind. Such a document has no treaty footing in India, so check which permit you hold before you travel. Traffic keeps to the left and the wheel is on the right.
title: An international permit comes in two kinds, and the Geneva one works here

body: India prohibits importing a drone, whether built up, semi-knocked-down or completely knocked down. The exceptions are narrow: government bodies, recognised educational and research organisations, drone makers for research, and defence or security needs. Every one of them still needs an import authorisation from the foreign trade directorate. The list of exceptions is exhaustive, and a traveller is not on it. Drone components, by contrast, are free to import. So a drone in the luggage is a prohibited import, and customs treats it as one.
title: A drone may not be imported at all, in any form

body: India is relaxed about alcohol, but two states are not, and the line between them is easy to miss. In Gujarat a foreign tourist may drink only on a tourist's permit, granted for the visit and never for more than a month. Without one, consuming, carrying or transporting drink draws up to six months in prison and a fine. Arriving in Gujarat already drunk is an offence of its own, even if you drank outside the state. In Bihar anyone found drinking is arrested at once and taken before a magistrate. He is let go on paying the penalty the state has set, and a month in prison follows if he does not. Release is not a right either: the magistrate may refuse it and send him into custody.
title: Alcohol in Bihar and Gujarat ends in arrest, not a warning

body: If your visa allows a stay of more than 180 days, register within 14 days of arriving in India. You apply online at indianfrro.gov.in or in the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app. No registration is needed on a visa of up to 180 days if you leave within that time. The same goes for a visa that limits each stay to 180 days, as long as you keep to that limit. Children under 12 and Overseas Citizen of India cardholders do not register. An endorsement on the visa can still require registration within the period it names. These rules replaced the Registration of Foreigners Rules of 1992 from 1 September 2025.
title: A visa longer than 180 days means registering within 14 days of arrival

applies_when: you arrive from a country other than Nepal, Bhutan or Myanmar — for those three the allowances are different.
body: Gold may be brought in as baggage only by a passenger of Indian origin or one holding an Indian passport, and only after six months abroad. Short trips inside those six months are ignored while they add up to thirty days or less. No other passenger may import gold in baggage. For those who qualify the weight, ornaments included, may not exceed one kilogram, and the duty is paid in convertible foreign currency. Their rate is 10 per cent plus a 3 per cent education cess; in other cases it is 36.05 per cent. Gold and silver in any form other than ornaments stay outside the duty-free allowance whatever they are worth.
title: A foreign passport does not let you bring gold into India at all

body: If you need a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance for medical use, ask the Narcotics Commissioner for permission to import it. Apply well before you leave your country. Send your prescription and any other relevant papers with the application. Once you have permission, you may bring the drugs with you. This applies even to drugs prohibited in India. The drugs listed in Schedule I of the NDPS Rules, 1985 (Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Rules) are prohibited there. The text does not say how long a supply may be. It also does not state a penalty for bringing these drugs without permission.
title: Narcotic or psychotropic medicines need advance permission to bring into India

body: Staying in India beyond the period your visa was issued for is an offence under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. So is breaking the conditions of your visa or a rule made under the Act, such as registration. Either is punishable with up to three years in prison, a fine of up to three lakh rupees, or both. Entering without a valid passport or visa carries up to five years or a fine of up to five lakh rupees. Using a forged or fraudulently obtained passport or visa carries two to seven years and a fine of one to ten lakh rupees.
title: Overstaying a visa or breaking the entry rules: up to three years in prison

body: Any foreigner in India must produce a passport or other travel document within 24 hours when an officer asks. The demand may come from a Registration Officer, an Immigration Officer, a District Magistrate or a police officer of Head Constable rank or above. For sufficient cause the officer may extend the 24 hours to a maximum of seven days. A Registration Officer or Immigration Officer may also ask you to hand the passport over and come back for it later. When you hand it over, you are entitled to a receipt. The duty comes from rule 14 of the Immigration and Foreigners Rules, 2025.
title: A passport can be demanded from any foreigner, and you have a day to produce it

body: In India, no one may destroy, remove, injure, alter, deface, imperil or misuse a protected monument. A protected monument is one declared to be of national importance under the 1958 Act. Removing a sculpture, carving, image, bas-relief, inscription or similar object from such a monument is also an offence. Either act carries up to two years in prison, a fine of up to 100,000 rupees, or both. The basis is the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, section 30.
title: Damaging a protected monument in India: up to two years in prison

applies_when: you arrive in India by air and fill in the customs declaration card before the customs check.
body: The Indian arrival card asks whether you are bringing any of eleven kinds of thing, and a single yes sends you to the red channel. It asks about prohibited articles, jewellery above the free allowance and gold bullion. It asks about meat, dairy, fish and poultry products, and about seeds, plants, fruits, flowers and other planting material. It asks whether you carry a satellite phone, a drone, or a plasma, LCD or LED television. Imports that are prohibited outright include narcotics, wildlife products, counterfeit notes and maps drawing India's borders wrongly. You sign the card, so a wrong answer is a false declaration rather than an oversight.
title: Eleven questions on the arrival card, and one yes sends you to the red channel

body: If you entered on a visa of up to 180 days and want to stay longer, register before the 180 days run out. The 14 extra days that used to follow the 180 are gone, removed by the Immigration and Foreigners (Amendment) Rules, 2026. Registering late is now allowed only in emergent circumstances. An order you disagree with can be appealed online to the Commissioner of the Bureau of Immigration within 30 days. The Commissioner hears you and should decide within 60 days.
title: On a visa of up to 180 days, register before the 180 days run out to stay on

body: In an Indian wildlife sanctuary, no one may tease or molest any wild animal or litter the grounds. Without a permit from the Chief Wild Life Warden, no one may destroy, exploit or remove any wild life, including forest produce. Damaging the habitat of any wild animal is also forbidden, except under a permit granted by the Chief Wild Life Warden. In this Act, wild life includes any animal and any land or water vegetation that forms part of a habitat. Entering a sanctuary needs a permit, and tourism is one of the purposes it is granted for. Exempt are public servants on duty, authorised residents and people with rights over immovable property there. Their dependants and people passing through on a public highway are exempt too. The removal and habitat bans, the entry permit and the teasing and litter bans apply in national parks too. The general penalty is up to three years in prison, a fine of up to 100,000 rupees, or both. Offences involving a Schedule I animal or hunting in a sanctuary or park carry three to seven years and a fine. So do offences in the core area of a tiger reserve. The basis is the Wild Life (Protection) Act, as amended in 2022.
title: India's sanctuaries and national parks: teasing wild animals is a crime

body: India licenses the possession of any wireless transmitter, and a satellite phone is one. Without that licence, possession alone is an offence: up to three years in prison, a fine, or both. The licence comes from the telegraph authority, and a tourist will not hold one. A court may treat the device as yours if it is simply under your charge. On conviction the court also decides whether the device is confiscated. So leave the satellite phone at home.
title: A satellite phone needs a licence you will not have

body: The first rule is the familiar one: 182 days in the tax year and you are a resident. The second is not obvious. Sixty days in the current year is enough if over the four preceding years you spent 365 days or more in the country. So someone visiting for three months every year becomes a resident in the fifth year without noticing. For those earning more than 15 lakh rupees from Indian sources the second rule's threshold rises from 60 days to 120.
title: Sixty days can make you a resident if you have been here before

applies_when: you arrive from a country other than Nepal, Bhutan or Myanmar — for those three the allowances are different.
body: A tourist of foreign origin brings in used personal effects, travel souvenirs and articles worth up to 15,000 rupees free of duty. People living in India, foreigners among them, get 50,000 rupees instead. Above that, or with anything dutiable or prohibited, you take the red channel and fill in the customs declaration card. The green channel is only for a passenger carrying nothing dutiable and nothing prohibited. Some things stay outside the free allowance whatever they cost: firearms, gold and silver other than ornaments, and a television of any screen size.
title: A tourist gets 15,000 rupees duty-free, a resident 50,000

body: India banned electronic cigarettes outright in 2019, and the ban names import and transport alongside sale. A vape in your luggage is therefore an import. The Act makes it a cognizable offence, which in Indian law means the police may arrest without a warrant. A first offence carries up to one year in prison or a fine of up to one lakh rupees, or both. Merely storing the devices is a separate offence of up to six months. The Act sets no traveller's allowance and no exception for personal use.
title: A vape in your luggage is an import, and importing one is an arrestable offence

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. India itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. Transit here counts most strictly of all: a layover at an airport in an affected country counts regardless of duration, even an hour. India applies its own list of such countries, which does not match the WHO list. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

body: In Italy the person who buys a counterfeit is liable too, not only the seller. The fine for a final purchaser runs from 100 to 7,000 euros, and the item is confiscated in any case. It is enough that the quality, the price or the person selling it made it obvious the goods were fake. On the spot the case is usually settled by paying 200 euros, but a report is still filed. Buying it for yourself does not excuse you: it only makes the case administrative rather than criminal.
title: For a fake bag from a street stall the fine goes to the buyer

body: In Italy an object more than seventy years old whose author is no longer living counts as being of cultural interest. Taking one worth over 50,000 euro out of the country requires an export certificate, the attestato di libera circolazione. The item is presented to the export office, which decides within forty days, and the certificate is then valid for five years. For books the threshold is 13,500 euro, and for archaeological finds there is no threshold at all. Below the threshold no permit is needed. But you must prove to the export office that the item falls outside the permit rules, by a declaration under the law on official statements.
title: A painting or a chest over 70 years old: no certificate, no exit

applies_when: you stay in Italy for up to three months, and the deadline depends on whether you arrive from a Schengen country or from outside it.
body: Two duties, and the second is the one hosts do not know. Arriving from a Schengen country you must declare your presence within eight days to the questore of the province you are in. Arriving from outside, you declare at the border itself. Miss it without force majeure and the sanction is not a fine but expulsion — the same as for staying past three months. Separately, whoever gives you lodging, even a relative, must notify the local public security authority in writing within forty-eight hours. Failing that costs them 500 to 3,500 euro. A hotel does this for you; a friend with a spare room has to do it himself.
title: Missing the declaration of presence costs expulsion, not a fine

body: Since 2024 physical presence is a ground of its own. Spend the greater part of the tax period in the country and you are resident, which in an ordinary year means more than 183 days. The count is unforgiving, because any part of a day counts, so layovers and day trips pile up alongside nights spent there. The second test was redefined: domicile now rests only on personal and family ties, and business interests no longer count. Registration in the resident population register survives but as a presumption, which can be rebutted by proof to the contrary.
title: Part of a day counts as a whole one, so a layover counts too

body: The centres of many Italian cities are limited traffic zones, ZTL, and each town council draws its own. Driving into one when you are not allowed to is an administrative offence with a fine of 83 to 332 euros. Such a breach is rarely stopped on the spot, so the fine comes by post. For someone living abroad the authorities have up to 360 days from the day of the breach to serve it. It often arrives long after the trip.
title: A limited traffic zone costs 83 to 332 euros, and the fine can take a year

body: An adult may bring into Japan duty-free 3 bottles of alcoholic drinks of about 760 ml each. The tobacco allowance is 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars or 250 grams of other tobacco. With more than one kind, the total allowance is 250 grams. Perfume up to 2 ounces is also free, and other goods with a total overseas value under JPY 200,000.
title: Duty-free into Japan: 3 bottles of alcohol and 200 cigarettes per adult

body: In Japan you must carry your passport whenever you go out, or your residence card if you have one. This is an obligation under Japanese law. You must also show it when the police ask.
title: In Japan, carry your passport or residence card whenever you go out

body: Declare cash and other means of payment worth more than JPY 1 million when you enter or leave Japan. If you are leaving for North Korea, the threshold is JPY 100,000. This covers cash (including foreign currency), cheques, traveller's cheques, promissory notes and securities. Gold bullion of at least 90% purity over 1 kg is declared too. Ask a customs officer at the airport or seaport for the form.
title: Declare more than JPY 1 million in cash when entering or leaving Japan

body: If you bring medicine containing narcotics or stimulants' raw materials into Japan for your own treatment, you need a permit first. Examples are morphine, fentanyl, oxycodone, codeine, tapentadol, GHB, pseudoephedrine and Vyvanse (lisdexamfetamine). Apply to the Narcotics Control Department office covering your arrival airport at least 14 days before travel. Send the application form, a medical certificate from your prescribing doctor, and photos of the medicine's package. The certificate must give the specific reason you take the medicine and be issued within 3 months. Carry the medicine yourself: you cannot post it or have family carry it. Show the import certificate to Customs. If you will take leftover medicine out of Japan, file an export application too. Heroin, opium powder, methamphetamine, amphetamine and methaqualone cannot be brought in by any traveller, even if prescribed. That includes Adderall, whose active ingredient is amphetamine. Psychotropics such as methylphenidate, zolpidem, alprazolam and diazepam need no permit up to the amounts in the official table. Above those amounts, or for injections, you need a doctor's certificate.
title: Some medicines need a permit before you enter Japan; amphetamine is banned

body: Driving without a valid permit or licence is punishable by up to three years in prison or a fine of up to 500,000 yen. Japan accepts only an International Driving Permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention and in its format. A permit issued under the Vienna Convention is invalid here, even from a country that signed the Geneva one. Licences from Switzerland, Germany, France, Belgium, Monaco and Taiwan count instead, with a Japanese translation attached. The translation must come from the issuing authority, the country's embassy or consulate in Japan, the Japan Automobile Federation (JAF) or another body named by order. As a visitor you may drive for one year from the day you land, and a Geneva permit itself is valid for one year from issue. The basis is article 107-2 of the Road Traffic Act, and the penalty is in article 117-2-2.
title: Japan: drive on a 1949 Geneva permit or a translated licence from six countries

body: Every drone or model aircraft of 100 g or more that flies outdoors in Japan must be registered, and unregistered ones may not fly. Registration is done online on the DIPS 2.0 dashboard of Japan's transport ministry, with identity verified by passport. Flying an unregistered drone can bring a fine of up to JPY 500,000 or up to one year in prison.
title: Drones of 100 g or more must be registered to fly in Japan

body: Using a radio device without the Japanese technical conformity mark means operating an unlicensed radio station. That carries up to one year in prison or a fine of up to 1,000,000 yen under the Radio Act. US FRS and GMRS radios, Australian UHF CB and New Zealand PRS cannot be used in Japan at all. Visitors may use handheld devices they bring, such as Wi-Fi terminals, for 90 days from entry, but only if certain conditions are met. Among them, the device must meet standards the ministry recognises as equivalent to Japan's. Foreign-standard equipment sold by mail order or online often does not conform and may not be usable in Japan.
title: US FRS and GMRS radios cannot be used in Japan; foreign Wi-Fi gets 90 days

body: You are generally prohibited from bringing meat products into Japan, even small amounts. This covers ham, sausage, salami, bacon and jerky, vacuum-packed meat, and food with even a little meat, such as dumplings. Products with an inspection certificate for Japan from the exporting country's government may enter and are inspected on arrival. Duty-free purchases are no exception. Some canned meat products and, since July 2026, certain instant foods may be allowed if they meet the exclusion criteria. Canned, bottled or retort-pouch goods must also contain liquid, be airtight and keep unopened for at least 12 months at room temperature. If bringing in undeclared meat is deemed malicious, it can mean arrest and a fine up to JPY 3 million or up to three years' imprisonment.
title: Meat products, even sausage or jerky, are generally barred from Japan

body: You become a Japanese tax resident if you have a domicile (jusho) in Japan, or a residence (kyosho) there continuously for one year or more. Everyone else is a non-resident and is taxed only on income from Japanese sources. Among residents, a foreign national whose domicile or residence in Japan totals five years or less in the past ten is a non-permanent resident. A non-permanent resident pays tax on all income except foreign-source income, plus foreign-source income paid in Japan or remitted to Japan. Other residents are taxed on their whole income, wherever it arises. If you own a residence in Japan and leave intending a temporary absence, you are treated as residing here meanwhile. That intent is presumed if, for example, your family stays in your Japanese household or you keep a residence for your return.
title: A domicile in Japan or a year of residence makes you a Japanese tax resident

body: Since 1 April 2026, leaving 10,000 yen or more of hospital bills unpaid in Japan can bring strict screening at your next entry. This applies to foreign visitors who live abroad and are not in Japan's public health insurance. If the total unpaid at an insured hospital reaches 10,000 yen with no prospect of payment, the hospital is asked to report it. The health ministry passes the record to the immigration authorities, who use it in entry screening. The threshold was 200,000 yen and fell to 10,000 yen for bills arising from 1 April 2026. If you pay later but the hospital has not entered the payment in the system, the strict screening may still apply. Japan's official travel guide warns that non-payers may be denied entry, and strongly encourages private medical insurance.
title: Unpaid hospital balances of 10,000 yen or more can mean strict entry screening

body: The offence is not a passport left at the hotel but having no document that gives you the right to be here. That means a visa, registration, residence permit or work permit, expired ones included, and staying on after your time is up. The fine grows with the delay: 5,500 som in the first month, 10,000 up to three months, 15,000 up to six. Beyond that it is 17,500 up to a year and 20,000 after a year. Being here for a purpose other than the one you gave at the border, or breaking the transit rules, costs 10,000. Ignore an order to put it right for 30 days and a court orders expulsion. Miss the court's deadline to leave and you can be held in a centre for up to 30 days.
title: No document giving you the right to be here: a fine that grows every month

body: Kyrgyzstan bars a foreigner or a non-resident from taking more than 5000 dollars in cash out of the country. For residents and citizens the line is 10000 dollars, and above it they pay 10 per cent of the excess. The measure is called temporary and holds until the Cabinet decides otherwise; it has held since January 2023. Declaring the money does not lift it — the declaration and this ban are different things. Licensed banks and exchange offices are outside it, a traveller is not. So decide how you take money out before you bring it in.
title: A foreigner may take at most 5000 dollars in cash out of Kyrgyzstan

body: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs costs 800 calculation units — 80,000 som — and the right to drive goes for two years. Refusing the test is dearer still: 1,000 units, that is 100,000 som, and three years without the licence. The same applies to a person who had no right to drive in the first place. Letting a drunk person take the wheel, or handing your car to one, costs the owner 200 units, 20,000 som. If drink-driving causes damage or hurts somebody by negligence, it is 1,000 units and three years.
title: Drink-driving is 80,000 som and two years without a licence

body: Kyrgyzstan now has a regime of its own: an instruction on drone registration has been in force since February 2026. The threshold is not weight alone but the camera: a craft under 150 grams escapes registration only if it carries no video or photo device. From 151 grams to four kilograms you need registration and an operator certificate; heavier craft also need a remote pilot certificate and airworthiness papers. The application goes in within ten working days of import or purchase. A foreigner is not shut out: foreign natural and legal persons register a craft on temporary registration.
title: From February 2026 a drone is registered, and a visitor can do it

body: Making, buying, keeping, carrying or sending a narcotic or psychotropic substance without intent to sell is a criminal article once the amount is large. The penalty is a fine of 1000 to 2000 calculation indices, or up to 5 years. An especially large amount means 5 to 10 years, and a fine is no longer an alternative. What counts as large is set by a government list, not by the code itself. A smaller amount is punished too, under the Code of Offences rather than this article. A calculation index is 100 som, so the fine runs from 100,000 to 200,000 som.
title: A large amount of a drug means prison in Kyrgyzstan, even without dealing

body: Do not unlawfully make, buy, keep, transport or mail narcotic or psychotropic substances, or analogues of them, in a small amount without intent to sell. For an individual the penalty is a fine of 200 calculation indices or 40 hours of community work. A calculation index is the unit the Code uses to set fines. What counts as a small amount is set by a list that the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan approves. This article does not say what happens with larger amounts or with amounts meant for sale.
title: Unlawful possession of a small amount of drugs: fine or community work

body: An ordinary medicine needs no permit: for personal use the customs officer asks neither for registry information nor for a permit document. A medicine containing a narcotic or psychotropic substance needs no licence either, within the quantity the destination's own law sets. It has to be for personal use on medical grounds, with documents that name the medicine and the amount. Those documents must be in the language of the country you are entering, or carry a notarised translation. Such goods fall under the union's restrictions, so they are subject to declaration. The declaration is made on the passenger customs declaration form.
title: A narcotic medicine passes on documents, and it must be declared

body: Do not swear in public, pester people, relieve yourself in the street, damage small property or show aggression. This is petty hooliganism. The penalty is a fine of 55 calculation units, or 30 to 40 hours of community work, or arrest for three to five days. Do not drink alcohol on a street, at a stadium, in a park or on public transport. The same goes for any other public place. The penalty is 10 calculation units, or up to 20 hours of community work. Smoking where it is not allowed costs 30 calculation units. Breaking the rules on quiet in a town or public place costs an individual 100 calculation units. Dumping household rubbish outside the places set aside for it brings a warning or 55 calculation units. A repeat within a year after a penalty brings 20 to 30 hours of community work. The text does not say what one calculation unit is worth in som, so check the current value before you plan.
title: Public swearing, drinking, smoking, noise and littering carry fines

body: Citizens of countries on a Cabinet list are exempt from registration for a set term, so a shorter stay needs none. It is 30 calendar days for most, including Germany, France, Spain, Britain, the United States, Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus and Armenia. It is shorter for Iran (8), Turkmenistan (10), Azerbaijan (15), Dominica (21) and Barbados (28). It is 60 for Tajikistan, Serbia, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Indonesia, the Philippines, Chile and South Africa. It is 90 for Türkiye, Ukraine, Georgia, Greece, Peru, Venezuela, Nicaragua, El Salvador and the Bahamas. If you stay longer than your country's term, you must be registered at your place of stay by its last day. Your hotel, guest house or whoever puts you up must do it, at a registration office or online. An online filing can take three working days, so do not leave it to the last day. You need not go yourself, unless the system has no record of your border crossing. After the term, you are registered only once the police have recorded the offence, and told how to pay the fine and leave. Uzbek citizens on a private stay are registered for 60 days from entry and Moldovans for 90, and a longer stay needs a visa. The list gives no term for other countries.
title: Many passports get 30 days without registering; after that your host files it

body: Residency here follows from physical presence: 183 days or more in any twelve consecutive months ending in the current tax period. The window rolls, and the 31st of December resets nothing. Leaving does not always stop the count: days abroad for treatment, a business trip or study are counted by the code as days in Kyrgyzstan. What matters more than the count is how narrow the consequence is. If you are not a citizen and hold neither a residence permit nor kayrylman status, only income from a source inside Kyrgyzstan is taxed. Foreign income stays out of the base, and the rate is 10 per cent. A declaration is due if the income came from someone who does not act as a tax agent.
title: The 183 days are counted in a rolling window, but only Kyrgyz income is taxed

body: Declare everything you bring across the Kyrgyz customs border that must be declared, and give true details. Staying silent or giving false details about goods is an offence under Kyrgyzstan's Code of Offences, Article 372. The fine for a private person is 200 calculation indices. That is the most the code allows against a private person for most offences. Hiding goods from customs control, or showing customs invalid or false documents, carries the same fine. If you move goods across the border outside a checkpoint or outside customs working hours, the fine is 600 calculation indices instead. The goods you carried may also be seized.
title: Not declaring goods at the Kyrgyz border costs a fine of 200 calculation indices

body: Do not use or sell electronic cigarettes in Kyrgyzstan. Using an electronic cigarette carries a fine of 100 calculation indices for individuals. Selling electronic cigarettes carries a fine of 200 calculation indices for individuals. The fines for legal entities are higher and do not apply to a private traveller.
title: Using or selling electronic cigarettes is fined

body: Citizens of Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Russia may spend 90 days in total in each 180-day period without stay papers. Serbia, Türkiye, Ukraine, Mongolia and Moldova get the same 90 days out of 180. Citizens of the countries in the first annex to the regulation get 30 days in each 60-day period. That annex lists, among others, Britain, Germany, the United States, Canada, Japan and South Korea. Citizens of Uzbekistan get 60 days in each 120-day period. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain get 180 days in each 360-day period. A treaty Kyrgyzstan is party to can set a different period.
title: EAEU citizens: 90 days in 180; the US, Britain, Germany and others: 30 in 60

body: Kyrgyzstan has no winter tyre rule of its own, so the union's technical regulation applies. Winter tyres are required in December, January and February, and they go on every wheel. A winter tyre is one marked M+S or with the three-peak mountain and a snowflake inside it. It counts as unfit at 4 millimetres of tread, against 1.6 for an ordinary car tyre. Studded tyres may not be used in June, July and August, and when used they go on every wheel too. Regional authorities may lengthen those periods but not shorten them. Driving a car whose condition forbids its use costs 55 calculation units, that is 5,500 som.
title: Winter tyres from December to February, studs banned in summer

body: Foreigners who will stay in South Korea for more than 90 days, for example to work or study, must apply for an Alien Registration Card (ARC). Register within 90 days of your arrival, at the immigration office or branch office responsible for your area. Holders of A-1, A-2 and A-3 visas are exempt. When you leave Korea for good, return the card to the immigration officer at the departure airport or port. Failing to return it results in a fine.
title: South Korea: stays over 90 days need an Alien Registration Card within 90 days

body: Report to customs if you bring into South Korea more than USD 10,000 or the equivalent in total in foreign currency, Korean won notes or cheques. Mark "yes" at item 3 of the Traveler Declaration Form and write the amount. Hand the form to a customs officer and take the Certificate of Foreign Currency Declaration. It cannot be issued once you have left immigration. A non-resident who takes out foreign means of payment within the amount brought in on the latest arrival need not report them again. They must hold the certificate of declaration. Moving cash or cheques across the border without a report risks up to a year in prison or a fine of up to 100 million won. If three times the amount involved exceeds 100 million won, the fine can reach three times that amount.
title: South Korea: declare over USD 10,000 in cash and cheques on arrival

body: You may bring goods with a total taxable value of up to USD 800 into South Korea free of duty. Farm, livestock and fishery products count only up to 5 kg of each, 40 kg in all and 100,000 won in total price. Apart from that you may bring 200 cigarettes and 100 ml of perfume. Travellers under 19, counted by year of birth, get no exemption for liquor and cigarettes. If you declare goods above the allowance yourself, the standard duty is cut by 30%. If customs finds them undeclared, you pay 40% on top of the regular tax, or 60% if it happens twice or more within two years.
title: South Korea: declare goods over USD 800 in total, or pay 40% extra if found

body: The K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) is the electronic travel permit for people who can enter Korea without a visa. Apply only on the official website www.k-eta.go.kr or in the K-ETA mobile app. The fee is KRW 10,000, about 7 to 8 US dollars. Review generally takes within 72 hours. Do not use agency or express-service sites that charge high fees. The Ministry of Justice warns that they are imitation or phishing sites. The text does not say what happens at the border if you arrive without a K-ETA. It also lists a temporary exemption from K-ETA. It also lists a FAQ on who is exempt, but gives no details here. Check the official notice before you go.
title: K-ETA travel authorisation: apply only on the official site or app

body: Get a permit from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety before you enter Korea with medicine that contains controlled substances. Controlled substances here means narcotic drugs or psychoactive substances. This covers medicine you carry for your own treatment. It applies to everyone, Korean or foreign. You can apply online starting December 27, 2024. The Ministry's attached guideline file explains how to apply. The text does not say what happens if you arrive without a permit.
title: Bringing narcotic or psychoactive medicine into Korea needs a Ministry permit

body: All of Seoul is a drone flight restricted zone, and Seoul and the capital region are prohibited and restricted airspace. To fly a drone in Seoul you need prior flight approval, obtained 3 to 5 days before the flight. Airspace checks and flight approval are handled by the Drone One-Stop service (drone.onestop.go.kr). If an unapproved flight is caught, it is punished: a fine of up to 5 million won under article 161 of the Aviation Safety Act. A conviction is entered in the police and prosecution criminal records.
title: South Korea: flying a drone in Seoul needs approval 3 to 5 days ahead

body: The administrative offences code has a separate offence: activity that does not match the purposes stated in the visa. Working without a qualification certificate or a work permit, where such a document is required, falls under the same paragraph. The penalty is harsher than for overstaying: 25 MRP, or administrative arrest of up to ten days, or expulsion from the country. At the 2026 rate that is about 108 thousand tenge. A repeat within a year of being penalised leaves one outcome: arrest of up to fifteen days together with expulsion. Note that the offence speaks of activity not matching the visa's purpose, not only of an employment contract.
title: Doing something other than your visa says is punished harder than overstaying

body: A participant who breaks the rules of a peaceful assembly in Kazakhstan faces a warning, twenty monthly indices or up to ten days of arrest. Twenty indices is 86,500 tenge. An organiser pays thirty indices, and a repeat within a year raises it to fifty indices or fifteen days. Disobeying the lawful demand of a person keeping public order is a separate offence at five indices. A repeat of that brings ten indices, community work or up to five days of arrest.
title: Standing in someone else's protest can cost ten days

body: Kazakhstan keeps a border zone with a regime of its own, and moving through it without identity documents is an offence. For a person it costs five monthly indices — 21,625 tenge. Changing your route while crossing the zone on the way to a border post is punished the same way. Activities, filming events or any organised undertaking inside the zone need notice to the Border Service first. The monthly index is 4,325 tenge from 1 January 2026.
title: The border strip has its own regime, and papers are checked inside it

body: You may not take more than the equivalent of $10,000 in foreign cash and foreign-currency instruments out of Kazakhstan. Presidential decree No 830 of 14 March 2022 sets this as an outright ban. The sum is converted at the National Bank's official rate on the day you take it out. The limit applies to each person, children included. Declaring the excess does not make it allowed. Cash that must be declared but is not, or is declared wrongly, brings a fine of 25% of that sum and its confiscation.
title: Kazakhstan bans taking out more than $10,000 in foreign cash

body: If you, or an organisation you head, owe 40 monthly calculation indices or more under an enforcement document, the bailiff must bar you from leaving Kazakhstan. Falling more than three months behind on periodic payments under such a document does the same. The ban takes effect five working days after you are duly notified, and a court must sanction it. It is then sent to the Border Service of the National Security Committee to enforce. It can be suspended if you need medical treatment abroad. It is lifted within one working day once the case is closed, periodic arrears are cleared, or the creditor asks, unless the creditor is the state.
title: A debt of 40 monthly indices or more can stop you leaving Kazakhstan

body: A phone runs on a Kazakh SIM only while its factory code sits in the state database. The operator is forbidden to serve a device that is absent from it, or whose code does not match. To register one you give the operator your Kazakh personal number, the device code and the subscriber number. Registration costs nothing, but a visitor without that personal number simply cannot finish it. An individual may verify no more than two imported devices in a calendar year. If the same code is already registered to somebody else, registration is refused outright.
title: A phone works on a local SIM only if its code is in the state database

body: Kazakhstan answers drink-driving with arrest, not a fine: fifteen days and the right to drive taken for seven years. Handing the wheel to a drunk person carries exactly the same. If it hurts somebody or damages vehicles, roads or other property, it becomes twenty days and still seven years. A repeat within a year of the last penalty ending is twenty days and eight years. A driver who had no licence in the first place gets twenty days of arrest.
title: Drink-driving here is fifteen days locked up and seven years without a licence

body: Driving in Kazakhstan without your licence or the vehicle's papers on you brings a warning or five monthly indices. A foreign licence left behind counts here, because the exemption covers only documents issued in Kazakhstan when you carry your ID. Driving with no right to drive, or without the right for that category, costs twenty indices — 86,500 tenge. Driving while disqualified costs fifty indices or ten days of arrest. Repeats push those to thirty and seventy indices. One monthly index is 4,325 tenge from 1 January 2026.
title: Papers left in the hotel are a warning; no licence at all is 86,500 tenge

body: Bringing a drone in is not banned, but registering it is compulsory. The threshold is not only about weight: registration covers craft from 0.25 kg and, on top of that, every system carrying data-collection equipment. A camera therefore puts any drone on the register whatever it weighs. The application goes through the e-licensing portal and must be signed with a Kazakh digital signature, which a foreigner cannot obtain without a local tax number. The service is free and takes 10 working days. A foreigner needs a notarised purchase contract with an official translation, and a certificate of removal from any foreign register the drone was on. Flying unregistered draws a fine from 40 MCI, and flying over protected sites without clearance risks confiscation.
title: A drone with a camera is registered whatever it weighs

body: Kazakhstan punishes non-medical use of narcotics, psychotropics, their analogues and potent substances on its own. Where it is not a criminal matter, it costs forty monthly indices — 173,000 tenge — or ten days of arrest. A repeat within a year doubles both: eighty indices, or twenty days. The article was added to the code in 2025, so older advice does not mention it. One monthly index is 4,325 tenge from 1 January 2026.
title: Taking a drug without a prescription is 173,000 tenge or ten days

body: Keep the goods you bring in for personal use within the duty-free limits. By air, the limit is goods worth up to 10,000 euros and weighing up to 50 kg. By other transport and on foot, it is goods worth up to 500 euros and weighing up to 25 kg. If you go over, you pay customs duties of 30% of the value, but not less than 4 euros per kilogram. The duty is charged only on the part above the value limit, the weight limit, or both. The text applies these limits to individuals crossing the customs border of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU).
title: Duty-free limit on goods: 10,000 euros by air, 500 euros otherwise

body: An ordinary medicine needs no permit: for personal use the customs officer asks neither for registry information nor for a permit document. A medicine containing a narcotic or psychotropic substance needs no licence either, within the quantity the destination's own law sets. It has to be for personal use on medical grounds, with documents that name the medicine and the amount. Those documents must be in the language of the country you are entering, or carry a notarised translation. Such goods fall under the union's restrictions, so they are subject to declaration. The declaration is made on the passenger customs declaration form.
title: A narcotic medicine passes on documents, and it must be declared

body: Apply for the QazETA electronic entry permit online at qazeta.kz at least 72 hours before your planned entry date. Show at the border the same passport you gave in the application. The permit is free (0 tenge) and valid for 180 calendar days. Until 30 June 2027 the permit is only recommended: arriving without one does not lead to refusal of entry, and border officers explain the rules. From 1 July 2027 it is mandatory, and arriving without it is an official ground for refusal of entry. The rollout starts on 1 November 2026 at Aktau international airport and the Urlitobe, Aukhatty, Atameken and Nurly Zhol road checkpoints. It reaches Astana and Almaty airports on 1 January 2027 and all other checkpoints on 1 March 2027. The requirement applies to citizens of the 85 states that have visa-free travel with Kazakhstan. Having the permit does not remove the border service's right to refuse entry on other grounds under article 48 of the Law on Population Migration. With supporting documents you are exempt if you are under 16 or over 65, or hold a valid Kazakh visa, temporary residence permit or residence permit. With supporting documents, airside transit passengers who do not cross the border are exempt, as are crews, diplomats and other listed categories. The allowed length of stay is set by migration law, not by the permit.
title: Electronic entry permit QazETA for visa-exempt travel to Kazakhstan

body: The penalty rises in steps, counted in monthly calculation units of 4,325 tenge each. Staying past your time by up to three days brings a warning. More than three and up to five brings a fine of 10 units. More than five and up to ten brings 15. Beyond ten days a different paragraph applies: evading departure costs 25 units or administrative expulsion from the country. Breaking the transit rules is its own offence at 15 units or expulsion. Expulsion is the part that outlasts the fine — it closes the door for years, and the fine does not.
title: Overstaying is charged by the day, and the eleventh day changes everything

body: Stop when police lawfully signal you to do so, and take any required alcohol or drug test. If you do not stop, you face a fine of forty monthly indices (173,000 tenge) or up to three days of arrest. A repeat within a year brings a one-year driving ban and five days of arrest. If you drive with no right to drive and refuse to stop, you face sixty indices or up to fifteen days of arrest. Refusing a sobriety test brings fifteen days of arrest and eight years without the right to drive. Repeating that refusal brings twenty days of arrest and nine years without driving, which is more than drink-driving carries.
title: Refusing a sobriety test costs eight years without a driving licence

body: Swearing in public, pestering people or any similar disrespect is petty hooliganism in Kazakhstan. It costs twenty monthly indices — 86,500 tenge — or community work, or five to fifteen days of arrest. Drinking alcohol on the street or in another public place costs five indices, 21,625 tenge. Being drunk in public in a way that offends human dignity is punished by the same article. A repeat within a year doubles the fine and can bring five days of arrest. One monthly index is 4,325 tenge from 1 January 2026.
title: Swearing in public costs 86,500 tenge, drinking alcohol in public 21,625

body: For citizens of visa-free countries registration is mandatory if the stay exceeds 30 days — it must be completed no later than day 30 after entry. Short trips need no registration, which is exactly why the duty is easy to forget once you linger. Electronic accounting runs on a 3-working-day deadline, and breach falls under article 518 of the Administrative Code.
title: Registration for stays longer than 30 days

body: Kazakhstan treats cigarettes, heated tobacco, shisha, heating devices and electronic systems with their liquids as one thing. Using any of them where the law forbids it costs fifteen monthly indices — 64,875 tenge. Doing it on board an aircraft costs fifty indices, which is 216,250 tenge. The monthly index is 4,325 tenge from 1 January 2026. So a vape is not a way around the smoking ban here: the article names it in the same breath as a cigarette.
title: Smoking where it is banned is 64,875 tenge, and on a plane four times that

body: The first test is the usual one: 183 calendar days or more within any 12 consecutive months. The second applies when there are fewer days: the centre of vital interests under article 222 of the Tax Code. It is met when three conditions hold together. First, citizenship, a residence permit or a residence card. Second, a spouse or close relatives living here. Third, housing available to live in at any time. So a flat you bought and a family that moved make you a resident even on short visits.
title: You can be resident without 183 days, through your centre of vital interests

body: The EAEU technical regulation bans operating cars and light trucks without winter tyres in December, January and February. Studded tyres are banned in June, July and August. Winter tyres go on all wheels. The same clause carries a caveat that usually goes unmentioned: a member state may set its own period on climatic grounds. Belarus has done so, and its season runs to 1 March. So when you cross between union countries, check the dates again rather than relying on the union-wide ones.
title: Winter tyres in winter, no studs in summer — but the dates differ by country

body: Driving onto the oncoming side where the rules forbid it takes the right to drive for six months. A turn or a U-turn made that way counts the same. Only those whom the code exempts from losing the right pay instead: thirty monthly indices. Driving along a pavement, a footpath or the verge costs fifteen indices — 64,875 tenge. Breaking the rules on where the vehicle belongs on the road, on passing oncoming traffic or on overtaking costs the same fifteen. A repeat within a year doubles that to thirty indices.
title: Crossing into oncoming traffic costs the licence, not money

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: Carry a yellow fever vaccination certificate if you come to Kazakhstan from a risk country. The World Health Organization (WHO) lists which countries count as at risk of yellow fever. The list marks this as a requirement for travellers arriving from those countries, not from any country. It also covers travellers who passed through the airport of such a country, however short the stop. The list does not say what happens if you have no certificate. A certificate that is valid cannot be rejected because more than 10 years have passed since the vaccination. Boosters or revaccination cannot be required. The list gives no age limit for Kazakhstan. It warns that country requirements can change at any time, so check with the Kazakh consulate or embassy before you travel.
title: Kazakhstan asks for a yellow fever certificate if you arrive from a risk country

body: Tourists may bring personal clothing and other essentials, two regular-size bottles of wine and one and a half liters of spirits. Toilet water is allowed up to a quarter liter. A small quantity of perfume and souvenirs is also allowed. Their value must not exceed US $250, and they must not be meant for commercial purpose. Tourist baggage does not cover goods in commercial quantities, goods imported for sale or exchange, or goods to be given as a gift to anyone else. It also does not cover goods owned by anyone other than you or a family member travelling with you. Foreign currencies, gold jewelleries and gems must be declared to the Customs Arrival No 1 Officer. Goods worth more than your allowance are taxed at the normal import duty rates. If you knowingly make a false or inaccurate declaration, you lose any exemptions and can be dealt with under the Customs Ordinance.
title: Tourists to Sri Lanka: duty-free limits on alcohol, perfume and souvenirs

body: There is no cap on how much foreign currency you carry, but above $15,000 or the equivalent it must be declared to customs. The way back has its own threshold: taking out more than $10,000 in notes must be declared too. Local rupees have a hard limit in both directions — no more than 20,000.
title: Declare currency above $15,000, and you may carry only 20,000 rupees

body: If you bring a drone into Sri Lanka as a visiting tourist for temporary use, you do not follow the import process meant for permanent imports. Instead, submit a request for flying approval through the online portal of the Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL). The official CAASL page names no penalty for flying without approval. Separately, drones in mass categories A, B and C may not be flown without valid insurance covering injury to third parties and/or damage. That insurance is not required for a drone of 0.25 kg or below. For a drone above 0.25 kg and up to 0.9 kg, the minimum third-party cover is 100,000 Sri Lankan rupees. For a drone above 0.9 kg and up to 4 kg, it is 400,000 rupees.
title: Tourists flying a drone in Sri Lanka request approval on the CAASL portal

body: The motor traffic department's circular sets out two routes. Exchanging your own licence needs a visa of at least a year, so a tourist is left with the temporary licence under section 132. It is issued for five months or the rest of your visa, whichever is shorter, and the fee is counted by the month. The convention requirement applies to the exchange only; for the temporary licence yours must be a full one, not learner, probationary or temporary. Only the motorcycle and light vehicle classes are recognised, and your licence must stay valid for at least another year. Every endorsement carries over: if yours says automatic only, so will the new one. The commissioner may ask your embassy to confirm the licence is genuine.
title: A local licence is needed, and a tourist cannot exchange their own

body: In Sri Lanka, entering and remaining in a national park without a permit, or breaking the permit's conditions, is an offence. If a wildlife ranger or senior officer detects it and you admit it, you may pay a prescribed sum instead of being prosecuted. In a national reserve, no one may put poison, waste, garbage or other polluting material into its waters. Nor may anyone do anything that may pollute the waters or harm its wildlife, plants or ecosystem. Diving or using a boat there needs a permit from the prescribed officer, issued for a fee. Breaking these bans carries a fine of 20,000 to 100,000 rupees, two to five years in prison, or both. A second or later conviction for the same offence brings a fine of 40,000 to 200,000 rupees, five to ten years, or both. A person may be granted permission to enter or remain in a national park, nature reserve, marine national park or a sanctuary on State land. If they cause a nuisance or disturbance there, they may be refused entry, ordered to leave or removed at once. The basis is the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance as amended by Act No. 22 of 2009.
title: Polluting or unpermitted diving in Sri Lankan reserves: a fine or 2 to 5 years

body: A personal supply of ordinary medicines is allowed without prior approval. The quantity is measured by the length of your stay or by 90 days, whichever is less. Controlled and psychotropic medicines — strong opioids, codeine products, ADHD stimulants — are regulated by the national medicines authority and require clearance before arrival. Carry the medicines in original packaging with a prescription or doctor's letter. Customs may demand proof of prescription, especially for painkillers and antidepressants.
title: Ordinary medicines need no clearance; controlled ones need it in advance

body: Pay the applicable visa fee at the port of departure if your Sri Lankan visa expires. You can leave without paying a penalty if you depart within 7 days of expiry. Overstaying more than 7 days up to 14 days incurs a penalty of USD 250 in addition to the visa fee. Overstaying more than 14 days incurs a penalty of USD 500 on top of the visa fee.
title: Sri Lanka visa overstay fees and 7-day grace period

body: Four grounds make you resident and any one of them is enough. The main one is 183 days or more in aggregate within any twelve months that begin or end during the year of assessment. A stay split across two years is therefore still caught. Simply residing in Sri Lanka is a separate ground, with no day count at all. If only the day count made you resident, residence starts back at the beginning of that 183-day window. In every other case it covers the whole year. Leaving is expensive: on ceasing to be resident a person is treated as having sold everything they own at market value at that moment.
title: 183 days in any 12 months, and living here makes you resident anyway

body: The regulations forbid manufacturing, importing, selling and offering for sale the products in their schedules. Bringing a device in for yourself is importing, so a traveller is squarely inside the ban. Two schedules matter; one covers any smokeless tobacco product, which catches snus and chewing tobacco. The other covers a flavoured or sweetened cigarette and an electronic cigarette that contains tobacco. Read the last words carefully: on the face of the text the device must contain tobacco, and most modern vapes hold nicotine liquid instead. In practice the rule is reported as applied to the whole category, and customs at Colombo take vapes off arriving passengers. So a nicotine-only device is a bet rather than an exemption.
title: Smokeless tobacco and tobacco vapes are banned; bringing one in is importing

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. Sri Lanka itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. Transit counts too: a layover of more than 12 hours at an airport in an affected country is treated as arriving from there. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

body: Importing a drone or model aircraft needs an import licence from the department in charge of Foreign Trade. This covers any unmanned flying machine with a motor and remote control, and it applies even if the machine is a gift. Bringing one in temporarily is a separate route and needs a special authorisation instead. For that, send customs a request at least 8 days before you arrive in Morocco.
