The request must give the importer's name, first name and passport number, the company name of the importing company, and how long the machine will stay. It must also identify the machine, with a description, photos, catalogues or a data sheet, and state the intended use. Add the entry and exit dates and the offices of import and re-export. Finally, list the sites where you will fly it, with their Lambert coordinates. A false declaration or no declaration means the machine is confiscated and you pay penalties. Customs then give you a receipt and/or a customs report.
title: Bringing a drone into Morocco needs an import licence or special authorisation

body: Importing and exporting dirhams is prohibited. Travellers may still carry up to 2,000 dirhams in banknotes in or out. A foreign non-resident can change leftover dirhams back with the original currency import declaration made on entry. It must come with the original exchange slips made out in their name. Without that declaration, banks and exchange offices can change back at most 20,000 dirhams, against an exchange slip in their name less than six months old. Banks and exchange offices at ports and airports can do this on a boarding pass for abroad, up to 2,000 dirhams per passport.
title: Morocco: dirhams may not be taken in or out beyond 2,000 in banknotes

body: Visitors may bring foreign banknotes and bearer instruments into Morocco freely. From the equivalent of 100,000 dirhams they must be declared at the customs check on arrival. No declaration is accepted afterwards. Keep it: it proves the origin of the currency, notably when you leave, and is valid for one stay of up to 6 months. Below 100,000 dirhams the declaration is optional; it can show where the currency came from when you leave. On leaving, a non-resident declares and justifies the origin of currency worth 100,000 dirhams or more. Smaller amounts are also declared, and customs may ask where they came from in some cases.
title: Morocco: declare foreign currency worth 100,000 dirhams or more on arrival

body: A traveller carrying 10,000 euros or more in cash must declare it to customs. Failing to declare is an offence, and the money is seized pending the case. All the cash counts together, whatever the currency.
title: Undeclared 10,000 euros are seized at the border

body: Flights are governed by the civil aviation agency under the 2023 rulebook. Two control zones matter for a traveller: those around Podgorica and Tivat airports. Inside the areas the agency has drawn, roughly four kilometres across, flying is not allowed at all. Only the Airspace Management Cell can clear it, and it publishes a NOTAM when it does. Elsewhere in those zones you may go no higher than 50 metres without clearance. Going from 50 to 120 metres needs separate approval from the same cell. The Tivat zone covers the Bay of Kotor — the most photographed place in the country.
title: Above 50 metres over the Bay of Kotor only with clearance

body: A drone does not fly over a Montenegrin national park on a whim: three permissions come first. The environment agency allows the activity inside the protected area, and the request names the place, the purpose and how long it lasts. The civil aviation agency allows the flight itself whenever the drone weighs more than 249 grams. The national parks enterprise has to approve it too, and every paper collected goes to them. Filming a feature or commercial film costs 200 euros a day, and a video clip or advert 400.
title: Over a national park a drone needs three permissions, not one

body: Montenegro names what proves a foreigner's identity, and a driving licence is not on the list. Only a foreign travel document, a valid identity card issued by another state, or a Montenegrin residence permit will do. You must carry one of them and show it when an authorised officer asks. Not having it is an administrative offence and the fine runs from 200 to 1,200 euros.
title: A driving licence will not do as your identity here

body: If you need a visa for Montenegro, a short stay visa (type C) covers tourist, business or personal trips. Your stay may not exceed 90 days in the period of 6 months, counted from your first entry. This holds whether the stay is continuous or added up over several visits. Holding a visa does not by itself let you in. You must also meet the other entry and stay requirements of the Law on Foreigners. At the border the police may shorten your visa in three cases. These are: you lack enough money for your stay, the visa runs longer than your passport is valid, or you would go over the 90-day limit. A visa application can be refused if you have no proof of health and travel insurance. It can also be refused if you have already stayed 90 days within 180 days of first entry. A visa does not allow you to work. For that you need a temporary residence permit for employment or seasonal work, based on a work permit issued beforehand. When applying, your passport must stay valid for three months longer than the visa.
title: Montenegro short-stay visa: 90 days in 6 months, and it does not guarantee entry

body: You may carry a reasonable personal supply of medicines, but no more than six months' worth. For a medicine containing a narcotic substance the limit is tighter: no more than 30 days' worth, and a certificate from your chosen doctor is mandatory. The certificate must be no older than 90 days. Missing paperwork counts as an offence, not a misunderstanding.
title: A narcotic medicine: 30 days' worth and a certificate

body: Every foreign visitor must be registered at their place of stay. A hotel, hostel or licensed campsite registers you within 12 hours of check-in. A private host must also register you within 12 hours. If no host does it, register yourself within 24 hours at a tourist information centre or a police station. Registering at the tourist office is free. If you move to another town for more than 24 hours, register again there. If registration is missing, it may come up when you leave the country, and a fine of €60 to €600 per person is possible. Paying within 8 days cuts the fine by one third. Non-registration alone does not bring an entry ban. Fines are paid at a post office or bank, not to the officer. Keep your confirmation, the so-called white card, until you leave.
title: Register your stay within 24 hours; missing it can cost €60 to €600

body: Staying 183 days or more in a calendar year makes you a Montenegrin tax resident. Residency can also arise from the centre-of-vital-interests test, even with fewer days. Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Rates are progressive and low (0% up to EUR 700 a month, 9% on 701–1,000), but the duty to declare arises regardless of the amount.
title: 183 days and you're a Montenegrin tax resident

body: Montenegro exempts goods in a traveller's personal luggage from customs duty and VAT. Arriving by air or sea the limit is 430 euros; arriving by road it is 300 euros. For a traveller under 15 the limit is 150 euros whatever the mode of arrival.
title: 430 euros by air, 300 by land, 150 for a child

body: The period is one, 15 November to 1 April, and winter conditions mean snowfall or snow, ice or black ice on the road. First of three requirements: in winter conditions vehicles of categories M and N need winter tyres on all wheels. This carries the heaviest charge: 300 to 1,000 euros for the driver, or detention of up to 60 days. Second: tread depth in that period must be at least 4 millimetres, or the fine is 120 to 400 euros. Third: on roads and sections covered by the special order, winter equipment is required whatever the weather, and that carries 80 to 250 euros. If a section is not covered by the order and there are no winter conditions, winter tyres are not needed. Studded tyres are prohibited outright, and buses and medium and heavy goods vehicles also need a shovel.
title: Winter tyres: three separate penalties, the heaviest up to 60 days' detention

body: The penal code's offence of drinking alcohol opens with the words «a Maldivian citizen», alongside not fasting in Ramadan and eating pork. The next provision is addressed to anyone. Producing, trading in or distributing alcohol as a business or by importing is an offence in its own right. So a visitor's exposure does not run through the drinking offence: it runs through the import ban and through what happens at the border and afterwards. The British foreign office reports arrest and deportation for possessing or drinking alcohol, or for being drunk, outside resorts and on inhabited islands. That is practice rather than the code. Publicly observing a religion other than Islam, same-sex relations and drugs are reported by the same advisory.
title: A visitor is punished for bringing in or trading alcohol, not for drinking

body: Do not bring liquor or alcoholic products into the Maldives without prior approval. The permit must come from the Ministry of Economic Development. Alcohol bought on the flight or in a duty-free shop on the way is not exempt, and customs advises against buying it. If you arrive with it, it will be confiscated at the airport. Alcohol is sold at tourist resorts and hotels, which imported it under a special licence issued before importation. The page gives no fine or prison term for travellers.
title: Alcohol brought into the Maldives without a permit is confiscated at the airport

body: Anyone arriving or leaving with cash or bearer negotiable instruments above a threshold must report the amount to Maldives Customs. Customs passes it on to the financial intelligence unit. The Act does not name the threshold — the Monetary Authority sets it. It stands at 10,000 US dollars, or the same in any currency. Where the sum went unreported and money laundering or terrorist financing is suspected, Customs may detain the whole of it and search you and your belongings. The same applies where the report carried false information. You are also bound by law to say where the money came from when asked.
title: A wrong figure on the form costs you the whole sum, not the difference

body: Bringing a Schedule 2 substance into the Maldives is an offence unless you hold the Ministry's written permission. You must also follow the regulation made under the Drugs Act. Schedule 2 is the statute's own list of narcotic substances used as medicine. It follows the schedules of the 1961, 1971 and 1988 United Nations drug conventions. The penalty on the face of the statute is 10 to 15 years in prison together with a fine of 50,000 to 1,000,000 rufiyaa. Attempting it, or helping someone else do it, carries 7 to 11 years. The terms on which a traveller may carry their own prescription sit in that ministry regulation, so arrange the permission before flying.
title: A controlled medicine without written permission is a prison matter

body: Maldives customs puts it plainly: the import of dogs and dangerous animals is strictly prohibited. There is no permit and no exception to ask for, so planning the trip with a dog is pointless. Another pet needs a health certificate from an authorised vet. The certificate must say the animal is free from infections and contagious diseases. Carry it with you: the leaflet lists pets among the goods that need a permit to import.
title: Dogs are not let into the Maldives at all

body: The civil aviation authority reviews drone flights case by case; no blanket permission exists. The procedure has three steps. First, clearance from the military: depending on the area you must apply to the Maldives National Defence Force. Then an application to the authority itself, which must carry the defence permit you obtained. The third step is left to you: clearing the flight with the resort, the island or city council, the airports company and anyone else it touches. The ceiling is 400 feet. The strictness comes from seaplanes, which land on the water between the atolls, and from the ocean being 99 per cent of the country.
title: Three separate approvals, and every flight is reviewed on its own

body: You get a tourist visa on arrival in the Maldives and do not need to apply in advance. Submit the free online Traveller Declaration on the IMUGA portal up to 96 hours (4 days) before you arrive, and show it to immigration. Every traveller, including children, needs their own declaration. Your passport must have a machine-readable zone and at least 1 month's validity, and children need their own passport. Passengers with an extended validity in their passports are not allowed to enter. Bring a full itinerary with confirmed return tickets, a prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility, and enough money for your stay. A sponsorship approved by Maldives Immigration can replace these. You must also meet the entry requirements of your next destination. Show a valid Yellow Fever Vaccination Certificate if you arrive from, or recently passed through, a country with Yellow Fever risk. Children under one year are exempt. A complete itinerary does not guarantee entry, because immigration officers decide admissibility at the port of entry. Israeli passports are not accepted for entry from 15 April 2025.
title: Maldives: visa on arrival, but submit a Traveller Declaration first

body: The General Fisheries Regulation of 2020 prohibits exporting corals and sea anemones, in a living state and a dead one alike. The same list holds trochus shells, big spider conches, oysters, lobster, eel and octopus. A separate list of protected species forbids even taking them from the sea: all corals, black coral, sea turtles and their eggs, and the triton conch. A fragment of coral picked up on the beach breaches both bans at once. Attempting to export draws a fine from 5,000 to 400,000 rufiyaa, calculated at twice the market price. There is one exception: a special ministry permit for species raised by aquaculture. A souvenir bought on the island does not qualify.
title: A shell or a piece of coral may not leave the country

body: Do not bring narcotics or psychotropic substances, pornographic material, religious materials offensive to Islam, live pigs or idols for worship into the Maldives. Maldives Customs lists them as prohibited goods, meaning goods that are banned completely. Pornographic material includes sex toys, books, magazines, films, videos, DVDs and software. This page does not state a penalty for these items, so check the law before you pack anything close to these categories. Other goods are restricted rather than banned and need a permit or prescription. Alcohol and pork need prior approval, and alcohol bought on the flight or in duty free shops will be confiscated on arrival. Controlled drugs for personal use need a valid prescription.
title: Narcotics, pornography, idols and live pigs are banned from import

body: You are resident once you are present for 183 days or more in any twelve-month period. Merely intending to be present counts too, before the days do. A permanent place of living in the Maldives makes you resident on its own. Residence by itself does not reach your foreign income, though. A foreigner staying on an immigration permit and not married to a Maldivian is only temporarily resident. A temporary resident is taxed on Maldivian income alone. Marry a Maldivian and that shelter falls away: the worldwide total applies.
title: Marrying a Maldivian brings your foreign income into tax

body: Do not bring electronic cigarettes, vaping devices or products made for use with them into the Maldives. Do not sell, hand out or use them there either. A vape in your bag is a banned item, not a customs formality. The President's Office says fines have been established for violations, but the text does not give the amounts. The import ban on vape products applies from 15 November 2024, according to a news report. The provisions on vaping devices in the amendment (Section 10-2) took effect on 15 December 2024. The same amendment tightens tobacco rules. No tobacco product may be sold to anyone under 21. Tobacco use is banned in all government institution buildings and their premises. Leave the device at home.
title: Vapes are banned in the Maldives: import, sale, giving away and use

body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. The Maldives itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. Transit counts too: a layover of more than 12 hours at an airport in an affected country is treated as arriving from there. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

body: Passengers over 18 may bring into Mexico up to 10 packs of cigarettes, 25 cigars or 200 grams of tobacco. They may also bring up to three litres of alcoholic drinks and six litres of wine. Alcoholic drinks and manufactured tobacco cannot be brought in as part of the duty-free allowance for other goods.
title: Duty-free in Mexico: 10 packs of cigarettes, 3 litres of alcohol, 6 of wine

body: Bring a foreign car into Mexico as a visitor and you need a Banjercito temporary import permit and a deposit you lose if it overstays. A visitor applies to Banjercito with a valid passport and the official immigration document, and may bring in one vehicle. The permit is paid in pesos: the equivalent of USD 51 plus VAT at the border or at a Mexican consulate in the US. Online, 10–60 days before entry, it is the equivalent of USD 45 plus VAT. The deposit is USD 400 for a 2007 or newer model, 300 for 2001–2006 and 200 for older ones. For a visitor the permit lasts as long as the authorised stay, including continuous renewals. To get the deposit back, present the car at a Banjercito border office when you leave.
title: Temporary import of a foreign car into Mexico: permit plus deposit up to USD 400

body: Declare cash and similar funds worth more than USD 10,000 when you enter or leave Mexico. Cash, cheques, payment orders and other documents for collection count together. Carrying such a sum is not a crime, but failing to declare it is. The fine is 20% to 40% of the amount above USD 10,000. If more than USD 30,000 goes undeclared, the penalty is 3 months to 6 years in prison. The excess then becomes property of the Federal Treasury unless its lawful origin is proven.
title: Declare more than USD 10,000 in cash when entering or leaving Mexico

body: Anyone entering or leaving Mexico with more than 10,000 USD, or the equivalent in other currencies, must declare it to customs. This covers cash, national or foreign cheques, payment orders, any other receivable document, or a mix of them. Carrying the money is not a crime; not declaring it is. On entry, you declare it on the Customs Declaration for Passengers Coming from Abroad. On leaving, you use the Money Declaration, passenger departure. Say on either form that you carry over 10,000 USD, and you must also fill out a second form. It is the Declaration of Entering or Leaving with Amounts in Cash or Receivable Documents. If you do not declare, you face a fine of 20% to 40% of the amount above 10,000 USD. If the undeclared amount is over 30,000 USD, you face 3 months to 6 years in prison. The federal tax authority also seizes the excess, unless you prove lawful origin. If lawful origin is not proved, you may face 5 to 15 years in prison and a fine of 1000 to 5000 days.
title: Declare more than 10,000 USD in cash or cheques when entering or leaving Mexico

body: A drone with a foreign registration, or one flown by a foreign operator, may not be operated in Mexico. The exception is a bilateral agreement between Mexico's aviation authority and that of the state of registration. Authorised scientific research drones are also exempt. Every drone with a maximum take-off weight over 250 grams must be registered on the SCT/DGAC website before it flies in Mexican airspace.
title: Foreign-registered drones and foreign operators may not fly in Mexico

body: Without third-party liability insurance on Mexico's federal roads, you face a fine of 20 to 40 daily minimum wages, read since 2016 as UMA. Every vehicle on a federal road must have a policy covering damage its driving may cause to other people and their property. Taking out the policy is the owner's duty, and nobody may force you to use a particular insurer. A car with wider motor insurance than this minimum may not be stopped from driving or fined on this ground. After a fine, the owner has 45 calendar days to take out a policy. Showing it to the revenue authority within that time cancels the fine. This rests on articles 63 Bis, 63 Ter and 74 Bis of the Federal Roads, Bridges and Motor Transport Law, added in May 2013.
title: Driving on Mexico's federal roads requires third-party liability insurance

body: You may bring animal, plant, aquaculture and fishery products into Mexico only in amounts for personal use and consumption. All of the goods are inspected, 100% of them. They must be free of pests and diseases. If the goods show insect holes or signs of live pests, the whole lot is returned or destroyed. The page does not list which products are allowed or give any quantity limits.
title: Food products allowed into Mexico: personal amounts, all inspected

body: A SIM or eSIM sold in Mexico only receives emergency alerts and calls emergency and citizen-service numbers, such as 911, and the provider. The contracted service is switched on once the line is linked to its holder, in the provider's shop or online. A foreigner proves identity with a passport, a CURP for foreigners, or an immigration card bearing a CURP. SIMs that cannot make voice calls, send SMS or place internet calls are exempt. This rests on the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission's guidelines of 9 December 2025, amended on 30 June 2026.
title: A SIM bought in Mexico works fully only once it is linked to its holder

body: You may bring up to three pets travelling with you into Mexico duty-free, among them cats, dogs, canaries, hamsters, ferrets and turtles. Birds of prey are not included. To do so, show customs the zoosanitary import certificate issued by SADER. For wild animals, a verification record issued by Profepa is also required.
title: Pets enter Mexico with a SADER zoosanitary import certificate

body: Medicines for personal use are part of the personal baggage you may bring into Mexico duty-free. For psychotropic substances, you must show a medical prescription.
title: Bringing psychotropic medicines into Mexico needs a prescription

body: Smoking any tobacco or nicotine product on a Mexican beach, in a park or on a restaurant terrace breaks federal law. Since January 2023 the tobacco regulation bans it in places where people gather. These include patios, terraces, balconies, playgrounds, parks, sports grounds, beaches, stadiums, shopping centres and markets. Hotels, hospitals, places of worship, places serving food or drink, and transport stops are on the list too. In a hotel you may not smoke in rooms or common areas; it may only have outdoor smoking zones. The Tobacco Control Law fines a breach up to 100 daily minimum wages, counted in UMA since 2016. The fine doubles for breaking the same rule again within a year of being notified of the last sanction.
title: No smoking on Mexican beaches, in parks or on restaurant terraces

body: You are a Mexican tax resident if you have set up your home in Mexico, under article 9 of the Federal Tax Code. If you also have a home in another country, you are resident in Mexico when your centre of vital interests is there. That is so, among other cases, when more than half of your income in the calendar year comes from Mexican sources. It is also so when your main professional activity is in Mexico. A resident pays income tax on all income, wherever it comes from.
title: Mexican tax residence follows your home and your centre of vital interests

body: Mexican law bans importing e-cigarettes and vapes, including disposable ones, with or without nicotine. It also bans their sale, distribution and transport for commercial purposes. Using or possessing one is exempt only when it serves none of the banned activities. Breaking the ban carries one to eight years in prison and a fine. Health authorities may take safety measures against such devices and dispose of them.
title: Mexico bans importing e-cigarettes and vapes

body: Carry your passport with you throughout your stay in Malaysia. If you cannot produce a genuine passport or entry permit on request, your presence can be treated as illegal entry. The penalty is a fine of up to RM10,000, up to 5 years in prison, or both, and whipping of up to six strokes. The offence can also be settled with a compound of RM3,000. Report a lost passport to the Immigration Department at once. The basis is section 6(3) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
title: Not producing your passport on request in Malaysia can count as illegal entry

body: Cash notes worth more than the equivalent of USD 10,000 must be declared when you enter or leave Malaysia. Failing to declare carries a fine of up to three million ringgit, up to five years in prison, or both. A false, inaccurate or incomplete declaration is punished the same way. Foreign currency notes are unrestricted in any amount; ringgit notes are unrestricted only up to the equivalent of USD 10,000. Customs officers may search you and detain the cash if they suspect an offence. The basis is sections 28B and 28F of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
title: Malaysia: undeclared cash over USD 10,000 can mean five years in prison

body: You may not drive on a road in Malaysia without a driving licence for that class of vehicle, unless the Act provides otherwise. Foreigners in Malaysia temporarily, for less than 12 months, are subject to stipulated conditions. Those from a 1949 Geneva or 1968 Vienna road traffic convention country may drive with an International Driving Permit (IDP) issued by its authorities. Citizens of ASEAN countries need only the driving licence of their own country, under a 1985 ASEAN agreement. This is what the director general of the Road Transport Department (JPJ) has said. The Act also counts a licence from a country party with Malaysia to a treaty providing for the recognition of domestic licences. It counts while it stays in force in that country. On conviction, driving without a licence brings a fine of 300 to 2,000 ringgit, up to three months in prison, or both.
title: Driving in Malaysia: an IDP from a convention country, or an ASEAN home licence

body: Flying a drone in Malaysia without authorisation can bring a fine of up to fifty thousand ringgit, up to three years in prison, or both. The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) says every drone flight in Malaysian airspace needs its authorisation to fly. Without it you may not fly within 5 nautical miles of an airport or higher than 400 feet. Apply to CAAM at least 14 working days before the flight. The basis is regulation 140 of the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016, with the penalty in regulation 206.
title: Every drone flight in Malaysia needs a permit from the aviation authority

body: Do not bring illicit drugs into or out of Malaysia. Importing and exporting drugs such as morphine, heroin, opium, or cannabis is strictly prohibited. The penalty for drug trafficking under the Customs Act 1967 and the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 is the mandatory death penalty. If you travel with prescription medication, you may only import or export it under licenses or permits issued by the Ministry of Health Malaysia.
title: Drug trafficking in Malaysia carries the death penalty

body: In a Malaysian marine park, taking or holding any sea animal or plant, dead or alive, is an offence without written permission. So is collecting or holding coral, and destroying, defacing or removing any object there. Anchoring a vessel by dropping a weight on, or tying a rope or chain to, coral, rock or another submerged object is also an offence. Spearguns, harpoons and other spearfishing gear may not even be carried in the park. The basis is sections 43 and 44 of the Fisheries Act 1985.
title: Malaysia's marine parks: taking coral or sea life is an offence

body: Before arriving in Malaysia, complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card online. At immigration you present both your valid passport and the completed card for checking. Submit it within the 3 days before your scheduled arrival. Use the official site, imigresen-online.imi.gov.my.
title: Fill in the MDAC digital arrival card online before you arrive in Malaysia

body: Do not bring prescription drugs into or out of Malaysia without a licence or permit issued by the Ministry of Health Malaysia. Importing or exporting prohibited drugs such as morphine, heroin, opium, or cannabis is strictly banned. Under the Customs Act 1967 and the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, drug trafficking carries a mandatory death penalty.
title: Prescription drugs require a licence or permit to enter Malaysia

body: Bringing in more than a month's supply of some medicines is an offence. It risks a fine of up to three thousand ringgit, up to a year in prison, or both. This covers prepared or packaged medicines that contain a substance on the Poisons List of Malaysia's Poisons Act 1952. Without a licence, you may bring them in your luggage, for yourself or your family. The amount must not exceed what one person reasonably needs for one month. Medicine brought in in breach of this is forfeited and handed to the Director General of Health.
title: Malaysia lets you bring at most a month's supply of Poisons List medicines

body: Your passport must remain valid for more than 6 months from the day you enter Malaysia. Count from the entry date, not from the day you leave. At immigration you show the passport together with the completed MDAC arrival card.
title: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months when you enter Malaysia

body: Every prepaid SIM in Malaysia must be registered before it is activated and used, tourists included. You register with the provider's service centre, an authorised agent or a dealer, showing your original identity document. On 26 February 2026 the regulator MCMC registered a new mandatory standard for prepaid registration. Under it, a non-citizen may hold at most two prepaid SIMs with each provider. Under the same standard, a tourist SIM works for at most three months and is then cut off automatically. The standard also sets out a framework that is to add biometric passport checks for non-citizens.
title: Malaysia: register prepaid SIMs; a 2026 standard ends tourist SIMs at 3 months

body: Bringing banned goods into Malaysia is a smuggling offence. On conviction, a first offence carries a fine of up to twenty times the goods' value or one hundred thousand ringgit, whichever is greater. Instead of the fine or with it, the court can impose up to three years in prison. Some goods are absolutely prohibited, whatever country they come from. They include indecent or obscene prints, photographs, books, films and other media. Cloth or animal skin bearing verses of the Quran is banned too. So is honeycomb, with or without honey, and so are pens or pencils that look like syringes. If you deny carrying such goods and they are then found in your bags, that is an offence in itself. The ban is in the Customs (Prohibition of Imports) Order 2023, and the penalty in the Customs Act 1967.
title: Malaysia bans bringing in obscene media, Quran verses on cloth, and honeycomb

body: Malaysian law counts vaping as smoking: it covers the smoke or vapour of tobacco and of other smokable products. Smoking where the Minister of Health has declared a no-smoking area brings a fine of up to 5,000 ringgit. Such areas include eating places, air-conditioned shops, shopping complexes, public transport terminals, public vehicles and public parks. Airports are no-smoking areas too, except listed places such as certain smoking rooms and zones. Where a listed place is a building, the ban also covers its five-foot way and three metres beyond its building line. In Melaka's World Heritage City, smoking is banned in all buildings, premises, public places and land except private homes and roads. In the George Town World Heritage Site, it is banned in all buildings, premises and open areas except private homes. People under 18 may not use tobacco products or smoke other smokable products, on pain of a fine of up to 500 ringgit or community service.
title: Smoking or vaping in Malaysia's no-smoking places costs up to 5,000 ringgit

body: If you are in Malaysia for 182 days or more in a year, you are a Malaysian tax resident, whatever your citizenship. The days need not run together, and any part of a day counts as a whole day. A shorter stay can also make you resident if it links to 182 consecutive days spent here in the year before or after. Residence decides the tax rate on your income from Malaysia. The basis is section 7 of the Income Tax Act 1967.
title: 182 days in Malaysia in a year make you a Malaysian tax resident

applies_when: you arrive from a country with a risk of yellow fever transmission, or transit more than 12 hours at its airport.
body: You need a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Malaysia if you arrive from a country WHO lists as having a risk of yellow fever transmission. The certificate is also required after a transit of more than 12 hours at the airport of such a country. The requirement applies to travellers aged 1 year and older. The certificate is valid for life, and no booster may be required. WHO warns that country requirements can change at any time.
title: Malaysia asks for a yellow fever certificate if you arrive from a risk country

body: In the Netherlands it is against the law to possess, sell or produce drugs. The Public Prosecution Service does not prosecute members of the public for possession of up to 5 grams of cannabis or up to 5 cannabis plants. Coffee shops may not sell cannabis to minors or more than 5 grams in one transaction. Under a toleration rule of 1 January 2013, only residents of the Netherlands may visit coffee shops and buy cannabis there. You count as a resident if you live in a Dutch municipality and are registered with it. Whether this rule is enforced depends on the municipality. Municipalities decide whether coffee shops may operate and can impose additional rules. If no more than 5 plants are grown for personal use, the police will generally only seize them. If more than 5 plants are found, the Public Prosecution Service will prosecute.
title: Netherlands: drugs are illegal, but up to 5 g of cannabis is not prosecuted

body: Foreign citizens who enter Portugal from another EU member state through a border without controls must make a declaration of entry within 3 working days. The declaration is made to the competent security force, such as the Public Security Police (PSP) or the National Republican Guard (GNR). It is not needed if you check into a hotel or similar accommodation right after entering the country. It is also not needed for residents, for those allowed to stay more than 6 months and for those under the EU regime.
title: Portugal: entering without border checks, declare entry within 3 working days

body: On Portuguese motorways with electronic-only tolls, gantries detect passing vehicles, and there are no toll booths and no need to stop. If you use these roads with a foreign-registered vehicle, you must have an activated means of payment. With Easytoll you link a Mastercard, Visa or Maestro bank card to the number plate, valid for 30 days after registration. Tollcard is a prepaid card activated by text message. If you drove on such a motorway without a valid means of payment, you must pay the amount owed to the operator of that toll system.
title: Portugal: a foreign car needs an active payment method on electronic-only tolls

body: If you become a tax resident in Portugal, you must change your status from non-resident to resident by updating your address. You have 60 days to report this to the Tax and Customs Authority (AT). The same 60 days apply when you move abroad and change your status back to non-resident. The text names no penalty for missing the deadline. You count as a tax resident in two cases. The first is that you stayed more than 183 days, consecutive or not, in any 12-month period. That period must begin or end in the tax year. The second is that you have a home in Portugal that clearly shows you intend to keep and use it as your habitual residence. This applies on any day of that period, even for a shorter stay. Residents typically pay tax on all their income, from Portugal or abroad. Non-residents pay tax only on income from Portugal.
title: Portugal taxes you as a resident after 183 days or with a habitual home

body: Importing wine or any intoxicating drink into Qatar carries up to three years in prison and a fine up to ten thousand riyals. The same article of the penal code covers exporting, making and preparing it. Selling, carrying or holding it to trade or promote falls under the same three years. So the duty-free bottle has no place in your luggage. Licensed hotel bars work under a separate permit regime, which this article does not touch.
title: Bringing alcohol into Qatar is a crime, not a customs matter

body: Anyone entering or leaving Qatar with 50,000 riyals or more declares it to the customs officer on the form the customs authority prepares. It covers cash, bearer instruments, precious metals and gemstones. The duty also covers what you send by another person, by cargo or by post. Say nothing, or say something false, and the officer may seize it and write a seizure report. You may be asked where it came from and what it is for. The officer may also hold whoever is involved, hand them to the interior ministry's security and send the case to the prosecution.
title: From 50,000 riyals you declare it; staying silent risks seizure

body: Qatar releases a narcotic or psychotropic medicine to a patient only after the Ministry of Public Health clears it. Ask the Department of Pharmacy and Drug Control before you fly. You need a medical report or prescription from the clinic treating you, issued no more than six months ago. It must show your details, the diagnosis, the treatment plan, the dose and the quantity, and carry the clinic's stamp. Add a copy of your passport and an undertaking to use the medicine yourself. Narcotics are allowed for thirty days or the length of your stay, whichever is shorter; psychotropics for two months. Anything above what you need is destroyed, and the medicines of schedule 1 of Law 9 of 1987 are not released at all.
title: A controlled medicine enters Qatar only with health ministry clearance

body: You may not drive on a road in Qatar without a driving licence from the Issuing Authority. This is the body the Minister of Interior designates. Visitors and tourists have two exemptions. First, a valid non-Qatari licence works if you commit to hand it to the Issuing Authority within fifteen days of entering the country. It is then approved for the period you may stay, or for a period the Issuing Authority sets. Second, visitors and tourists holding a valid international driving licence are exempt. For this second route the text sets no filing step and no time limit. Citizens of the Gulf Cooperation Council states may drive on a valid home licence. They must replace it with a Qatari one if it expires during their stay. Driving without a licence can mean one month to three years in prison. It can also mean a fine of 10,000 to 50,000 riyals, or just one of the two. A repeat offence carries a minimum fine of 20,000 riyals.
title: Driving in Qatar needs a licence, with two exemptions for visitors

body: The civil aviation authority's terms are written for organisations: a company must be registered in Qatar and state the nature of its activity in a letter. The operator must be at least eighteen, with no more than five aircraft per entity and an insurance policy before flying. Modifying the aircraft or attaching anything to it is forbidden, and the application goes through the national login system, which needs a local account. There is no separate route for a visitor in these terms at all. The framework is also being rebuilt: the law on unmanned aircraft was issued on 29 June 2026, and its executive regulation is still pending. Everyone the law addresses has six months to bring their affairs into line. While the regulation is pending, planning drone filming here is unwise.
title: Permits go to companies registered in Qatar — a visitor has no route

body: Gambling is a crime in Qatar, and the code defines it as any game where gain and loss turn on chance and each side stakes money. Playing carries up to three months in prison, a fine of up to 3,000 riyals, or one of the two. In a public place, a place open to the public or one kept for the purpose, both figures double: six months and 6,000 riyals. Opening or running such a place, or organising games in public, carries up to a year and up to 5,000 riyals. The court confiscates the money and the equipment used and orders the place closed.
title: Gambling for money is a crime, and in public it costs twice as much

body: Anyone who accommodates a foreigner in Qatar must report the guest within 24 hours of arrival: a hotel, a tourist establishment or a private host. The report gives the guest's name and address to the security department. Hotels do this themselves. If you stay with friends or in a private rental, make sure your host does it. A host who fails to report faces a fine of up to 20,000 riyals.
title: Qatar: whoever houses you reports you to security within 24 hours

body: If you need to get an entry visa before you reach the border, you must buy a visitor's health insurance policy first. The visitor visa will not be granted until you have bought one. If you can get a visa on arrival, you do not need the policy for the first 30 days after entry. You must buy one if you want to stay longer than 30 days. The policy costs QAR 50 per month. Only policies from insurers registered with the Ministry of Public Health, or from approved international insurers, are accepted. An international policy must cover Qatar for your whole stay and emergency and accident care up to QAR 150,000, with no deductibles or copayments. Holders of a Hayya Card must have insurance for the rest of the card's validity. Transit passengers and temporary entry travellers are not covered by this requirement. The page does not state a penalty for having no policy.
title: Visitors needing a visa before arrival must buy health insurance first

body: Qatar's cybercrime law punishes spreading, through the internet or a phone, photos, videos or recordings that touch on someone's private or family life. It applies even if what is shown is true. Insulting or slandering someone online, or violating social values or principles online, falls under the same article. The penalty is up to three years in prison, a fine of up to 100,000 riyals, or both. The law is Law No. 14 of 2014, article 8.
title: Sharing private photos or insults online can mean three years in Qatar

body: Qatar's prohibited goods list puts plants beside the drugs, and the plants are ordinary shop items elsewhere. Poppy seeds, poppy straw, black poppy and hemp seeds are all on it. So are coca leaf, cannabis sativa, khat and the chewable betel preparations sold as paan. A bread roll or a cake with poppy seeds is therefore a prohibited good at the border. Nothing on that list can be brought in by declaring it: prohibited means prohibited.
title: Poppy seeds and khat are on the prohibited list, next to cocaine

body: Drinking alcohol in a public place is a crime in Qatar, not an administrative slip. It carries up to six months in prison, a fine of up to 3,000 riyals, or both. The same penalty falls on anyone found drunk on a main road. It also covers being intoxicated and disturbing other people. Opening a shop or a house to trade in alcohol is punished under the same article.
title: A drink in the street is a criminal matter, and so is being drunk

body: The income tax law expressly does not apply to salaries, wages and allowances, so nothing is paid on them here. Residence is still determined, and that matters to the tax office back home: any one of three tests is enough. The first is a permanent place of residence in the State. The second is more than 183 days, consecutive or separate, during any twelve months. The third is having your centre of vital interests in Qatar, which is tied neither to days nor to housing.
title: No tax on salary, but a home or a centre of interests makes you resident

body: Qatar's customs authority lists electronic cigarettes among the goods prohibited by the unified tariff. The line covers electronic devices for cigarettes, electronic shisha and electrically heated tobacco devices alike. Parts for them are on the same list, batteries aside, so a spare pod or coil is prohibited too. A prohibited good is not something you declare and pay for: it may not cross the border at all. Leave the device at home rather than hope for a quiet green channel.
title: A vape is a prohibited good in Qatar, spare parts included

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. Qatar itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. The requirement states no separate transit rule, but with a connection in an affected country it is safer to have the certificate. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

body: Serbia exempts a traveller's personal items worth up to 100 euros from import duty. By European standards that is a low threshold. A new phone, a laptop or an expensive gift formally goes over it and has to be declared and paid for. Tobacco and alcohol are counted separately: 50 cigarettes, one litre of spirits and one litre of wine.
title: The duty-free threshold is 100 euros — a new phone already exceeds it

body: Every motor vehicle on Serbian roads carries a warning triangle, apart from mopeds, motorcycles and the like. Two triangles are required when a lorry or bus tows a trailer, and for the last vehicle of an organised convoy. A car also carries a first-aid kit of the national size B standard, and it must be somewhere you can reach it. A reflective vest has to be inside the passenger car, lorry or bus whenever it is on the road. Seat belts are compulsory for the driver and for every passenger in a seat that has one.
title: Triangle, first-aid kit and a reflective vest travel with the car

body: Cash of 10,000 euros or more must be declared to customs — in dinars, euros or any other currency, counted as one total. The duty applies both ways: when you enter and when you leave. People forget the exit half more often, and the money is counted just as carefully there.
title: From 10,000 euros you must declare, both entering and leaving

body: A child under twelve may not travel in the front seat of a car in Serbia. Anyone shorter than 135 centimetres travels strapped into an approved child seat fixed to the vehicle. Breaking those rules costs 5,000 dinars. Holding a child under twelve on your lap in the front row is another matter. That costs 20,000 to 40,000 dinars, or up to thirty days in prison. It also carries six penalty points. A child under twelve may not be carried on a moped, a tricycle, a motorcycle or a quadricycle at all.
title: No child under twelve in the front, and none on a lap at all

body: In Serbia a driver counts as under the influence with more than 0.20 milligrams of alcohol per millilitre of blood. From 0.50 to 0.80 the fine is 10,000 to 20,000 dinars, with six penalty points and at least three months without driving. From 0.80 to 1.20 it is 20,000 to 40,000 dinars or up to thirty days in prison, and at least four months without driving. From 1.20 to 2.00, or if you refuse the breath test, the law starts at fifteen days in prison or 100,000 to 120,000 dinars. Driving under a psychoactive substance costs eight penalty points and at least six months without driving.
title: Above 0.2 you are drunk here, and from 1.2 it is prison

body: A drone of 250 grams or more must have its operator registered with the Civil Aviation Directorate. The same holds for any drone carrying a sensor able to collect data about a person. Before every flight the operator files a notification in the Directorate's mobile application and keeps within the limits of the category. The remote pilot has to meet the age and competence conditions. For many categories that means passing the Directorate's theory exam or holding its certificate of competence. Flying while unregistered, without the notification or without the required training costs a private person 50,000 to 150,000 dinars. Parts of the sky are closed as geographical zones for drones, and short bans appear as NOTAM messages.
title: From 250 grams the operator registers, and every flight is notified

body: The Law on Foreigners does not oblige you to carry your passport at every moment, but it does oblige something people miss. Throughout your stay and on the way out you must use the travel document of the state you entered on. Holding two passports does not let you choose: for Serbia you are a national of the country whose document you came in with. And if your name changes while you are here, you have six months to obtain a new travel document with the changed details.
title: You must use the passport you entered on, not whichever you prefer

body: Do not enter Serbia illegally, and do not stay in a way that goes against the reason your visa, residence permit or single permit was issued. Leave within the deadline set for your voluntary return. Do not enter or stay while an entry ban is in force. Show your identity document to a police officer when asked. Do not hand your own document to someone else, use an invalid one, or pass off someone else's as yours. A foreigner who breaks these rules is fined 50,000 to 150,000 dinars. A protective measure removing you from Serbian territory may also be imposed. A private person may also be punished for helping a foreigner. This covers helping, or trying to help, a foreigner enter Serbia illegally, cross it in transit, or stay illegally. The punishment is up to 60 days in prison plus the same fine. Objects may also be seized in that case.
title: Illegal entry or stay in Serbia is fined 50,000 to 150,000 dinars

body: You may carry only the amount of medicine you need for yourself, or for a pet travelling with you. It may not exceed six months' need in a calendar year, depending on the nature and length of the disease. If you carry more than 15 days' worth, show customs the approval of the competent ministry when you enter or leave Serbia. That approval is based on the opinion of your chosen doctor. Up to 15 days of personal use, you do not need this approval. Medicines containing psychoactive substances fall under special conditions, which this text does not spell out. The text does not say what happens if you cannot show the approval.
title: Serbia: medicines beyond 15 days of use need ministry approval

body: Serbia forbids not only using a device that detects or jams speed measuring equipment, but having one in the car at all. Merely carrying one costs 10,000 to 20,000 dinars and three penalty points. Using it costs 20,000 to 40,000 dinars or up to thirty days in prison, six penalty points and at least three months without driving. The ban covers devices aimed at any equipment that detects and records traffic offences, not only speed. Selling or advertising such devices is forbidden separately.
title: A radar detector in the car costs money even switched off

body: Serbia prices speeding in steps, and the cheapest step is 3,000 dinars for up to 10 km/h over the limit in a settlement. Between 10 and 20 over it is 5,000 dinars. Between 30 and 50 over it becomes 10,000 to 20,000 dinars, four penalty points and at least thirty days without driving. Between 50 and 70 over it is 20,000 to 40,000 dinars or up to thirty days in prison. Between 70 and 90 over the law starts at fifteen days in prison, or 100,000 to 120,000 dinars. More than 90 km/h over the limit in a settlement is no longer speeding but reckless driving.
title: Speeding here is a ladder: 3,000 dinars at the bottom, prison at the top

body: You become a Serbian tax resident by either of two tests. The second is the one that catches travellers: 183 days or more on the territory of the Republic. They are counted within any twelve months that begin or end in the tax year. Not a calendar year, and the days need not run together — the law counts them continuously or with interruptions alike. Part of a day counts as a whole day, at any hour between midnight and midnight. Only the part of a day spent in transit through the country is left out. The first test is a residence or the centre of your business and personal interests here, and it needs no day count at all.
title: 183 days over any twelve months, and they need not run together

body: Two duties run in parallel, and both are 24 hours. Whoever provides accommodation for payment, or is being visited, reports the foreigner's stay to the police within 24 hours. A foreigner in neither of those cases reports their own stay within 24 hours of entering the country. The same 24 hours run again from a change of the place of stay. Moving from a hotel to a friend's flat starts a new registration. A foreigner who misses it is fined 5,000 to 150,000 dinars. A private host who fails to report a guest faces the same range.
title: Twenty-four hours from entry, and the clock restarts when you move

body: From 1 November to 1 April a vehicle must carry winter equipment whenever snow, ice or black ice lies on the road. For a car that means winter tyres — marked M+S, Snow or Winter — on every wheel, and chains on at least two driven wheels. The tread of those tyres must be at least 4 millimetres deep. Studded tyres may not be fitted at all, at any time of the year. Inside a built-up area the chains are not required. Not having the equipment, or not using it as prescribed, costs 5,000 dinars. A police officer can order a driver to fit it, and a driver who does not obey has the vehicle taken off the road.
title: From 1 November: winter tyres on snow, and studs are banned outright

body: If you are liable for conscription, you may not leave Russia once the military commissariat has issued you a summons. The ban lasts until you carry out the duty to report to the commissariat under the summons. The text names no penalty for this ban beyond the bar itself. The ban starts on the day the summons is posted in the public register of sent (served) summonses. It no longer depends on the summons being treated as served. Until the state register of persons liable for military service and the summons register are running, a different start applies. In that case the ban starts on the day the summons is sent to you. It also starts on the day a commissariat employee hands it to you in person against signature. A summons sent to your workplace or school counts from the day it is sent.
title: A conscription summons bars you from leaving Russia until you report

body: A drone with a maximum take-off mass from 0.15 kg to 30 kg must be put on state accounting. This applies if you bring it into Russia or buy it there. The owner submits an application to the Federal Air Transport Agency (Rosaviatsia), with a photo of the aircraft. For an imported drone the deadline is 10 working days from the day of import. For a drone bought in Russia it is 10 working days from the day of purchase. A home-built drone needs its application before it is first used for flights. The application can be sent by post or electronically, through the Gosuslugi portal or the state accounting portal. Rosaviatsia can refuse to put the drone on accounting if the application does not meet the rules or its information is false. The text gives no penalty for missing the deadline. Foreign citizens who temporarily bring a drone to take part in model aircraft sporting events are exempt. The same rules also cover ultralight manned aircraft with an empty mass of 115 kg or less. They run until 1 March 2028.
title: Drones of 150 g to 30 kg: apply for state accounting within 10 working days

body: The duty-free allowance depends on how you cross the border. By air it is goods worth up to 10,000 euros and up to 50 kg. By land or on foot it is only 500 euros and 25 kg — a twentyfold difference. Above the limit you pay 30 per cent of the value, and never less than 4 euros per kilogram. The allowance is counted per person and per crossing. A boxed new laptop or phone brought in by car will barely fit inside it.
title: 10,000 euros by air, 500 by car or train

body: Since 2 March 2022 you may not take foreign currency cash worth more than 10 thousand US dollars out of Russia. The same goes for monetary instruments in foreign currency. The sum is converted at the Bank of Russia's official rate on the day you leave. The ban has no exceptions for particular people. The Bank of Russia can give a permit to take out more, in cases and under rules it has set.
title: Foreign cash worth over 10 thousand US dollars may not be taken out of Russia

body: After entry a foreigner must be placed on migration registration at their place of stay — the general deadline is 7 working days. The host normally does this, a hotel automatically. In a rented flat or staying with friends the duty falls on the property owner, who often doesn't know about it. Breach means a fine of 2,000 to 5,000 roubles, possibly with administrative expulsion. Keep the detachable part of the notification until you leave.
title: Migration registration within 7 working days

body: A child may leave Russia with one parent without the other parent's consent, as long as there is no ban on the trip. A parent or guardian can file such a ban for one country, several or all, and for a set period. It is checked at border control, so find out in advance at the Interior Ministry whether there is one. The ban does not stop the Russian parent who filed it from travelling with the child. It can be withdrawn without a court, but disputes are settled only in court. A child travelling without any parent or guardian, for example with other adults, needs a passport and a notarised consent from one parent or guardian.
title: A child leaves Russia with one parent unless the other has filed a ban

body: Bringing in medicines containing potent or toxic substances is allowed only with a document proving they were prescribed to you. A prescription, an extract or a certified copy will do. There is one exception: medicines registered in Russia and sold there without prescription. If the substance is classed as narcotic or psychotropic, the matter is not administrative. Unlawful carriage across the border falls under part 1 of Article 229.1 of the Criminal Code, up to seven years' imprisonment. The danger is that many ordinary medicines containing codeine or tramadol are controlled far more strictly in Russia than where they were prescribed.
title: A potent medicine without proof of prescription is a criminal matter, not a fine

body: Residence is a matter of actual presence: 183 calendar days or more within twelve consecutive months. Absences shorter than six months do not break the period, so a three-month trip will not reset the count. Status for a calendar year is worked out from the total time spent in the country during that year. The code contains no other criteria at all: neither citizenship nor a foreign residence permit removes residence by itself. Nor does the code set any list of documents that prove where a person actually was. And an asymmetry people learn about late: no certificate of non-residence is issued at all. A refusal to issue the residence certificate is not proof of the opposite.
title: 183 days in any 12 months, and short trips do not break the count

body: Two administrative fines within three years can bar you from entering Russia — for three years. Any article of the Administrative Code counts, traffic offences included. These need not be serious offences. The list covers failing to give way to a pedestrian, driving without a roadworthiness certificate, or incorrectly mounted number plates. Ignoring signs and road markings, an unfastened seatbelt or no motorcycle helmet count too. So two minor fines from different trips close the border for years, and you find out only when you get there. The basis is part 4 of Article 26 of Federal Law 114-FZ.
title: Two fines in three years — an entry ban

body: In Russia a car or a light van of categories M1 and N1 may not be driven without winter tyres in December, January and February. Winter tyres, and studded ones where used, must be on every wheel. In June, July and August studded tyres are forbidden. The Russian traffic rules list each of these as a defect with which a vehicle may not be driven. Driving with one brings a warning or a fine of 500 roubles.
title: Winter tyres from December to February, and no studs from June to August

body: Saudi customs lists intoxicants of every kind among the banned goods that travellers most often carry. Alcohol is an intoxicant, and a bottle from a duty-free shop is no exception. The same list names drugs of every kind. Goods from this list will not pass customs. Leave all alcohol out of your luggage, gift sets included.
title: Alcohol of any kind cannot be brought into Saudi Arabia

body: Saudi Arabia's Anti-Cyber Crime Law punishes invading someone's privacy by misusing a phone camera or a similar device. Defaming or harming others through any information technology device falls under the same article. Both carry up to a year in prison, a fine of up to 500,000 riyals, or both. Producing, sending or storing online material that impinges on public order, religious values, public morals or privacy is heavier. That carries up to five years in prison, a fine of up to three million riyals, or both.
title: Invading privacy with a phone camera can mean a year in prison in Saudi Arabia

body: Every traveller entering or leaving Saudi Arabia must declare certain items valued at 40,000 riyals (SR) or more. These are currency, monetary instruments, gold bullion, precious metals, precious stones and fine jewellery. The duty comes from Article 23 of the Anti-Money Laundering Law. Restricted and prohibited goods must also be declared. For currency, bearer negotiable instruments and precious metals worth 40,000 SAR, the app is not enough. For restricted or prohibited goods too, you must go to the declaration office at the port, even after declaring electronically. If you carry 40,000 riyals or more and do not declare it, you face a fine. The fine is 25% of the seized value for a first violation and 50% for a repeat. If suspicion of a link to a crime or money laundering remains, all of the money is seized. You are then referred to the Public Prosecution and a court. The court may order confiscation of the full amount. It may also impose up to 10 years in prison or a fine of up to 5 million riyals, or both.
title: Declare 40,000 riyals or more in cash or valuables, and visit the port office

body: Registration is only the first step: it runs under GACAR Part 48. No one may operate a small drone in the Open Category without a Permit to Operate from the civil aviation authority. The operator of a drone with a sensor able to capture personal data must be registered, and filming or photographing needs approval too. The remote pilot certificate needs you to be at least 18, pass security clearance, and read and speak English. You must also pass the authority's theory exam or hold a drone pilot licence from an ICAO state it accepts. A visitor is not shut out. The authority may let the holder of a foreign remote pilot certificate fly a foreign-registered drone without a Saudi one.
title: Flying a drone needs a permit, and the pilot needs security clearance

body: Check which convention is printed on your international driving permit's cover before relying on it. The booklet in your hand may belong to a treaty Saudi Arabia never joined, as international driving permits follow two non-interchangeable patterns. Several countries still issue the 1949 pattern. The Kingdom acceded to the Vienna Convention on Road Traffic of 1968 on 12 May 2016, but never joined the Geneva Convention of 1949. Its only reservation to the 1968 convention concerns settling disputes between states, with nothing about driving.
title: Saudi Arabia accepts the 1968 driving permit, not the 1949 one

body: Visitors arriving by land should register in the Absher app under "Absher Travel for Visitors" before the trip. The service was launched on October 26, 2026, and the text says it becomes mandatory for visitors six months after launch. It covers Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nationals and other visitors at all of the Kingdom's land border crossings. You register traveler and vehicle information and obtain vehicle insurance through it. In the app you choose your nationality, enter your mobile phone number and document type, and give the border crossing and expected travel date. Then you fill in the traveler, vehicle and insurance details. The text names no penalty and does not say what happens at the border if you have not registered.
title: Absher Travel for Visitors will be mandatory for land border arrivals

body: The Food and Drug Authority clears a traveller's medicine on request, filed at its office in the port you arrive through. Attach a prescription or medical report from the clinic treating you, issued no more than six months ago. Narcotic and controlled medicines are cleared for the length of your stay and no longer. Other medicines are cleared for three months or the stay, whichever is less. Whatever exceeds what you need is not cleared and is destroyed together with customs. Some are never cleared: category D of the schedule and category A of the second table of the narcotics control law. Vaccines, medicines made from human blood and medicines that need medical supervision do not get through either.
title: Medicines need clearance from the Saudi Food and Drug Authority

body: The authority's own residency certificate application offers two routes, and the second is the surprising one. Either you remained 183 days or more in the Kingdom during the tax year, or you remained less than 183 days but more than 30. The short route does not stand alone. It asks you to attach the rental or ownership contract for the place you stayed. You also say whether that place is rented or owned by someone other than you. So a month in a flat you hold a contract for is the authority's own threshold, and it is far lower than most people assume.
title: Thirty days and a lease can make you tax resident here

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. Saudi Arabia itself is not such a country, so on a direct flight from a country without the disease the certificate is not asked for. Transit counts too: a layover of more than 12 hours at an airport in an affected country is treated as arriving from there. The requirement applies to everyone over 9 months of age. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry — it does not take effect immediately. The international certificate is valid for life and the country may not require a booster.
title: A yellow fever certificate — if you travel via an affected country

applies_when: you arrive from a country outside the Schengen area — that is exactly when the Article 75 certificate does not apply. If you travel from another Schengen country it does work and replaces clearing it with customs.
body: Ordinary prescription medicines are fine: a supply for the trip, commonly 30 to 90 days accepted, with a prescription from a licensed doctor. Have the prescription translated into the local language. Controlled medicines are harder, and there is a common misconception here. The Schengen medical certificate is issued to residents travelling to another Schengen State and is valid for at most 30 days. Each substance needs a certificate of its own. No agreements at all have been concluded with countries outside the Schengen area on carrying narcotic or psychotropic medicines. So arriving from outside, you cannot rely on it: check the procedure with the destination's customs authority before you fly.
title: The Schengen certificate will not help if you are not coming from Schengen

body: Non-EU travellers admitted for a short stay are registered in the Entry/Exit System (EES), an electronic system that replaces passport stamping. It records the time and place of each entry and exit and calculates your authorised stay itself. Visa-exempt travellers have a facial image and fingerprints taken. The fingerprints are of four fingers (index, middle, ring and little) of the right hand where present, and otherwise of the left. Children under 12 do not give fingerprints. Nor does anyone for whom fingerprinting is physically impossible. If the impossibility is only temporary, it is recorded and you must give fingerprints on exit or at your next entry. Border officers may ask you to explain why. A short stay is no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across the states operating the system. Any extension of authorised stay counts towards that limit on your next entry. If there is no exit record after your authorised stay expires, your record is flagged and a visa-required traveller is entered on the list of overstayers.
title: Schengen borders take fingerprints and a photo, and count your days

body: A passport for the Schengen area has to satisfy two separate conditions, not one. It must stay valid for at least three months after the day you intend to leave. And it must have been issued within the previous ten years. The second condition catches passports that were extended rather than reissued, and any document older than ten years however long it is still valid. Both are entry conditions, so it is the border guard who checks them. The three-month rule may be waived in a justified emergency; the ten-year rule has no such exception.
title: Your passport must pass two tests, and the second one is its age

applies_when: you are applying for a Schengen visa
body: The Visa Code sets this insurance, and it is no formality: the minimum cover is 30,000 euros. It has to be good across the member states and for the whole stay or transit, and to cover urgent treatment, hospital care, death and repatriation. For a multiple-entry visa you prove cover for the first trip only, and sign that you know it is needed for the later ones. The policy is taken out in your country of residence, and somewhere else only if that is impossible. The consulate also weighs whether a claim against that insurer could be recovered inside a member state. Holders of diplomatic passports are exempt.
title: Insurance for the visa: 30,000 euros, and the country you buy it in matters

body: Declare foreign currency worth more than $20,000 to customs, both on entry and on exit. Thai baht have a separate and much lower limit on the way out. You may take up to 500,000 baht to a neighbouring country and only 50,000 anywhere else. Not declaring, or giving customs false information, is a criminal offence in Thailand, not an administrative one.
title: Declare foreign currency over $20,000; take out no more than 50,000 baht

body: You can bring any amount of foreign currency into or out of Thailand. If you carry foreign currency worth more than USD 20,000 in total, or the equivalent, you must declare it to Customs. This applies both when you enter and when you leave. The text does not say what happens if you fail to declare.
title: Declare foreign currency above USD 20,000 at Thai customs

body: Before flying a drone in Thailand, register it with two authorities: the drone with civil aviation, its radio frequencies with telecommunications. Tourists must do this too; a short trip is no exemption. It applies to any drone with a camera, even one under 250 grams, and to any drone over two kilograms. Flying without registration can bring up to five years in prison or a fine of up to 100,000 baht, and the drone is seized.
title: A drone needs two registrations; flying without them is a crime

body: You may bring in duty-free 200 cigarettes or 250 grams of cigars or tobacco, and one litre of spirits. Other things for your own use pass duty-free up to 10,000 baht, if the quantity is reasonable. Cigarettes and alcohol bought at duty-free shops in the airport terminal get no exemption. So count everything you carry, including what you bought on the way or on arrival. Customs advises plainly: bring no more than the allowance.
title: Duty-free bought at the arrival airport still counts toward your allowance

body: In Thailand it is a crime to defame, insult or threaten the King, the Queen, the Heir Apparent or the Regent. The sentence is three to fifteen years in prison. There is no fine instead and nothing below three years. Foreigners are judged the same way as citizens. A repost or an old comment can be enough. Conditions in Thai prisons are harsh, and access to medical care is limited.
title: Insulting the King: three to fifteen years in prison, never just a fine

body: Narcotic medicines of category 2 may be brought into Thailand only with a permit from the Thai drug administration. They include codeine, dihydrocodeine, fentanyl, morphine, oxycodone, hydrocodone, methadone, pethidine and tapentadol. Apply online two to four weeks before the trip; it cannot be sorted out on arrival. Bring no more than 30 days' supply. You also need a doctor's certificate with the diagnosis, medicine name, dosage, total quantity and the doctor's licence number. On arrival, go through the red channel and show the medicines, documents and permit.
title: Codeine or morphine: get a permit two to four weeks before the trip

body: In a Thai national park, no one may collect, remove, harm or degrade wood, soil, rocks, gravel, sand, minerals or other natural resources. Nor may anyone lure or take out wild animals, or harm them in any way. Each of these offences carries up to five years in prison, a fine of up to 500,000 baht, or both. If what is taken is a seasonally renewable resource worth 2,000 baht or less in total, the fine is up to 5,000 baht. Visitors must also obey park officers' orders under section 20; disobeying them costs a fine of up to 100,000 baht. The basis is the National Park Act B.E. 2562 (2019).
title: Thai national parks: taking stones or sand, or harming wildlife, is a crime

body: Overstaying your permitted stay costs 500 baht a day, up to 20,000 baht. You must pay before you are allowed to leave. How long you are then banned from returning depends on whether you came forward yourself. If you report to the checkpoint yourself, an overstay of up to 90 days brings no ban. Over 90 days means a one-year ban, over a year three years, over three years five years. If you are arrested and prosecuted, an overstay under a year means a five-year ban, and over a year means ten.
title: Overstaying costs 500 baht a day and a re-entry ban of up to ten years

body: To bring a cat or dog into Thailand, you need a permit from the Department of Livestock Development. It comes from the Animal Quarantine Station at the arrival airport, and you apply in advance by email. The Thai embassy in Canberra says it takes at least 3 business days, the one in The Hague at least 7 working days. The rabies vaccination must be given at least 21 days before departure, and the animal must be at least 4 months old. Dogs also need a negative leptospirosis test taken within 30 days. Pit bulls and American Staffordshire Terriers are banned. Without the permit the animal is sent back at your expense.
title: A cat or dog needs an import permit arranged before departure

body: In Thailand a moped counts as a motorcycle, whatever the engine size. Thailand signed the Vienna Convention on Road Traffic in 1968 and ratified it on 1 May 2020. Under article 54 it declared that it treats mopeds as motorcycles. So the small automatic scooter everyone rents is a motorcycle wherever the Convention applies. The licence or permit you show must include the motorcycle category.
title: A rented scooter counts as a motorcycle, so your licence must cover motorcycles

body: It applies to a Thai tax resident: someone who spends 180 days or more in the country in a calendar year, whatever the visa. A resident pays tax on Thai income and on foreign income brought into Thailand. Since 1 January 2024 this covers income brought in in any year, not only in the year it was earned. It is taxed for the year the money arrives. Income that arose before 1 January 2024 is not covered, even if you bring it in later.
title: Foreign income brought into Thailand is taxed, except income from before 2024

body: If you spend 180 days or more in Thailand in a calendar year, you become a tax resident, whatever your visa. Then foreign income you bring into Thailand becomes taxable, such as a transfer to a local account or a cash withdrawal from an ATM. This applies to income earned from 1 January 2024. Thailand has more than 60 double taxation treaties, but they do not remove the duty to declare. Count your days: the threshold is 180, not the usual 183.
title: 180 days in Thailand in a year make you a tax resident

body: Every non-Thai traveller submits the Thailand Digital Arrival Card before arriving, by air, land or sea. Infants and children included; crew are not. The card goes in within 3 days of arrival, counting the day you land, and up to 72 hours before entry. One card covers one entry, so a new one is submitted every time. The confirmation and a QR code come by email; a family submission takes up to 10 people at once. A technical landing or a transit without passing immigration needs nothing — but leaving the airport does. The card is free.
title: Fill in the TDAC arrival card before you fly to Thailand

body: Thailand treats a vape as prohibited goods. Bringing one in is punished by up to ten years, or a fine of five times its value, or both. The device, what it is packed in and even the vehicle that carried it are confiscated. Holding or receiving one is a customs offence as well: up to five years, or four times the value with duty, or both. Selling or providing them carries up to three years, or six hundred thousand baht, or both. A vape counts as a tobacco product, so using it in a smoke-free zone is a separate fine of up to five thousand baht. A possession case can be settled at the customs stage, but that is the best outcome and not the rule.
