title: A vape is contraband in Thailand: bringing one in is a customs crime

applies_when: you arrive from a country where yellow fever is present, or transit through one.
body: You need a yellow fever vaccination certificate if you arrive from a country where the disease is present. Thailand itself is not such a country. A layover of more than 12 hours at an airport in an affected country counts as arriving from there. The rule applies to everyone older than 9 months. The vaccination must be given at least 10 days before entry, because it does not work straight away. The international certificate is valid for life, and a booster may not be required.
title: Yellow fever certificate needed if you come from or through an affected country

body: Foreigners may temporarily bring in their own, rented or borrowed vehicle for personal use without customs duties or taxes. The vehicle may arrive with you or before or after you. A vehicle must always be declared to customs electronically or in writing; an oral declaration is not enough. Customs sets the period of temporary import from your declaration, taking into account how long you stay. That period must stay within any limits the Government sets for temporary import. If you make a reasoned request, customs may extend the period, again within those limits. You may take the vehicle back out through any customs office, and no duties or taxes are charged on re-export. If the vehicle is seriously damaged in an accident or by force majeure, it does not have to be taken back out. A vehicle used to carry passengers for pay or goods commercially follows other rules.
title: Driving into Tajikistan: declare your car; no duties for your stay

body: You may take up to USD 3,000 (or the equivalent in any currency) out of Tajikistan at one time without a written declaration or papers. From USD 3,001 to 10,000, declare the cash in writing. You need no proof of where it came from. Above USD 10,000, declare it in writing and also show documents proving its source. Accepted proof includes the customs declaration made when you brought the money in, or a bank's currency exchange receipt. A bank's money transfer receipt or cash withdrawal slip also counts. Bringing cash in is different: up to USD 10,000 needs no written declaration, and USD 10,000 or more must be declared in writing. These rules apply to residents and non-residents alike. If your declaration is wrong or missing, customs may suspend and restrict the movement of the money. The text says only that violators are held liable under other Tajik legal acts, and names no fine amount.
title: Leaving Tajikistan with over USD 3,000 in cash requires a written declaration

body: Goods for personal use worth up to USD 1,000 and weighing up to 50 kg per person enter Tajikistan free of customs duties and taxes. Vehicles do not count, and the goods must not be meant for business. The allowance does not cover goods whose import or export is prohibited or restricted. Within these limits, goods in your accompanied baggage may be declared orally. Alcohol, tobacco and other excise goods are duty-free only within the separate limits of the annex to the rules. Failing to declare goods that must be declared, or declaring them wrongly, brings a fine of half to twice their value, and the goods are confiscated. This rests on government decree No 544 of 2 November 2007, as amended on 21 May 2022.
title: Duty-free into Tajikistan: goods up to USD 1,000 and 50 kg per person

body: Drinking alcohol in the street, at stadiums, in squares and parks, on any public transport or in other public places is an offence in Tajikistan. So is appearing drunk in public in a way that offends human dignity and public morals. The fine is 3 to 5 calculation indicators, and the same again for a repeat within a year. The fine is from the Code of Administrative Offences in its edition of 13 November 2023.
title: Drinking alcohol in public places in Tajikistan is fined

body: Bringing a drone into Tajikistan, selling it and flying it are allowed only under a licence. Civil drones are registered with the civil aviation authority, and a drone without identification marks may not be used. Each flight needs a flight plan in advance, giving its purpose, time, area, drone type and altitude. Flying is banned near airports, on the state border, where senior state officials are present, over crowds and near military or strategic sites. There it is allowed only under the procedure set by the State Committee for National Security. A drone may not carry cargo from one place to another, and filming citizens' homes and property needs the owner's consent. Police and security forces may destroy a drone flown in breach of the rules, including with firearms, and its user pays for the damage.
title: Drones in Tajikistan need a licence, state registration and a flight plan

body: The consular fee table for Tajikistan's e-visa lists an entry permit for GBAO (Gorno-Badakhshan) at USD 20. The permit for special border areas is put on the e-visa form: choose the special item when you fill in the application. Under the border zone regulation, foreigners may enter and stay in the border zone only with permission of the foreign ministry and internal affairs bodies. That permission is not needed when the entry visa or the invitation names places in the border zone. Breaking the border zone entry rules brings a warning or a fine of 5 to 10 calculation indicators. A repeat within a year after an administrative penalty brings 10 to 30 indicators, with or without expulsion.
title: Tajikistan's GBAO entry permit costs USD 20 and goes on the e-visa

body: You may bring a limited quantity of medicines into Tajikistan for your own medical or other non-commercial use, whether or not they are registered there. When you leave, you may take out medicines in the quantity you need for personal use. Spoiled, counterfeit and expired medicines may not be brought in. Narcotic and psychotropic medicines follow separate rules set by other laws of Tajikistan. The text sets no figure for the limit and names no penalty for breaking these rules. Bringing in medicines as a business is a different route: legal entities do it under rules set by the government and need a foreign trade permit.
title: Tajikistan: medicines for personal use, in a limited quantity

body: Foreigners must register with Tajikistan's internal affairs bodies within 10 working days of entry. If you stay no more than 10 working days and leave within that time, you need not register. Holders of an e-visa are exempt from registration. Tajik law or international treaties recognised by Tajikistan may provide otherwise; some agreements exempt citizens of certain countries for set periods. Hotels in Tajikistan can register your passport, as can the internal affairs ministry and its offices. Breaking the registration rules brings a warning or a fine of 10 to 15 calculation indicators. A repeat within a year after an administrative penalty brings 15 to 30 indicators, with or without expulsion.
title: Register with Tajikistan's internal affairs bodies within 10 working days

body: Bringing religious literature or other religious items into or out of Tajikistan needs a conclusion of the state religious studies expert review. So do selling and distributing them. Without it, a person is fined 60 to 70 calculation indicators, and the items are confiscated. A repeat within a year after an administrative penalty brings 90 to 100 indicators, again with confiscation. The fines are from the Code of Administrative Offences in its edition of 13 November 2023.
title: Religious literature needs a state expert review to enter or leave Tajikistan

body: A person in Tajikistan for more than 182 days in any 12-month period is its tax resident for the current calendar year. The period must start or end in that year. In the year residency begins or ends, it counts only from the first or until the last day of physical presence in Tajikistan. A tax resident's income tax covers income from all sources, in Tajikistan and abroad. A non-resident is taxed only on income from sources in Tajikistan. This is the Tax Code No 1844 of 23 December 2021, in its edition of 13 November 2023.
title: More than 182 days in Tajikistan in 12 months makes you its tax resident

body: Taking cultural or natural property out of Türkiye is punished by five to twelve years in prison. The sentence carries a judicial fine of up to five thousand days as well. The term is read broadly: old coins, potsherds, pieces of mosaic, a worked stone from a dig or a beach. Saying you found it does not help — a find must be reported to the nearest museum within three days. Buying or accepting an unreported item is itself two to five years in prison. Buy souvenirs in a shop and keep the receipt.
title: Taking an old coin or a stone from a dig out of Türkiye: five to twelve years

body: A law of 1951 protects the memory of Ataturk, separately from the article on insulting the state. Publicly insulting it or swearing at it carries one to three years in prison. Damaging, breaking or defiling a statue, bust or monument of him, or his grave, carries one to five years. Doing any of it together with another person, in a public place or through the press raises the sentence by half. Urging someone else to do it is punished the same as doing it. Prosecutors open such a case on their own motion, so there is nobody to withdraw a complaint.
title: Insulting Ataturk is a crime of its own: one to three years

body: If you take more than 185,000 Turkish lira out of Turkey, declare it to a customs officer. The same goes for more than 10,000 euros in foreign currency cash or its equivalent. Amounts below these limits need no declaration. If customs finds you took out more than that without declaring it, you get an administrative fine. All the cash you carry is held. The case is reported to the public prosecutor and to the Financial Crimes Investigation Board. Customs may also ask you how much cash you carry and where it comes from. You must then answer fully and truthfully. If you give no explanation, or a false or misleading one, the fine is 10 per cent of the undisclosed amount. All your cash is held, and the same two authorities are told. Some cash may not be carried out at all, such as personal debts, gifts, inheritance or loan payments. It may only leave through banks, and if found on you it is seized.
title: Declare cash above 185,000 lira or 10,000 euros when leaving Turkey

body: Tobacco and alcohol are duty-free only up to set amounts, and only if you carry them in your own accompanied baggage. They may not come by post or express cargo. Passengers under 18 get no tobacco or alcohol exemption at all. The amounts are 600 cigarettes, 50 cigars, 250 g of pipe tobacco, and 1 litre of spirits above 22% alcohol. For drinks of up to 22% the limit is 2 litres. Each amount is the total allowance per passenger for that product. The text does not say what happens to tobacco or alcohol above these amounts. For non-commercial goods brought for personal or family use, the part above the exemption is taxed. A single flat tax applies: 18% if the goods come directly from an EU member state, 20% if from other countries. The flat rate applies only to items not exceeding 1500 Euros in value for each passenger over 18 or for each shipping. If the total value of items in accompanied baggage exceeds 1500 Euros, the normal import tax rates apply.
title: Duty-free tobacco and alcohol: adults only, in your own baggage

body: Do not intentionally demolish, spoil, destroy or harm in any way a registered heritage site. The same goes for a protected immovable cultural or natural asset, or its protection zone. This applies once its protection has been notified or announced. Doing building or physical work on such a place without the required permission is covered by the same provision. The penalty is two to five years in prison and a judicial fine of up to 5,000 day-fines. If the act is done to smuggle the cultural or natural asset abroad, the penalty is doubled. Smaller repairs and alterations that need no building permit are treated separately. Doing them without the required permission, or against it, carries six months to three years in prison or a judicial fine. The basis is Article 65 of the Law on the Conservation of Cultural and Natural Property.
title: Damaging a registered historic site in Türkiye: two to five years in prison

body: Register any drone with a maximum takeoff weight of 500 grams or more. The register is run by the civil aviation authority (Sivil Havacılık Genel Müdürlüğü). If you bring one in from abroad yourself or take one over inside Turkey, you must register it within three days. Missing that deadline costs 50,000 lira. A false statement or false data entry when registering costs 100,000 lira. Flying without a flight permit, or outside the areas set by the authority or local governors, costs 60,000 lira when the police catch you. Breaking the rules on import, sale, registration, licensing or airworthiness draws 5,000 to 100,000 lira from the authority. The page attached to the text asks you to sign in with e-Devlet (the state portal) before registering a purchased drone.
title: Drone of 500 grams or more: register within three days, fines up to 100,000 lira

body: A phone brought into Turkey from abroad can be used for 120 days from the day you entered, without registering. If it is not registered within that time, it is cut off from the networks. Registration is for phones and other devices with an IMEI number, the device's identity number, which you can see by pressing *#06#. Some people can register through the e-Devlet portal, the state online services site. These are people with a Turkish or foreigner identity number who can get an e-Devlet password. You also pay a state fee. Registration is allowed only if 365 days have not passed since you entered Turkey. Diplomatic document holders cannot use e-Devlet, so they apply to the operators' Subscriber Registration Centers. A short stay does not change the 120-day limit. Phones that arrive by post or are bought online cannot be registered.
title: A phone brought into Turkey works 120 days, then is cut off unless registered

body: Article 301 punishes publicly denigrating the Turkish nation, the state, its parliament, government or judicial organs. The range is 6 months to 2 years, not up to 3 as the advisories put it. It carries two safeguards that are usually left out. Expressions of thought made for the purpose of criticism do not constitute an offence, and a prosecution needs the permission of the Minister of Justice. The flag is a different article: tearing, burning or otherwise publicly denigrating it carries 1 to 3 years. Denigrating the Independence March carries 6 months to 2 years. The increase of a third for an offence committed abroad applies to a Turkish citizen, not to every traveller.
title: Insulting the state: 6 months to 2 years; the flag is a separate article

body: Turkish customs lets jewellery and other articles of precious metals and stones worth up to 15,000 US dollars in and out freely. They must not be for sale. Anything above that may be taken out only if it was declared to customs on arrival, or if there is proof it was bought in Türkiye. An expensive watch on your wrist falls under the same rule, even though nobody treats it as luggage. Declare the item on the way in, because on the way out there will be nothing to prove you brought it with you.
title: A watch over 15,000 dollars: declare it on the way in

body: You may bring medication for your own treatment in reasonable amounts. Carry it in your accompanied baggage, or send it one month before or three months after you arrive. Show customs a document saying you must use the medication during your trip. A report from a healthcare organisation, a doctor's report or a prescription all count. The amount must be reasonable for the time you will spend in Turkey. This rule applies to people visiting Turkey for personal treatment. The sheet names no penalty for missing paperwork. It does not mention a separate advance permit, original packaging, a pharmacy label or the language of the document.
title: Personal medication is allowed with a doctor's report or prescription

body: In Türkiye's national parks, nature parks, natural monuments and nature conservation areas, wildlife may not be destroyed. Upsetting the natural and ecological balance is forbidden. So is any interference that changes the site's character or pollutes its soil, water or air. Hunting, grazing and taking forest products that upset the natural balance are banned too. Breaking these bans carries one to three years in prison and a judicial fine of up to 5,000 day-fines. Acts banned by the forest, hunting and fisheries laws carry double the penalty when committed in these places. In a park run by the Directorate General, entering without paying brings an administrative fine of four times the entrance fee. The basis is Law No. 2873 on National Parks.
title: Türkiye's national parks: one to three years for destroying wildlife

body: The Revenue Administration calls you a non-resident if you have no home in Türkiye and do not stay there more than six months in a row. A non-resident pays Turkish tax only on income earned in Türkiye. Nothing is filed here for income earned abroad. Stay longer in one stretch and the reverse applies: worldwide income falls under Turkish tax. The count runs by calendar year, and the word that matters is continuous. Planning a winter stay or remote work, count the days before you go.
title: Six months in a row in Türkiye and Turkish tax reaches your foreign income

body: Foreigners wishing to enter Türkiye must carry a passport or travel document with an expiration date at least 60 days beyond their allowed stay. This means 60 days beyond the duration of stay of your visa, e-Visa, visa exemption, or residence permit. For example, a 90-day allowed stay requires at least 150 days of validity at entrance, and a 30-day stay requires at least 90 days. Citizens of certain countries permitted to enter with national identity cards, or holding passports recognized as expired for specific periods, are exempt.
title: Passport must stay valid at least 60 days past your allowed stay

body: The fine for passing without paying is four times the toll itself; until 2018 the multiplier was ten. Pay the toll properly within fifteen days and the fine is not applied. Pay the toll with a fine equal to it within 45 days, and the fine counts as one times the toll. For foreign plates, though, the law does not wait out those fifteen days. The fine is collected by informing the driver, with no formal notification. Paying the toll within the same fifteen days still cancels the fine. And the main point is stated in the law, in force since 2015: a foreign-plated vehicle may not leave the country until collection has taken place. And until such a toll and its fine are paid, the vehicle cannot pass technical inspection or be sold. Since 2025 the exit ban also covers the tolls and penalties of motorways whose operation was granted or transferred to an operating company. These can also be collected at the customs gates.
title: A foreign-plated car cannot leave the country until the toll is collected

body: If you carry foreign currency worth more than ten thousand US dollars, you must declare it to the Customs authorities. Do this when you arrive and again when you leave. The rule says "exceeding ten thousand", so exactly ten thousand does not need declaring. The limit is in US dollars or the equivalent in another currency. The text does not say how to total several currencies. How to declare is set by the Anti-Money Laundering (Cross Border Declaration of Currency and Bearer Negotiable Instruments) Regulations, which are not part of this text. If you break the rule, you are liable to a penalty as provided for in the Foreign Exchange Act. This text does not give the amount. Separately, nobody may take Tanzanian legal-tender notes or coins out of the country without the Governor's permission.
title: Declare foreign currency above ten thousand US dollars, arriving or leaving

body: No one may import narcotic drugs for personal use into Tanzania. Medicines for personal use need an import permit from the Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority (TMDA). The application must include a proforma invoice (a supplier's advance invoice) for the medicines and a genuine doctor's prescription. Apply online through the TMDA trader portal. Medicines that contain psychotropic substances (substances that act on the mind) get a thorough examination before TMDA decides. TMDA advises applying six weeks before the consignment is loaded. This avoids storage costs at the port of entry and disposal costs if the consignment holds products that are not allowed. After a permit is issued, the consignment must be inspected at the port of entry. In some cases it may be released there unopened and inspected within one week at the owner's premises. The text names no penalty for breaking these rules.
title: Tanzania bans narcotic drugs for personal use; other medicines need a permit

body: Any drone flight in Tanzania requires a permit from the civil aviation authority. Recreational flights included: there is no exception by purpose. Foreigners must obtain the permit before arriving in the country. The authority itself states the processing time: three to four weeks for non-residents. Booking a safari a week ahead and sorting it out on the spot will not work. Flying without a permit risks a large fine, confiscation of the aircraft and criminal prosecution, and imprisonment in serious cases. Filming in national parks needs a separate permit from the parks authority, charged per day.
title: A drone permit takes 3-4 weeks — you cannot sort it out on arrival

body: Here, unlike in India, both kinds are recognised: the Act names the Geneva Convention of 1949 and the Vienna Convention of 1968 outright. It recognises not only the international permit but also a domestic licence issued under either convention. The Act ties nothing to your visa: recognition falls away if the permit itself expires, or if you stay in the country beyond six months. Driving without a valid licence is prohibited, and with no penalty of its own the general one applies. That is up to six months' imprisonment or a fine. The amount is not quoted here: in the published version it is nominal, and later finance acts have not been fully applied to the text. Traffic keeps to the left: giving way to an emergency vehicle, a driver must pull to the left-hand edge.
title: Vienna and Geneva permits are both recognised, for up to six months

body: All plastic carrier bags are prohibited in mainland Tanzania, whatever their thickness. The ban covers importing, exporting, making, selling, storing, supplying and using them. Possessing or using one is punished by a fine of thirty thousand to two hundred thousand shillings, or up to seven days in prison, or both. Bringing them in is a heavier article: from twenty million shillings, and up to two years. So take every bag out of your luggage before the flight, the duty-free one too. These rules are for the mainland — Zanzibar legislates for itself.
title: Plastic bags are banned in mainland Tanzania, carrying one included

body: Tanzania's Penal Code makes same-sex sexual relations a crime, in private as well as in public. Carnal knowledge against the order of nature carries at least thirty years and up to life imprisonment. Acts of gross indecency between men carry five years, whether in public or in private. Gross indecency between any two people carries one to five years or a fine.
title: Same-sex sexual acts are a crime in Tanzania, up to life imprisonment

body: Since 28 March 2025 the price and the payment for every good and service inside the country must be in Tanzanian shillings. Paying in foreign currency is not the only offence. Quoting or advertising a price in it, compelling or accepting payment in it, and refusing shillings are all forbidden. The Bank of Tanzania addresses foreigners, tourists included, directly: change money at a commercial bank or a licensed bureau de change. Cards and other cashless methods keep working as before. The regulations do list transactions that may still be conducted in foreign currency. But entering into or renewing contracts payable in it has been banned since that date.
title: Paying in dollars is out, and so is quoting a price in them

body: There are three tests and any one of them is enough. If you have a permanent home here, a single visit during the year makes you resident: presence on any day at all counts. Without a home the days are counted: 183 in the year of income. Or an average of more than 122 days a year across the current year and the two before it. A resident is taxed on worldwide income on a progressive scale topping out at 30 per cent. A non-resident is taxed only on local income, but at a flat 30 per cent with no tax-free band.
title: A permanent home here, and one visit a year is enough

applies_when: you arrive from a country the World Health Organization lists as at risk of yellow fever, or you spent more than twelve hours in transit through an airport of such a country
body: Tanzania is not a country where yellow fever occurs, and it does not ask everyone for a certificate. It asks travellers who arrive from a country the World Health Organization lists as at risk, from the age of one. The trap is the footnote: the requirement also covers anyone who spent more than twelve hours in transit through an airport of such a country. Kenya is on that list, so the popular safari in Kenya followed by Zanzibar brings the certificate into play. Flying in from Europe with no African stopover does not. One more thing worth knowing: since 11 July 2016 a yellow fever certificate is valid for life. It cannot be refused for being more than ten years old, and no booster may be demanded of you.
title: Not everyone needs the yellow fever shot, but a long layover triggers it

body: Buy Zanzibar's local inbound insurance policy, which is compulsory for all visitors entering the island. You must purchase this local cover even if you already hold valid travel or medical insurance from another provider. A policy brought from home does not lift the requirement. The official price is 44 dollars for an adult and 22 dollars for a child. Travellers from Southern African Development Community (SADC) and East African Community states pay 22 dollars instead. Fees and coverage may change in line with regulatory requirements, so check before you travel. Ask when you buy about the length of cover, as the page does not state it.
title: Zanzibar requires its own visitor insurance even if you already have a policy

body: At a land crossing you may bring in goods worth up to 500 euros and up to 50 kg duty-free. By air the figure is 1,000 euros. The relief applies only if you enter Ukraine no more than once in any 24 hours. Enter a second time and the same goods go on a written declaration, taxed at 10 per cent duty plus VAT. Above the allowance and up to 10,000 euros the same rate applies, but only to the excess. For short cross-border trips this is the main trap.
title: A second entry within a day makes the whole allowance taxable

body: Taking currency valuables worth more than the equivalent of EUR 10,000 out of Ukraine, you must declare them. And declaring is not enough: above the threshold the bank has to confirm where the money came from. A statement showing a cash withdrawal from your own accounts, or a purchase of investment metals, will do; naming a figure will not. The requirement belongs to the martial law regime and was brought in to stop capital leaving the country. It was lifted for nine days in March 2022 and then reinstated by an NBU Board resolution, so check before you travel whether it still stands.
title: Above EUR 10,000 a declaration is not enough, the bank must vouch for it

body: A curfew is not advice to stay in but a ban on being in streets and other public places without an issued pass. Vehicle movement during those hours is prohibited too. The pass is issued by the commandant's office and only for its own territory: one obtained in a city does not work in another. A foreigner presents the pass together with a passport and a document confirming the lawfulness of their stay in the country, so carry both. The military command may check documents and, where needed, search belongings, vehicles, baggage and premises. There is no single nationwide time: the hours are set by the military command together with the military administrations. Check them for the particular city shortly before the trip.
title: A curfew pass works only in the city that issued it

body: A drone counts as an aircraft under the Air Code, so flying one is use of Ukrainian airspace and falls under the airspace regulation. One under 20 kilograms flown for fun is not entered in the aircraft register, and that is no exemption. It still has to be recorded. Compliance with the airspace rules is checked by Air Force units, the National Police, the security service and the border guard. They check it while the border, critical infrastructure and public order are being protected. Those same units carry out the neutralising of threats created by a drone flown in breach of the rules. A police officer or serviceman of those units who detects such a breach on duty must stop it at once and bring the offender to answer.
title: A tourist drone goes unregistered, but one flown in breach may be neutralised

body: In Ukraine you may not publish photographs, video or text showing where units are or where they are moving. The same holds for the results of a strike and the place it hit. Air defence at work and military vehicles on the move are on the list too, as are defence plants and critical infrastructure. The ban covers social networks and messengers, not only the press. Breaking it brings criminal or administrative liability under the law of 24 March 2022. So put the phone down during an alert, and say nothing about where anything landed until officials do.
title: Do not film or post strikes, air defence or troops on the move

body: Ukraine's airspace remains closed, so you cannot fly into the country. The Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport says daily missile and drone attacks directly threaten passengers' lives and the safety of international flights. Plan to arrive by land instead, for example by train, bus or car from Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania or Moldova. A flight to a neighbouring country followed by an overland leg is the way in. The Ministry describes work on preparing for a safe reopening of the airspace, but gives no date. Check the current situation before you book.
title: Ukraine's airspace is closed, so you cannot fly in

applies_when: you need a visa for Ukraine, or you are applying for a residence permit
body: The law on the status of foreigners says what entry takes: a passport document and a visa, where a visa is needed. Insurance is not among those conditions, nor among the grounds for refusing entry. That list is closed and names things like a forged document or a previous breach at the border. Where insurance does count is one step earlier: a visa may be refused to someone with no valid medical policy. That applies only where such a policy can be taken out in the country of application, and a residence permit needs one outright. So if you are applying for a visa, buy the policy: refusal on that ground is written into the law. If you travel without a visa, this law does not make insurance a condition of your entry.
title: Insurance is a visa matter here, not a condition of entry

body: Medicines not registered in Ukraine may be brought in for your own use as personal belongings, in hand or checked baggage. The limit is five packs of each name per person. Medicines containing narcotic or psychotropic substances are excluded from that allowance. They pass in the quantity stated on a prescription you are carrying, issued in your own name. It must bear the seal of the doctor or of the clinic. Sending such substances by post for personal use is forbidden outright, so there is no way to have them follow you.
title: Five packs of each medicine, and a narcotic one needs your own prescription

body: Ukraine counts money among the conditions of entry, not among the formalities. A foreigner needs enough for the planned stay and for the way home or onward. The border service publishes the sums: 9,570 hryvnia for one day, 23,925 for ten and 55,825 for thirty. Cash, a card statement, a paid booking, a tour voucher, a host's guarantee letter or a dated return ticket all count. The check is selective and belongs to second-line control, so most travellers never meet it. Fail any one of the entry conditions and the crossing is refused.
title: Money is an entry condition here, with published sums

body: Whether you count as a tax resident of Ukraine is decided in steps, and counting days comes late. First, having a place of residence in Ukraine. If you also have one abroad, a permanent home in Ukraine makes you a resident. If you have a permanent home in both countries, the country with closer personal or economic ties (your centre of vital interests) decides. Where your family permanently lives, or your registration as an entrepreneur, is enough to place that centre, though not the only sign. The 183-day test applies only if that centre cannot be determined or you have no permanent home anywhere. Then you are a resident if you spend at least 183 days in Ukraine in the tax year, counting the days of arrival and departure. If none of this settles it, Ukrainian citizenship makes you a resident. Declaring Ukraine as your main place of residence, or registering as a self-employed person, is also enough on its own.
title: Ukraine tax residency: home, family ties, then 183 days, then citizenship

body: A foreign national aged 14 or older who stays in the US for 30 days or longer must apply for registration. They must also be fingerprinted before the 30 days are up. This applies only if they were not already registered and fingerprinted under the provisions the law names. A parent or legal guardian must apply to register a foreign child under 14 who stays 30 days or longer. This applies only if the child has not already been registered under those same provisions. Willful failure or refusal to register or be fingerprinted is a misdemeanor. On conviction it carries a fine of up to $1,000, up to six months in prison, or both. For nonimmigrants, the Attorney General may waive fingerprinting on the basis of reciprocity.
title: Foreigners staying 30 days or longer must register and be fingerprinted

body: Report cash and monetary instruments over $10,000 on a dedicated form when entering or leaving. If you do not report the money, authorities seize the entire sum rather than just the amount above $10,000. Carry 15,000 and say nothing, and you risk losing all fifteen. This applies even if you earned the money honestly and intend it for a lawful purpose. Beyond losing the money, you face a fine of up to $500,000 and up to ten years in prison.
title: Unreported cash over $10,000 is seized in full, not just the excess

body: Declare every article you bring into the United States to a CBP (US Customs and Border Protection) officer. You can do this in one of three places. The first is the first port of arrival. The second is a conveyance on its way in, where a CBP officer is assigned for that purpose. The third is a US preclearance office abroad. Plants and plant products are covered, and bringing them in against the Plant Protection Act can be penalised. A civil penalty for an individual can reach $50,000. For a first violation by someone moving regulated articles not for monetary gain, it may not exceed $1,000. Anyone who knowingly violates the Act can be fined, imprisoned for up to 1 year, or both. Knowingly bringing in plants or plant products for distribution or sale can mean up to 5 years in prison. After a second conviction it can mean up to 10 years.
title: Declare everything you bring into the US, plants included, to CBP

body: You must present your phone or other device in a condition that allows inspection. An officer may ask for your passcode and keep it for the duration of the search. A basic search can be done with or without suspicion. An advanced search connects equipment to copy or analyse the contents. It needs supervisor approval. It also needs reasonable suspicion of a violation of laws that CBP (US Customs and Border Protection) enforces, or in some cases a national security concern. If a passcode stops the inspection, the officer may detain the device. Detention ordinarily should not exceed five calendar days. A manager can extend it, and extensions beyond fifteen days come in steps of no more than seven days. If your device is detained, you get a completed Form 6051D. A passcode may not be used to reach information stored only remotely, such as in the cloud. Officers may ask you to turn off network connections.
title: US border officers can search your phone without a warrant

body: Driver licensing in the United States is a matter of state law, so the conditions change at a state line rather than the national border. The codes of Virginia and Florida both allow driving on your own country's licence. Virginia allows it from sixteen years and three months, Florida from sixteen for an ordinary car, and neither requires an international permit or a translation. The widely quoted span of 90 days to a year appears in neither text. Florida ties the exemption to lawful presence in the country: if the licence is invalid under that rule, the exemption does not hold. The real trap: a state licence is due within thirty days if you start work or enrol a child in a state school. Virginia's section carries no such condition but has a separate reciprocity mechanism, and what triggers a switch to a local licence is settling, not the calendar.
title: The licence question belongs to the state, and the conditions differ

body: A drone over 250 grams must be recorded, and a visitor can only do it after arriving. What is issued is not an aircraft registration but a certificate of ownership: a foreigner is not entitled to US registration. For recreational flying you take the free online TRUST exam, which takes about half an hour. If the aircraft is registered in another country and broadcasts Remote ID, a separate notice must be filed with the aviation authority before the first flight.
title: A visitor gets a certificate of ownership, not a registration

body: The visa becomes void the moment the authorised period of stay ends, if you stayed beyond it. That is in the statute, not consular practice. The next visa will be issued only at a consulate in the country of your nationality, unless the Secretary of State finds extraordinary circumstances. Unlawful presence of more than 180 days but less than a year bars entry for three years, provided you left voluntarily before removal proceedings began. A year or more bars it for ten, whether you left or were removed, and the bar runs from the date of departure. Time spent under the age of eighteen does not count as unlawful presence at all. And the thing most people get wrong: the statute speaks of the period authorised on admission, not the date on the visa sticker.
title: A day over voids the visa, half a year shuts the door for three

body: The threshold is not 183 days in a year, as people assume, but a sum under a three-year formula. You count all days of the current year, a third of last year's and a sixth of the year before. Reach 183 and you are a tax resident. The second condition is simple: at least 31 days in the current year. The trap is for regular visitors: three two-month trips a year quietly add up to residency. Exceptions exist — certain student and work visa categories, and a declaration of a closer connection to another country.
title: Residency is counted across three years at once, not one

body: Before boarding a flight from a foreign country to the United States, you must sign an attestation. This is a statement that you have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in the previous 21 days. The airline collects it, on paper or digitally. If you do not sign, you will be denied boarding. Knowingly giving false information may lead to criminal fines and imprisonment. Being in the DRC includes connecting through a DRC airport, even if you stayed on the plane. Day 0 is the day you leave the DRC, and you may board from Day 22. It applies to US citizens and Green Card holders, and to people only connecting through the US. Only a US Government exemption lifts it. It covers flights departing at or after 11:59 pm Eastern Standard Time on November 3, 2026. A parent, guardian or travel companion can sign for a child or for someone unable to sign. It does not apply to land border crossings or seaports, and US territories are not foreign countries.
title: Flights to the US from abroad need a signed statement of no DRC stay in 21 days

body: The FDA lets foreign nationals bring or ship a 90-day supply of their own medicine. A foreign national is anyone who is not a US citizen or permanent resident. If you stay longer than 90 days, more can be sent to you. With medicine sent by mail or courier, the FDA suggests including papers showing it is for your own use while visiting. These may be a copy of your visa or passport, a doctor's letter and a prescription in English. Some medicines are also controlled substances, and the DEA generally decides whether they may be brought in for personal use.
title: Foreign nationals may bring a 90-day supply of their own medicine

body: Foreign citizens and stateless people must follow Uzbekistan's rules of stay. Article 225 of the Code of Administrative Responsibility punishes several breaches. These include living on travel documents that have expired. They also include ignoring the set rules on registration at your place of stay, movement or choice of residence. Avoiding departure when your stay period ends is punished too, as is breaking the transit rules. The fine depends on how long the violation lasts. Up to ten days it is five basic calculation units. Over ten and up to thirty days it is fifteen. Over thirty days it is twenty-five. If you do not pay, you are expelled from Uzbekistan and barred from re-entering for one year. If you break the rules again within a year after a penalty, you are expelled and barred for three years. Foreign citizens under eighteen are not held administratively liable for breaking the stay rules.
title: Breaking Uzbekistan's stay rules costs 5 to 25 basic units, maybe expulsion

body: You may take up to 100 million sum in cash out of Uzbekistan, all currencies counted together, without restriction. Above that, residents may take cash out only on a Cabinet of Ministers order, as members of government delegations on official trips. A non-resident may take out more within the cash declared on entry and not spent. A non-resident who won or took part in an international competition held in Uzbekistan may too, with documents proving the money was lawfully received. So may a non-resident, within the proceeds of jewellery declared on entry and sold in the Termez International Trade Centre free trade zone. Over 100 million sum, declare the cash and show it to the customs officer. The declaration states the whole amount, not only the excess.
title: Leaving Uzbekistan with cash: no more than 100 million sum

body: If you owe money under a court decision and miss the deadline without good reason, the state enforcement officer can temporarily bar you from leaving Uzbekistan. He can act at the creditor's request or on his own, and the border troops receive a copy of the decision. If you owe a criminal fine, the officer must impose the ban as soon as the enforcement proceedings open. The ban is lifted when you comply or the proceedings end, and the officer tells the border troops no later than the next day. For child support, paying in advance or signing a pledge also lifts the ban. The pledge must be worth at least two hundred and fifty base calculation amounts. You can appeal the officer's decision.
title: A court-debt travel ban can stop you leaving Uzbekistan

body: Cultural property created fifty or more years ago may not be taken out of Uzbekistan at all: this is a flat ban, not a permit regime. Everything else leaves on a certificate from the Cultural Heritage Agency, obtained in advance and after an art appraisal. The law covers anything merely found on the territory of the country, not only what local craftsmen made. An old suzani, a carpet, a coin or a copper jug from the bazaar is exactly the case the seller will not warn you about. Carrying it past customs control brings a fine of five to ten base units and confiscation of the item itself. On a repeat offence and on a large scale it becomes article 182 of the Criminal Code, up to five years.
title: Cultural property fifty or more years old cannot leave Uzbekistan at all

body: The government portal words the recognition narrowly. Valid on Uzbek territory are international and national driving licences meeting the Convention on Road Traffic signed in Vienna on 8 November 1968. That is convenient for the neighbours: licences from Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Ukraine, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan qualify. A separate international permit is not required. The United States, however, is not a party to the Vienna Convention: it acceded to the 1949 Geneva Convention instead. So an American licence does not fall under the wording quoted, and other foreigners' licences are verified by the traffic police through the foreign ministry. Those recognised are exchanged for Uzbek ones, with a medical examination and theory and practical tests, so check the procedure in advance.
title: Licences are recognised under the Vienna Convention, and American ones are not

body: Cabinet resolution 658 bans import, sale, acquisition, storage and use of unmanned aircraft, their components and spare parts. Only a short list of named state bodies is outside the ban. Transit is the exception written into the ban itself, on condition the aircraft is declared. Toy models are outside all of it, with their own conditions. Up to 50 metres, no closer than 150 metres to an aerodrome's approach strips, at a safe distance from people and in constant visual contact. Aeromodels for training, sport or cultural events fly only in designated zones. Anything else needs a government permission first, then a radio-equipment permit from the communications ministry, then registration with the aviation agency, and only then airspace clearance.
title: Drones may not be brought into Uzbekistan; transit only if declared

body: In Uzbekistan, disrespect towards an object of tangible cultural heritage is an administrative offence. It covers writing or drawing on it, spoiling it, or acts that defame or mock it or its cultural value. Acts at such an object that breach public order count too. The fine is five to ten basic calculation units. If the act causes minor damage, worth up to 30 units, the fine is ten to fifteen units. If the damage is small, worth 30 to 100 units, the fine is fifteen to twenty units. Doing it again within a year of a penalty brings fifteen days' administrative arrest. People who by law cannot be arrested pay 20 to 30 units instead. Foreigners are liable on the same terms as Uzbek citizens. The basis is Article 64-1 of the Code of Administrative Responsibility.
title: Writing on or spoiling a heritage site in Uzbekistan: a fine, then arrest

body: A phone you bring from abroad must be registered by its IMEI within 30 calendar days of first connecting to an Uzbek mobile network. A phone already registered in Uzbekistan does not need registering again. After that, an unregistered phone loses access to mobile services. You get an SMS when it first connects and five days before the deadline. Register through the public services portal with a digital signature or Mobile-ID. Or use the system operator's website with the IMEI, your personal identification number and your phone number. Registration is paid: pay the bill within ten calendar days of applying.
title: A phone brought from abroad must be registered by IMEI within 30 days

body: Foreign citizens must register the phone's IMEI within 60 calendar days of the first network event (inserting a local SIM); residents have 30 days. The basis is Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 778 of 17.09.2019. Registration is done via mygov.uz or uzimei.uz and is chargeable. The fee is pegged to the base calculation value and changes with it, so check the current amount on uzimei.uz. Without registration the device is blacklisted and cut off from local operators' networks. Registration is done by whoever brought the device into the country.
title: IMEI phone registration

body: Your child under 18 gets a biometric passport for travel abroad only with the notarised consent of both parents or the guardians. No notary is needed if both parents come to the data collection point or apply through the public services portal, with a digital signature only. One parent's consent is not needed if that parent has died, is a foreign citizen, or had their residence registration cancelled on moving abroad for good. The same holds if a court deprived that parent of parental rights or declared them missing or incapable, or if the mother raises the child alone. If someone other than a parent or guardian will travel with the child, that person signs a notarised undertaking. From 15 to 18, your child may travel abroad alone only with the parents' consent to independent travel. Without the required documents the passport is refused.
title: A child's passport for travel abroad needs both parents' consent

body: Without any medical paperwork you may bring in up to 10 medicines by name, at most 5 packs of each, plus 5 medical devices. Narcotic medicines are outside that allowance: they pass only up to a 7-day supply. That needs a document from a medical institution in your country of residence or stay, naming the medicine, its form and the amount for the course. Psychotropics need no such document, but their allowance is narrow: 5 names, two packs of each, within the course of treatment. Both must be declared at the crossing point, and whatever exceeds the declared amount is seized and destroyed.
title: Ten medicines, five packs each — and a narcotic one only for seven days

body: Fill in the passenger customs declaration when bringing a phone in — even if the device is within duty-free limits. If it isn't declared, IMEI registration checks the customs database and charges a 30% duty on the device's value; the phone only works after you pay. In force since early 2024.
title: Declare your phone at customs

body: Registration at the place of stay happens one of two ways. Either in person at the migration unit of the interior ministry, or through the E-mehmon system if you are in accommodation or a hospital. That second way is a notification, not an application. The length is the catch. You are registered for the period stated by the owner of the premises, and no longer than the visa-free period or the validity of your visa. Not observing the registration procedure is one of the acts that make up the offence of breaching the rules of stay. Living on an expired travel document and failing to leave on time are others.
title: The hotel registers you, but only for as long as the owner writes down

body: Under the intergovernmental agreement between Russia and Uzbekistan, Russian citizens are exempt from registration of stay for 15 days from the date of entry. The previous period was 3 days. The period runs from the entry date confirmed by a migration card stamped at border control or a stamp in the passport. If you stay longer than 15 days, you must register.
title: Russian citizens: 15 days without registration

body: The main test is the usual one: more than 183 calendar days within any twelve consecutive months beginning or ending in the tax period. The second test catches the rootless. Someone who spent fewer than 183 days here is still resident if they spent longer here than in any other single country. Short absences of under six months for treatment or study do not break the count, so two months in a foreign clinic will not reset it. There is also a way in: with a long-term employment contract you can be recognised as resident on your own application. You do not have to wait out the twelve months. A resident is taxed on total income, not only on what was earned in Uzbekistan.
title: Fewer than 183 days still makes you resident, if it beats everywhere else

body: A foreigner moving around Vietnam must carry a passport, a travel document, or the papers issued to foreigners for entry, exit or residence in Vietnam. An ABTC card also counts. If you carry none of them, you face a warning or a fine of 300,000 to 500,000 dong. Separately, if an authorised Vietnamese official asks to see these documents and you do not show them, the fine is 500,000 to 2,000,000 dong. Refusing an official's request to search your person, vehicle or belongings is fined the same way. The rule applies from 15 December 2025 and replaces the earlier decree 144/2021/NĐ-CP.
title: Carry your passport or entry papers when moving around Vietnam

body: Declare cash at the border if you carry more than 5,000 US dollars or the same in another currency, or more than 15 million dong. The two thresholds count separately and are not added up. You declare on the way in and on the way out alike. There is a second case people miss. If you bring in 5,000 or less but want to pay that cash into a foreign-currency account at a Vietnamese bank, you must declare it anyway. The stamped entry declaration is what lets the bank accept the money.
title: Two separate thresholds: $5,000 and 15 million dong

body: In Vietnam, harming or destroying a relic site's cultural heritage or landscape, or risking its destruction, costs an individual 40 to 50 million dong. The offender must also restore the site to its original state. At a festival, a warning is given for burning incense or votive paper outside designated places. The same goes for swearing or insulting the sacred so as to disturb the festival's solemnity, and for impolite dress or dress unsuited to Vietnamese tradition. These penalties apply to foreigners too; organisations pay double the fine. The basis is Decree 87/2026/NĐ-CP, in force since 15 May 2026.
title: Vietnam: harming a heritage site costs up to 50 million dong

body: A drone flies in Vietnam only with a valid registration certificate. Registering one you brought in takes the import licence and its customs declaration. The pilot must be 18, with no alcohol, drugs or sedatives in blood or breath. From 0.25 kilograms up a visual-line-of-sight licence is required; from 2 kilograms, or out of sight, an instrument one. A foreigner must meet all of that and have a Vietnamese sponsor: an organisation's representative or a Vietnamese individual. So arriving with a drone and flying it the same day does not work.
title: A foreigner flying a drone in Vietnam needs a local sponsor

body: You may bring medicine for your own treatment without an import licence, but only within set limits. Narcotic medicines are limited to 7 days of use. Psychotropic medicines and precursor medicines are limited to 10 days. Days are counted by the dosage on the prescription you carry. Declare these medicines to customs, and do not bring more than the prescription states. Other medicines are limited by value, not days. The customs value may not exceed 200 USD each time, and you may receive medicine no more than 3 times a year. For people with critical illnesses, the limit is VND 10,000,000 each time (about 400 USD), up to 4 times a year. Labels must show the drug name, active ingredients, concentration, content and expiry date, and you need a physician's prescription. If you need more than 7 or 10 days of a controlled medicine, declare it at customs at your port of entry. Bring your itinerary and a doctor's proof of need. Customs then decides whether to let it in.
title: Personal medicine: 7 or 10 days for controlled drugs, value caps for others

body: Filming, photographing or sketching a prohibited place or zone of defence or security is an administrative offence in Vietnam. The fine is 6 to 8 million dong. The camera, phone or drone used for it can be confiscated. Such places are usually marked, but not always, so do not photograph military units or checkpoints.
title: Filming a prohibited military or security zone costs up to 8 million dong

body: You become a tax resident of Vietnam if you meet either of two conditions. The first is being in the country for 183 days or more. The second is having a permanent place of residence here. The days are counted over a calendar year or over 12 consecutive months from your first day in Vietnam. So a stay that straddles the new year can still reach 183 days. The permanent residence condition needs no minimum number of days. The day you arrive and the day you leave each count as a day, based on the immigration stamps in your passport. If you enter and leave on the same day, that counts as one day. A resident is taxed on income earned inside and outside Vietnam. A non-resident is taxed only on income earned in Vietnam. A non-resident's salary is taxed at a flat 20 per cent.
title: 183 days in a calendar year or 12 months makes you a Vietnam tax resident

body: The host tells the police that a foreigner is staying the night, not the visitor. The host is the owner of the accommodation, its legal representative or someone they authorise. Any place where a foreigner stays overnight counts, so a single night at a friend's falls under the rule. Since 24 July 2026 the declaration goes through the electronic system, immediately on arrival: the old grace period is gone. The twelve hours survive only for the paper form, taken to the commune police within that time, or a day in remote areas. Even then it has to be sent at once by any available means. Renting through a digital platform changes nothing: the duty covers that case in so many words.
title: From July 2026 the declaration is immediate, not within twelve hours

body: Using an e-cigarette or a heated tobacco device is an administrative offence in itself, fined 3 to 5 million dong. Decree 90 of 30 March 2026 put the figure in Article 26, and the penalty applies from 15 May 2026. Letting other people vape on premises you own or manage costs more — 5 to 10 million — unless they are close family. The device itself is not simply taken away: the decree orders it destroyed. So leave the vape at home rather than pack it.
title: Vapes and heated tobacco are banned

body: Since 1 January 2025 the law forbids driving with any alcohol at all in the blood or the breath. It is not a threshold but a zero: if the meter shows anything, the offence is complete. On a motorcycle or scooter the fine is 6 to 8 million dong above 0.25 milligrams per litre of breath. Above 0.4 it is 8 to 10 million. In a car the middle band alone costs 18 to 20 million. Refusing the test costs the same 8 to 10 million as the worst reading, so there is nothing to be gained by refusing. The same law bans holding a phone while driving, and driving without a licence at all.
title: Zero alcohol on any vehicle; refusal costs as much as the worst reading
